title: South African Graffiti Artists Reflect on Past Present and Future
content:
Durban, South Africa — “In the early days we were painting on two-by-one Masonite boards,” said Iain Robertson, a Durban-based graffiti artist who goes by the name

Ewok

. “That’s how we would do exhibitions as graffiti artists … we’d built our own walls. And this meant that we had to work within quite tight parameters.”


For many years, this was the environment South African graffiti artists had to work under, much of this owing to the generally negative attitudes surrounding graffiti art since its inception in the 1960s. Fast forward to 2026 and societal perceptions around graffiti art have drastically shifted as high-profile art studios and even billion dollar companies have steadily embraced the art form.


South African Graffiti Artist Unveils Anti-Consumerist Mural in Durban


Long gone are the days when graffiti artists were largely viewed as parasites and blights to society. To the contrary, many of those same once ostracized artists have now become revered as cultural icons. Any one living in a major city merely need step outside their door to see the evidence for themselves.


There is no urban environment in the world where graffiti has not made it’s mark. Even in places like Durban — an area mostly known for being the birthplace of Shaka Zulu — there exists a thriving and unique graffiti art community.


History of Graffiti Art and Spread to Africa


The word ‘graffiti’ originates from the Greek word; “graphein,”which means “to write.” The earliest known examples of said art dates back to the stone age illustrated on cave walls in Sulawesi Island, Indonesia. Other well know examples include Aboriginal cave art in current day Australia, as well as the San rock paintings of southern Africa.


Pettakere Cave “Hand print paintings,” the oldest known cave paintings are more than 44,000 years old. [source:

Wikimedia

]


San Bushman rock painting in the Drakensberg. South Africa  [source:

South African history online

]


Aboriginal Rock Art in the caves at Wary Bay, Bigge Island, Kimberley, Western Australia. [source:

John ,Benwell

]


The history of graffiti art in modern times, however, can be traced back to the rise of the hip-hop movement in the late 1960s, with

American artists TAKI 183 and Cornbread being widely recognized as some of the earliest pioneers

.


While most people treat hip-hop as just another word for rap music, in reality rap is just one of the four essential elements of hip-hop culture, the others being breakdancing DJing, and graffiti. Some graffiti legends have rejected this association, countering with the fact that the practice of drawing on walls long predates the advent of hip-hop and that the two cultures are entirely separate.


What can not be debated is that the alliances formed between various graffiti artists, rappers, DJs and breakdancers from the NYC area in the early 70s became the foundation of hip-hop culture. The subsequent boom in popularity of this culture quickly spread across the United States and to the rest of the world, propelling graffiti to international heights.


Cape Town, South Africa


Cape Town was the

first city from which hip-hop

 — and by extension graffiti — was introduced to South Africa. At that time the country was in the final stages of the racist authoritarian apartheid system which had dominated the government for over 50 years.


As well as being a tool for artistic expression, graffiti also became an outlet for young disenfranchised South Africans — in particular the ethnic minority Coloured population — to express their dissatisfaction with the ruling order.

[note: the term ‘Coloured’ refers to a South African multiracial ethnic group primarily made up of mixed European and Indigenous African origin.]


From Cape Town, graffiti steadily made it’s way into the streets of Durban and Johannesburg in the early 90s. It was at this time that Durban-based artists like Tax, Rulez and Ewok began to pick up spray cans and spread their works all throughout the city.


When asked about the origins of graffiti in Durban, Ewok explained that it was essentially via a traveling circuit of Durbanite artists who were inspired by fellow artists in Cape Town and Johannesburg who in turn borrowed heavily from the graffiti scenes in the U.S. and the U.K.


“We traveled to Cape Town, and Johannesburg connecting with other artists there. We would find out what they were doing and we’d literally bring it back here. There was also, at that time, after …

author: Dionne Phillips, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Indigenous New York Fashion Week brings family and futurity to the runway
content:
Details at Cheyenne LeGrande’s show at Indigenous NYFW on Sept. 11. Photo by Dionne Philips


Backstage at Indigenous New York Fashion Week (INYFW), Dusty LeGrande helped lace up garments from his sibling Cheyenne Rain LeGrande’s collection. A year earlier, Cheyenne had been there to model and help him with his own designs.


“It’s kind of so special because now he’s backstage with me, helping me lace up these garments, and it’s kind of nice that we can help each other out in that way,” she told IndigiNews.


The artist from Bigstone Cree Nation closed the Emerging Voices show on Sept. 11 with a collection that included laced-up mini skirts, tops with jingle dress cones and a wearable art piece made from 3,300 pop can tabs and ribbons.


A model showcasing LeGrande’s designs including the piece made from pop tabs and ribbons. Photo by Dionne Phillips


INYFW’s second year ran from Sept. 10 to 15, bringing together 30 Indigenous designers for six shows in Lenapehoking (Lenape homelands), on the island Mannahatta (Manhattan).


Just off Fashion Avenue, the American Indian Community House was transformed for the event, with seats lining the runway and fabric cascading to the floor.


Korina Emmerich (Puyallup descent) and Liana Shewey (Mvskoke), co-founders of Relative Arts and INYFW, organized the event with volunteers and professionals. 


The six shows featured Contemporary Culture, Emerging Voices, Knowledge Keepers, Thought Leaders, Luxury and Couture. Designers came from around the world, including several with ties to Indigenous communities in “Canada.”


A design for Creator Complex on the runway by Nishina Shapwaykeesic-Loft who is Kanien’kehá:ka from Tyendinaga Mohawk Territory. Photo by Dionne Phillips


Family ties behind the designs


Cheyenne Rain LeGrande ᑭᒥᐊᐧᐣ, brought their background in visual and performance art to the collection, describing fashion as “a way for me to tell stories and express my queer identity.”


Cheyenne Rain LeGrande at the 2026 INYFW. Photo by Dionne Phillips


Their work offered bright interpretations of traditional hide garments, including laced-up dresses and headpieces, with colour and fringe throughout. The collection also featured the latest version of their Moccasin Platform in black, which LeGrande said would be available soon.


“I think that Indigenous futurism is definitely a theme that is talked about in my work,” she said.


“I think it’s really special to see what emerging designers are doing, and what an honour to get to be a part of that group.”


Presenting a collection at INYFW was an evolution LeGrande said “makes sense” given their love of fashion and wearable art. Watching their brother’s designs evolve, they have also been thinking about how their own work might grow. They recalled conversations with Dusty, who has his own label, Mobilize Waskawewin, about what their work could become.


“I’m kind of thinking always about how do I take a concept, almost like a seed, and let it keep growing,” she said.


One of LeGrande’s designs on the runway. Photo by Dionne Phillips


Models walked to a song LeGrande wrote and their mother translated into Cree.


“She is a singer-songwriter who writes in our language and is a really big inspiration to me,” LeGrande said of their mother. 


LeGrande became tearful while describing a hug from their brother at the end of the show.


“I don’t know if I would be where I am in fashion if it wasn’t for him,” she said. 


“I feel so grateful to be a part of this and share my art with everyone in this kind of way.”


Cheyenne LeGrande blowing kisses to the crowd after her show. Photo by Dionne Phillips


LeGrande also had encouragement for younger generations hoping to share their work.


“You can do it,” she said.


“You just gotta create and believe in yourself and trust the ancestors; they’ll guide you.”


As the show came to a close, Emmerich commended the designers.


“Congratulations to the Emerging Voices designers,” she said.


“I’m so impressed by everyone’s work, and for a lot of them, it’s their first runway show.”


The joy of playing dress-up


Dusty presented his Mobilize Waskawewin collection in the Thought Leaders show on Sept. 12.


“My collection tonight was dreaming up what we’re going to be wearing in the next revolution, but that was truly inspired by my children,” he told IndigiNews.


He opened with a spoken-word performance.


Dusty performed spoken word to begin his runway show. Photo by Dionne Phillips …

author: Unknown
title: "Never Again": Czechoslovakian Hardcore in the Syrian Civil War
content:
In the following narrative, anarchists who participated as internationalist volunteers in the fight to defend Rojava against the Islamic State describe the role that the anti-militarist song “Už Nikdy” (“Never Again”) by the Czechoslovakian hardcore band Kritická Situace played in their experience.


This text is adapted from the newest issue of the anarchist hardcore publication

Inside Front

.

 We share it here to explore the importance of revolutionary music and culture in social movements.

The personal is geopolitical.


These events took place in March 2019, near the end of the fight against the Islamic State. At that time, the Turkish army and its Syrian proxies had brutally seized the majority-Kurdish district of Afrin in northwest Syria, and Donald Trump was

signaling

 that he would permit them to attack the rest of Rojava as well. At the same time, the Islamic State still controlled territory in Deir Ezzor in the southeast, where the final battles took place at al-Baghuz Fawqani.


As soon as the Islamic State was defeated, the United States government gave Turkey the green light to

butcher

 those who had defeated it. In 2024,

Turkish-backed forces

 came to power in Syria, creating

new challenges

 for the multiethnic revolutionary experiment in Rojava. Nonetheless, the fight for free life continues—in Rojava and the

rest

 of Syria, in

Turkey

, in Czech Republic and Slovakia, and even in the United States.

The struggle continues.


“Už Nikdy” by Kritická Situace.


We received the following accounts of the same events from two different correspondents.


Account I. — “Never Again”


In March 2019, I was in Syria, an internationalist volunteer in the midst of the civil war.


We were fighting on two fronts. To the northwest, our comrades were locked in a defensive war with Turkish proxies and the Turkish state itself, whereas we were engaged in an offensive war with Daesh in the southeast. To the northwest, death from above: snipers and drones. In the southeast, death from below: snipers and mines.


My friends and I were positioned on the second floor of an abandoned building in the ruins of the town of Al-Baghuz Fawqani. A Tweety Bird blanket was hung over one of the blacked-out windows in our room. There was a small kitten who would sleep with us. The comrades in the hospital to the north had sent us there with an ambulance. We took it forward to retrieve casualties from the front line, administering what care we could. Usually, I drove.


This cat briefly held the most advantageous position in the Syrian civil war.


In our group, there were volunteers from around the world who had come to Syria to defend the revolution. We found ourselves there in the last days of the last battle of the territorial war against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria. In our ambulance unit, none of us shared common citizenship or a native tongue, but we soon found that we did share a background in the global punk counterculture.


One of the comrades described to me the sadness he had felt on the day that he had been forced to shave off his mohawk and flee his country. “But punk is not here,” he said, pointing at his hair. “It is here,” he said, pressing his fist to his heart.


“A Tweety Bird blanket was hung over one of the blacked-out windows in our room.”


By leaving my phone on the roof for several hours, I had managed to download a song titled “Never Again,” recorded in 1992 by the Czechoslovakian band

Kritická Situace

. The song had come to my attention in the year 1998, when it was featured in a memorable and impassioned review in

issue 11

 of the North American hardcore publication

Inside Front.

 It tells the story of a conscript fleeing from the army
through the wilderness, vowing that his superiors will never be able to force him to kill.


My friends and I were now in the exact inverse of that situation: we were internationalists who had crossed the world voluntarily to defend the principles of autonomy, ecology, and women’s liberation that the social movements in northeastern Syria were putting into practice. Still, war
is war. Many nights, after

tekmil

, we would sing “Never Again” together quietly in the darkness, to the sound of gunfire, mortar fire, and bombs. Those fluent in Slavic languages would sing the words, and the rest of us would carry the rhythms and harmonies as best we could.


In a dark dungeon, in the glow of torches,


You hide from the exercise of power.


You do not …

author: Bianca Blell
title: Virginia Voters Will Decide the Future of Reproductive Freedom, Marriage Equality, and Voting Rights This November
content:
On November 3rd, Virginia voters will decide on three proposed amendments to the state constitution concerning reproductive freedom, marriage, and voting rights. The amendments would add a constitutional right to reproductive freedom, remove Virginia’s constitutional prohibition on same-sex marriage and require equal treatment of marriages, and automatically restore voting rights to people convicted of felonies upon release of incarceration.

Together, the measures represent one of the most consequential ballot slates for civil rights in the state’s recent history, including a rare opportunity for voters to enshrine protections directly into the state constitution, beyond the reach of a hostile legislature or a change in administration. All three amendments were approved by the General Assembly through Virginia’s constitutional amendment process and will appear on the November 2026 ballot.

The first amendment establishes a constitutional right to reproductive freedom and access. The amendment defines the right as including decisions about prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, contraception, abortion care, miscarriage management, and fertility care. It would also prohibit the Commonwealth from penalizing or prosecuting individuals for exercising those rights, as well as doctors, nurses, and others who assist patients with their voluntary consent.

The question voters will see on the ballot:

“Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) protect the freedom to make personal decisions about prenatal care, childbirth, postpartum care, birth control, abortion, miscarriage management, and fertility care; (ii) protect doctors, nurses, and patients from being punished for these decisions; and (iii) allow for restrictions on access to abortion during the third trimester of pregnancy except when the patient’s health is at risk or the pregnancy cannot survive?”

If passed, this would make Virginia’s protections some of the most durable in the South, solidifying it as the last Southern state without an abortion ban. This status would keep reproductive rights safe from the current legislature but also from whoever holds the governor’s office next. In a state where 8,570 people traveled from states like Georgia, Florida, and North Carolina in 2025 to receive healthcare, establishing reproductive access has never been more important. Virginia voters can impact generations to come in a Post-Dobbs environment.

The second amendment would remove the Virginia Constitution’s existing language stating that only a union between one man and one woman may be recognized as a valid marriage. It would replace that language with a provision stating that marriage is one of the vital personal rights essential to the orderly pursuit of happiness.

The official ballot question asks:

“Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended to (i) remove the ban on same-sex marriage; (ii) affirm that two adults may marry regardless of sex, gender, or race; and (iii) require all legally valid marriages to be treated equally under the law?”

Same-sex marriage has been legally recognized in Virginia since 2014 following a federal court ruling, and the U.S. Supreme Court recognized a constitutional right to same-sex marriage nationwide in Obergefell v. Hodges that same year. Virginia’s Constitution, however, still contains language prohibiting same-sex marriage. The proposed amendment would remove that language and establish equal treatment of legally valid marriages in the state constitution.

If approved, the amendment would take effect January 1, 2027.

The third amendment would automatically restore voting rights to formerly incarcerated Virginians once they are released from prison and complete any additional required steps, such as parole or probation. Currently, Virginia is one of the few states where a person with a felony conviction must individually petition the governor to have their voting rights restored, producing a discretionary, case-by-case process which rights restoration advocates have long called arbitrary and disenfranchising.

The ballot question asks voters:

“Should the Constitution of Virginia be amended (i) to provide for the fundamental right to vote in the Commonwealth, (ii) to revise the qualifications of voters so that a person convicted of a felony is not entitled to vote during his period of incarceration but is automatically invested with the right to vote upon release from incarceration, and (iii) to update the …

author: Kevin Carson
title: Ruthanna Emyrs, A Half-Built Garden, Tor 2022
content:
Recensione a cura di

Kevin Carson

. Originale:

A Half-Built Garden, by Ruthanna Emrys (Tor 2022)

, del 29 luglio 2026. Traduzione italiana di

Enrico Sanna

.


A Half-Built Garden

 è una storia di contatto alieno ben congegnata, dalla trama avvincente, cose che da sole fanno una piacevole lettura. Come forse saprà chi ha già letto altre mie recensioni, quando recensisco storie di fantascienza ambientate in un futuro prossimo utopico, libero e postcapitalista, il mio interesse riguarda anche come questo mondo è strutturato. Un peccatuccio che condivido con Auden che scrive ispirandosi alla bibbia.


Siamo negli anni 2080, dopo l’Età delle Turbolenze di metà secolo, e il mondo emerge dalle rovine del capitalismo per creare una nuova, tollerabile società.


La principale istituzione di governo è la watershed network, una federazione di istituzioni locali autogestite grossomodo corrispondenti alle bioregioni, comprendente gran parte della popolazione e delle risorse mondiali. L’equilibrio di potere è il risultato di una rivoluzione perlopiù nonviolenta iniziata una o due generazioni prima e finita verso il 2050: una serie di boicottaggi, sabotaggi e altre azioni dirette spingono le aziende economiche a rinchiudersi in enclave in alto mare. La vicenda è narrata attraverso gli occhi di un abitante della Chesapeake Watershed, che ricorda quando i suoi genitori “mettevano i primi sensori vietati nel fiume Potomac e barricavano le fabbriche per imporre la volontà collettiva della nascente rivoluzione dandelion.”


Le aziende sono perlopiù “padroni miliardari e dipendenti servi ammassati dietro il filo spinato nelle loro isole artificiali.” Tranne “qualche convertito e visitatore”, gli abitanti sono “i discendenti delle persone arrivate con il loro fondatore: dipendenti e sodali che preferivano scappare dall’apocalisse piuttosto che unirsi in comunità e evitarla.”


Le enclave aziendali sono circondate da “filo spinato” evidentemente imposto dalle watershed durante la rivoluzione. “Finalmente abbiamo vietato le aziende. Mio padre e altri, che hanno dato vita alla prima rete del cambiamento, hanno operato per fermarle.” La rivoluzione “limita la produzione di CO

2

 per contenere il riscaldamento climatico bloccando i trasporti quando si supera il limite.” Le aziende, “refrattarie al cambiamento, … finiscono per barricarsi dietro il filo spinato in alcune isole artificiali…”


Esiliate nelle isole, gran parte delle aziende, che “già da tempo hanno perso ogni parvenza di legalità”, rifiuta qualunque riconoscimento ufficiale dalle watershed. Inviano osservatori ai dialoghi sulla CO

2

, obbediscono tacitamente alle limitazioni dell’anidride e di altri inquinanti che le watershed, attori principali, impongono loro, e imbrogliano pensando di poter sfuggire ai controlli. Data la loro relativa debolezza, sono costrette a chiedere il permesso delle watershed consorziate quando l’impatto delle loro attività supera i confini.


Gran parte delle funzioni economiche delle società, tolte alcune zone che hanno ancora il monopolio del know-how, sono state rilevate dalle watershed. Comprese certe istituzioni industriali risalenti al periodo precedente, come il “MIT e l’Associazione di costruttori panasiatica” che sono “collegati alle reti dandelion”.


Le relazioni tra watershed e aziende sono generalmente da guerra fredda.


“Compriamo ancora da loro, saltuariamente… Cose che ci servono e che ancora non siamo riusciti a riprodurre con l’ingegneria a ritroso, oppure pratichiamo qualche scambio nella speranza di indurli a unirsi a noi. Quando succede, lasciamo che visitino le watershed, purché promettano di comportarsi bene.”


Nel loro rapporto con le aziende, il compito principale delle watershed è la gestione del declino: cercano di rilevarne le funzioni indispensabili rimanenti e mantenere i contatti così da indurle a cambiare la propria cultura, prevenendo ogni azione disperata di retroguardia che farebbe molte vittime.


Non scompariranno presto; dobbiamo continuare a parlare con loro o non cambieranno mai abbastanza da unirsi a noi…


“Abbiamo ancora bisogno di loro. Quando avevano il potere per poco non distruggevano il pianeta; ma fabbricano ancora delle parti importanti per la nostra infrastruttura. Loro pensano di aver bisogno di noi perché senza quelle esportazioni perderebbero la ragione d’esistere. In realtà, questo legame esile è la loro ultima possibilità. Ogni contatto serve a ricordare loro che c’è un’altra strada …

author: Unknown
title: Apply Heat, Melt ICE: Flashpoints in the Fight : A Guide to Resisting ICE around the Country this October
content:
All around the United States, people are organizing to resist the federal mercenaries who carry out Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Here, we announce three upcoming mobilizations and share reports from two recent confrontations.


In

Arizona

, people have been blocking the construction of the border wall since July 27; they are calling for people from around the country to come join them. In the

Twin Cities

, people are calling for a countrywide day of action on October 3 to express solidarity with the Minnesota 15, who have been federally charged for allegedly conspiring to resist Operation Metro Surge. In

Vermont

, people have organized a week of action for October 4-9 and are inviting people to come participate or carry out solidarity actions elsewhere. Clashes with federal mercenaries have recently broken out in

Austin, Texas

 and

Frederick, Maryland

.


Awareness of the harm that ICE is inflicting on communities peaked in January, during the

massive popular resistance

 against the federal occupation of the Twin Cities. Yet deportations have only

increased

 since then, with most of the abductions taking place behind closed doors as ICE agents work with police and jails to capture immigrants. The recent wave of resistance to ICE offers a crucial chance to take the offensive ahead of what is bound to be a tumultuous fall.


As many liberals shift to focusing on the midterm elections this November, naïvely hoping that elections alone will provide change, it is especially important to continue to focus on what we can accomplish directly by means of collective power. However the elections turn out, only effective grassroots action can create a situation in which neither party will be able to continue the violence of ICE.


Remember, the abduction and deportation of immigrants

did not begin under Donald Trump

; as recently as last year,

mainstream Democrats

 were proposing to

adopt

 Trump’s xenophobic policies wholesale. Even if the far right loses control of the government, whoever inherits state power will maintain every repressive policy that we do not force them to discontinue. The victory that the movement against ICE achieved in the Twin Cities, forcing Trump to end Operation Metro Surge and fire ICE and Department of Homeland Security officials, shows what we can accomplish when we don’t wait on politicians.


It is time to shift from

reactive

 to

proactive

—from organizing rapid response networks to seizing the initiative. Pick the struggle that is nearest to you geographically or politically and participate in it, whether by traveling to join it or by organizing a local action in solidarity.


Wherever you are, you are probably close to ICE infrastructure, ICE profiteers, or a current hotspot in this struggle. Make plans to travel to a flashpoint near you or organize something at a relevant local target. You can help to boost all of the other events by mentioning all of them in your messaging.


Apply heat, melt ICE!


Minnesota


Out of the tens of thousands who participated in

resisting

 Operation Metro Surge in Minnesota between December and February 2026,

fifteen people

 have been federally charged for allegedly conspiring to resist the violence that ICE agents inflicted on their communities.


The Minnesota 15 Anti-Repression Committee is calling for

a nationwide day of solidarity actions on Saturday, October 3

 to express support for the defendants and all those targeted by ICE. Plan an action at your local ICE office or federal building!


In Minneapolis, on October 3, a labor-led march will traverse downtown to show solidarity with the defendants and to call out the federal government and their corporate enablers. Meet at Peavey Plaza, 1101 Nicollet Mall.


Vermont


From October 4-9, in Chittenden County, Vermont, people will host a week of mass action to end ICE surveillance, targeting, and separation. Everyone is invited!


Vermont is a national nerve center for ICE surveillance. Through the Law Enforcement Support Center and the National Criminal Analysis Targeting Center, both of which are located in Williston, Vermont, ICE collects tips on our immigrant neighbors, spies on civilian social media accounts, and builds lists of targets for kidnapping and deportation. Alongside a dozen other offices scattered around Chittenden County, these sites provide the bureaucratic backbone and surveillance infrastructure for ICE activity countrywide.


How to get involved …

author: Emma Jacobs
title: What the climate movement can learn from organized labor
content:
This article

What the climate movement can learn from organized labor

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Climate activists engaged in nonviolent direct action are used to the rinse and repeat of arrest: handcuffs, short trip to jail, a misdemeanor charge and then release to friends for a post-action pizza dinner. Show up at court a few weeks later for a brief arraignment and wait for the case to be dismissed. Low drama.


That’s changed under Trump. From the

Declare Emergency activists charged with felonies

 (for applying washable paint to the protective case around a Degas sculpture) to the

Extinction Rebellion activists under investigation by an FBI terrorism task force

 (for undisclosed reasons), activists can no longer depend on walking away unscathed from direct actions.

Multiple states have passed anti-protest laws

 since Trump was elected, increasing penalties imposed on activists. Grassroots action has a higher cost now. 


Simultaneously, with the gutting of the Inflation Reduction Act and its attendant tax credits for clean energy investment, the federal path to climate action is blocked. And local wins, while important, cannot surmount the incredible rollbacks happening at the federal level, as Sunrise Movement Executive Director Aru Shiney-Ajay

recently pointed out

. 


Indeed, the U.S. climate movement is in

deep trouble

. If all that weren’t enough, the climate crisis is no longer top of mind for many on the left, especially with the rising authoritarian threat and the focus on affordability. With civil disobedience demanding greater risk, traditional policy advocacy for climate action at the federal level closed off and public attention turned elsewhere, what tactics do we in the climate movement have left?


What’s left is deep engagement with the labor movement — its members and its tactics. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


Organized labor has a broad base, a track record of major wins and the power to shut down the economy. And make no mistake: Economic leverage is a necessary ingredient in the struggle to bring down companies as profitable as those in the fossil fuel industry. 


Climate activists have relied heavily on tactics of protest and persuasion (see Gene Sharp’s

categories

), underinvesting in tactics of economic noncooperation. While the environmental movement has a history of consumer boycotts, there have been fewer instances of work stoppages or rent strikes. The climate groups that do engage in symbolic work and school stoppages (most famously, Fridays for the Future), have mostly been confined to students and are largely to make a political statement rather than a strategic attempt to gain concrete concessions from a specific target. 


Strategically aligning workers with a rapid energy transition not only broadens the coalition needed to win durable policy victories, but builds power with a movement versed in strikes, walkouts, slowdowns and other forms of economic disruption. (Not to mention a bevy of tools like

community benefit agreements

 and

co-enforcement

 to promote follow-through on corporate environmental promises.)


Labor-climate alliances go back decades (see Blue Green Alliance, Climate Jobs National Resource Center and Labor Network for Sustainability), and unions have long advocated for a

just transition

 that supports workers employed in polluting industries. But in the current political environment, we need these relationships to be stronger than ever.  


One major opportunity for the climate movement is the May Day Strong coalition, which brings labor and community groups together to organize mass strikes and make big demands for systemic change. The coalition’s demands don’t yet include climate, but the climate movement can still organize with them to learn nonparticipation tactics and build solidarity toward a broad base that sees climate, anti-authoritarianism and affordability as one united fight. 


Lessons from labor

 


Think about the situation at your job. Workplaces are pretty authoritarian: the leader doesn’t care much for the input of the people on the shop floor, and what the leader says goes. If someone gets hurt, let the government step in to help them. As unions teach us, for a group of workers to extract real concessions from a profit-maximizing boss requires building enough power among workers to shut the workplace down (or at least threaten to do so) …

author: Valerie Anne
title: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Straightwashed Its Lesbian but Maisie Williams Played Her Gay Anyway
content:
Leading up to the release of Practical Magic 2, we were all hoping this witchy sequel would be even gayer than the gay undertones of the first because, in the source material, Sally Owens’ daughter Antonia is a lesbian. And while there were potentially versions of the movie that expressed that, the final edit left Antonia’s sexuality undetermined. However, Maisie Williams has been sure to tell everyone on the press tour that she knew the source material and regardless of what the final edit revealed, she played Antonia as a “sapphic icon” and that it brought some nuance to certain scenes since it meant Antonia had a different perspective on men than the other women in her family.

This is a shame and not the first time queerness in a book has been watered down or erased altogether in their adaptations. To name a few: Fried Green Tomatoes, The Color Purple, and don’t even get me started on comic book characters that are queer on the page but straight on screen. Studios are cowards and it’s the same reason queer storylines are often cut from animated films, or even single lines in big box office hits that would mean a lot to the queer community but scare the money men. This feels especially egregious in a movie franchise like this, because witches have such a rich queer history and having a film (as so few are) jam-packed with women and to have all of them be straight feels like a waste.

It’s disappointing to say the least, especially in the year 2026, but at least we have people like Maisie making sure we know that SHE knows that the character should have been queer, and that it was unfortunately out of her hands in the end.

Sandra Bullock has said there could be a third Practical Magic in the future, centering on Antonia and Joey King’s Kylie, so fingers crossed the queer lines and scenes don’t end up on the cutting room floor of that one.

author: Indymedia Pueblos Originarios
title: Punta Querandí reclama a Nordelta la reparación por la destrucción de enterratorios indígenas
content:
La Comunidad Indígena Punta Querandí rechazó la profundización del modelo urbanístico de Nordelta y exigió medidas de reparación histórica por los daños ya ocasionados sobre el patrimonio indígena y los humedales, a partir de las conclusiones del propio Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Acumulativo (EIAA). Entre las principales demandas se encuentran el reentierro de 42 ancestros en el territorio de donde fueron extraídos, la creación de un Espacio de Memoria Ancestral y fondos financiados por Nordelta destinados a las comunidades y población indígena del distrito.


Movilización en diciembre de 2021. (Foto: Omar Bogado)


La destrucción de cementerios y sitios ancestrales indígenas por el avance de los barrios privados sobre los humedales de Tigre y Escobar está en el origen mismo de la lucha de Punta Querandí. Durante dos décadas, la Comunidad denunció la destrucción y afectación de lugares sagrados, reclamó la restitución de los cuerpos humanos excavados y logró concretar los primeros reentierros en el Área Metropolitana de Buenos Aires.


Ahora, el Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Acumulativo (EIAA) presentado por Nordelta S.A. ante el Municipio de Tigre evalúa los impactos producidos durante casi tres décadas de desarrollo urbano y forma parte del proceso del que depende la posibilidad de avanzar con nuevas obras en sectores todavía no consolidados del emprendimiento. El estudio reconoce que, antes del comienzo de las obras en 1998, los sitios Arroyo Sarandí 1 y 2 conservaban su integridad como yacimientos indígenas y enterratorios ancestrales, datados entre los años 800 y 1400 d.C., y que posteriormente fueron “destruidos o sepultados como consecuencia de las obras de construcción de Nordelta”.


Frente a ese reconocimiento, la Comunidad Indígena Punta Querandí presentó ante el Municipio de Tigre una serie de demandas de reparación histórica, territorial, cultural y ambiental.


Señalización realizada en noviembre de 2016. (Foto: Archivo Punta Querandí)


Durante julio y agosto, el Municipio de Tigre abrió un proceso de Participación Ciudadana sobre el EIAA, que incluyó una Consulta Pública para que vecinos, organizaciones e instituciones pudieran presentar observaciones y preguntas sobre el estudio. El proceso incluyó además una Audiencia Pública realizada el 21 de agosto en el Teatro Municipal Pepe Soriano de Benavídez.


El reclamo de reparación se plantea por los daños ya ocasionados, independientemente de la decisión que finalmente adopten las autoridades respecto del EIAA y del futuro desarrollo urbanístico de Nordelta. La presentación contó con el patrocinio de la abogada Paula Mercedes Alvarado Mamani, perteneciente al Pueblo Kolla y especialista en Derecho Internacional de los Derechos Humanos, con trayectoria en causas vinculadas a los derechos de los pueblos indígenas.


El EIAA califica además la pérdida o afectación del patrimonio arqueológico y paleontológico como un impacto “negativo muy alto”. También advierte que otros contextos arqueológicos pueden haber desaparecido debido a la transformación de la Planicie Litoral por urbanizaciones cerradas sin estudios arqueológicos preventivos.


LOS 42 ANCESTROS DEBEN VOLVER A ARROYO SARANDÍ


Fragmento del Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Acumulativo de Nordelta.


Uno de los principales reclamos es garantizar un espacio protegido dentro del área donde se encontraba Arroyo Sarandí, actualmente dentro de Nordelta, para concretar el reentierro de los 42 ancestros que fueron excavados de ese sitio y permanecen en el Museo de La Plata.


La restitución de estos restos humanos a Punta Querandí fue aprobada por el Instituto Nacional de Asuntos Indígenas (INAI) en enero de 2022, como continuidad del proceso que permitió recuperar y reenterrar ocho ancestros en Punta Querandí y en La Bellaca.


El reclamo cuenta además con un importante antecedente institucional: en 2020, el Concejo Deliberante de Tigre declaró de interés legislativo los procesos de restitución y reentierros impulsados por Punta Querandí, incluyendo el de Arroyo Sarandí.


El lugar del reentierro deberá contar con protección jurídica permanente y Punta Querandí solicita además su reconocimiento como Sitio Sagrado.


Junto al lugar de reentierro, Punta Querandí propone crear un Espacio de Memoria Ancestral, financiado por Nordelta y administrado por la Comunidad, destinado a preservar y transmitir la memoria de los pueblos originarios del territorio, la historia de Arroyo Sarandí y las prácticas culturales …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Indonesia: Campaña de financiación para talleres de formación ante la criminalización, la violencia y las acciones represivas
content:
Durante más de una década, las comunidades de base de Bandung se han estado organizando contra la gentrificación, el desplazamiento y la pérdida de los espacios por los que han luchado para mantenerlos vivos. Miles de personas han formado parte de esta larga lucha, enfrentándose a la presión y la represión mientras seguían organizándose desde la base.

Esta campaña surge directamente de esa historia. La idea de celebrar el taller allí partió de uno de los líderes comunitarios que se encuentra en el centro de esta lucha, alguien que ha estado organizándose con la comunidad a lo largo de estos años de presión y desalojo.

El taller también reúne a antiguos presos de Chaos Star y a anarquistas sociales de base: dos grupos que, hace años, apenas podían encontrarse cara a cara. Desde el año pasado, han comenzado a trabajar juntos, reconociendo que, tras años de represión y lucha, se necesitan mutuamente.

Por favor, ayuda a difundir la campaña

author: Andrés
title: Un héroe colectivo
content:
12 de marzo de 2025 Foto: Juan Foglia


El 12 de marzo de 2025 Nicolás Chiarini, ex bombero voluntario, sostuvo de manera ininterrumpida el cráneo perforado de Pablo Grillo para que no se desangre. Del otro lado, Héctor Jesús Guerrero, Cabo 1° de la Gendarmería Nacional, había disparado su escopeta lanzagases en ángulo horizontal -violando protocolos y manuales de uso- con el beneplácito de toda la cadena de mando, incluida Patricia Bullrich, por entonces Ministra de Seguridad. Esta es la crónica de cómo se perpetúa la violencia institucional para llegar a una situación semejante. Pero sobre todo es la crónica, en la voz de Chiarini, de lo que pasó la tarde en que sostuvo la línea de vida del fotorreportero en la palma de su mano.

Por Andrés Manrique (ANRed). 


“…el pueblo aprendió que estaba solo 


y que debía pelear

por sí mismo


y

 que de su propia entraña

sacaría los medios,


el silencio, la astucia

 y la fuerza…”

Rodolfo Walsh.


Como pueblo le salvamos la vida a un pibe que lo quiso matar la policía


“Podría haber sido yo”, dice Nicolás, con formación como bombero voluntario y rescatista: “parece tonto, pero me emociona que alguien te diga gracias. Había salvado otras vidas, y más allá de que no lo hice como bombero esa vez, me tocó asistir a un compañero, y hoy la vida de Pablo sigue adelante.


“Lo primero que se aprende en los bomberos es que hay que asegurar la escena: y la escena la aseguró la plaza llena, la aseguraron los pibes que se pusieron alrededor y nos cubrieron de los gases, de los tiros, de la avanzada policial y de gendarmería, armados con dos hidrantes, escopetas lanzagases, postas de goma, palos, gas pimienta. Por eso subrayo que es lo que hicimos. Toda esa memoria colectiva en la que nadie le preguntó a nadie qué hacer: eso hay que rescatar. Porque si la plaza no estaba llena nada de esto hubiera sucedido, nada de esto hubiera sido posible. Sé que lo que hice le salvó la vida, decir otra cosa sería mentir, pero pude hacerlo porque otros estaban ahí, también haciendo su parte. Sin el que estaba adelante para que la policía no avanzara, no hubiera podido. Mientras esto pasaba, en el mismo momento, del otro lado (se refiere al lado de la avenida Rivadavia) a Jonathan Navarro le volaban el ojo de un escopetazo. Entonces, quiero insistir en que fuimos todos los que estuvimos bancando. Por eso hay que contar lo que hacen las doñas en los comedores, lo que hacen los alfabetizadores, lo que hacen los fotoperiodistas. Porque no nos mataron a un pibe, y tenemos una efeméride en vida; como pueblo le salvamos la vida a un pibe que lo quiso matar la policía. Y eso no pasa todos los días.”


Nicolás cuenta su historia sin jactancia, en la paz de su casa. Sabe que va a tener que hacerlo de nuevo en el juzgado, y la recuerda en detalle. Es riguroso, hoy el tiempo está de su lado. Actualmente trabaja de cartero: “pero yo siempre quise volver a ser bombero. Días antes de lo de Pablo venía pensando en viajar a Córdoba, a ver si podía dar una mano contra los incendios, pero después empecé a sentir que tenía que darle pelota a todo esto, porque lo que hice fue determinante.”


Esa tarde en el Congreso la oposición lograba reunir fuerzas para investigar al Ejecutivo por el caso de la criptomoneda Libra, el fraude de más de 100 millones de dólares que tiene al presidente, junto a Santiago Caputo y Karina Milei, como principales implicados.


Fotos del 26 de marzo y 30 de abril de 2025 (Foto: Andrés Manrique)


Ningún procesado en la línea de mando


El tiro que lo dejó al borde de la muerte al fotorreportero, fue uno de los tantos que hizo esa tarde el Cabo 1° de Gendarmería, Héctor Jesús Guerrero, sin respetar el reglamento de uso, y con beneplácito de toda la cadena de mando. En videos grabados por las mismas fuerzas, lo vemos disparando el tiro que le rompe el cráneo a Pablo en ángulo horizontal, con indicación directa de su superior, Jorge Luis Reyes. Reyes (uno de los jefes del grupo SEI -Sección de Empleo Inmediato- de Gendarmería) camina al lado de Guerrero por delante de los escudos, se le acerca al Cabo, extiende el brazo y señala en dirección de los manifestantes. Guerrero apoya la rodilla sobre el asfalto y dispara a la línea de horizonte; vuelve a pararse y antes de regresar tras los escudos, Reyes le da un golpe con la mano abierta sobre el hombro, en manifiesta señal de aprobación. El cartucho de gas recorre entre 47 y 50 metros hasta la frente de Pablo.

author: Ludmila Pizarro
title: Nossa Senhora Aparecida vira evento eleitoral e aprofunda crise entre ministros do STF
content:
Nossa Senhora Aparecida se transformou em um dos maiores eventos políticos de 2026, com 1,3 milhão de publicações e 12,4 milhões de interações entre 23 e 27 de setembro, ou seja, na penúltima semana antes do primeiro turno das eleições. A informação é do monitoramento realizado nas redes sociais neste período pelo Instituto Democracia em Xeque (IDX).


Não foi sem razão, portanto, que a campanha do senador e candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) acionou, já na sexta-feira, 25 de setembro, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) tendo como o alvo a publicação do humorista Antonio Tabet.


A alegação dos advogados de Flávio era que se tratava de desinformação, uma mentira, afirmar que ele apoiava a retirada do título de “padroeira do Brasil” da santa. De fato, o post de Tabet ocorreu em meio a uma onda de desinformação sobre a relação do senador com um Projeto de Lei apresentado pelo então deputado Professor Victório Galli (PP-MT), pastor evangélico e arquivado em 2008. A proposta alterava a lei do feriado de 12 de outubro, trocando “padroeira do Brasil” por “padroeira dos brasileiros católicos apostólicos romanos”,

conforme a Agência Pública mostrou

.


Flávio Bolsonaro batizado no rio Jordão, em Israel, numa repetição de ato feito pelo pai em 2016


O que o relatório do IDX mostra, entretanto, é que o debate sobre o assunto nas redes sociais ultrapassou rapidamente a “fake news” e se desenvolveu no embate político sobre liberdade religiosa, intolerância, defesa da padroeira e impacto eleitoral.


“A maior parte da conversação está em torno do debate cultural, religioso, judicialização, liberdade de expressão e defesa da padroeira, com 83% do universo analisado. Somente 17% do universo mencionam a acusação que originou a controvérsia”, afirma o relatório do Instituto.


A própria publicação de Antonio Tabet não faz relação direta ao projeto de lei. Trata-se de uma imagem da santa com a frase: “A família miliciana odeia tanto mulher preta, que resolveu atacar Nossa Senhora Aparecida!”.


Dino versus Mendonça


O tangenciamento entre o que é desinformação e o que acabou se tornando debate político, gerou uma nova batalha de decisões entre ministros de dois tribunais superiores, que deve ser levada ao plenário do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).


No domingo, 27 de setembro, o ministro do STF Flávio Dino suspendeu as decisões do colega André Mendonça da última sexta-feira, 25, que determinava às redes sociais como X (antigo Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, TikTok e YouTube a retirada de postagem de Tabet e de outras contas nas redes sociais. Uma das decisões de Mendonça relaciona mais de mil links de publicações sobre o mesmo tema que deveriam ser retiradas pelas empresas responsáveis pelas mídias sociais.


Mendonça também afirmou na decisão, como atual vice-presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), que as redes sociais “atuem preventivamente contra a disseminação dos conteúdos abrangidos por esta decisão”. A decisão do ministro, derrubada por Dino, ainda fixa uma multa diária de R$ 50 mil ao provedor que não cumprir a medida.


Entre as justificativas do ministro Flávio Dino para anular as decisões de Mendonça está o risco de “censura em massa”, diante da “‘derrubada’ de milhares de postagens, inclusive de adeptos do culto à Nossa Senhora Aparecida”. Além disso, Dino afirma que o TSE “delegou largos poderes censórios às empresas de internet”, e que é necessário um “debate sobre o controle de constitucionalidade de decisões monocráticas de um ilustre ministro que faz parte de um Tribunal Superior”.


O ministro ainda salienta no documento a importância de valores como a liberdade religiosa, “já que o tema de fundo em discussão pública refere-se à determinação legal de ser Nossa Senhora Aparecida a ‘Padroeira do Brasil’”. Na mesma decisão, Dino solicita a análise da questão pelo plenário do Supremo.


Com a suspensão da derrubada de seu posicionamento, Tabet, também no domingo, publicou novamente a foto da santa com a mesma frase. O humorista ainda escreveu na rede social X: “Flavio Dino acabou de derrubar a decisão de André Mendonça, ‘preservando a liberdade de expressão e a liberdade religiosa’ dos que defendem Nossa Senhora Aparecida. Como será impossível restabelecer a postagem que foi apagada, vou publicá-la novamente. E conto com vocês para fazê-la chegar mais uma vez a todos que a viram e aos que não puderam vê-la”.


Nesta segunda-feira, 28 de setembro, a defesa de Flávio Bolsonaro solicitou ao …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Eduardo Cerdá: "No hay que reemplazar al glifosato, hay que cambiar el modelo de producción"
content:
Por Nahuel Lag


La Red Nacional de Municipios y Comunidades que Fomentan la Agroecología (Renama) marcha al decimosegundo

Mes de la Agroecología

. Será en noviembre, cuando las tranqueras se abrirán para demostrar un modelo de producción que está presente en todo el país. Eduardo Cerdá es el impulsor de ese espacio a partir de su trabajo como ingeniero agrónomo y asesor de campos que son “faro”, como le gusta decirles, y este año fue coautor del libro

Agroecología en Municipios

, que repasa la construcción de la primera década de la Renama.


Desde el trabajo con los productores a la construcción de políticas públicas con los municipios y de allí a la Dirección Nacional de Agroecología (DNA), que encabezó durante el gobierno de Alberto Fernández y fue eliminada con la llegada de Javier Milei. “Los funcionarios públicos aún no han llegado a comprender lo que genera la agroecología en el campo, nosotros lo vemos funcionar y escuchamos a los productores decirnos: ‘La agroecología me salvó’”, asegura.


¿En qué situación está la agroecología a tres años de gobierno de Milei? Cerdá repasa las decisiones de la gestión de La Libertad Avanza para “desfinanciar y romper todo”. Desde la disolución de la DNA a la desarticulación del programa Cambio Rural del INTA —que durante la gestión anterior llegó a reunir cerca de 200 grupos con 1.600 productores agroecológicos—, la

eliminación del Inafci

, la decisión de

prohibir la mención a la palabra “agroecología”

 para realizar investigaciones en el INTA, la desjerarquización del Instituto Nacional de la Yerba Mate (INYM), con el que se habían iniciado cursos de planteos agroecológicos para sus equipos técnicos. Esas decisiones generaron un “amesetamiento”, analiza, que esté menos en la agenda pública, pero “por debajo la agroecología sigue en pie”, asegura.


“Este modelo de gobierno propone la disgregación, que el otro es tu enemigo. Eso afectó la mirada de los gobiernos provinciales y municipales, y generó una sensación de angustia”, señala Cerdá y por eso rescata el paso por la DNA que permitió “darle institucionalidad a la agroecología”. “Durante la gestión de la DNA aumentaron las ordenanzas municipales de restricción de agroquímicos, de fomento a la agroecología, las direcciones de agroecología, los proyectos de cesión de terrenos, ferias agroecológicas, entregas de semillas, cursos, sistemas participativos de garantías (SPG)”, enumera y reconoce que eso se realizó con un gestión que buscó fomentar, pero lo hizo sin presupuesto.


Foto: Renama


“El Estado es considerado como un presupuesto. A mí me puteaban mucho porque me decían 'este no hace política porque no le da bola al presupuesto’. Para mí el presupuesto es la gran encrucijada que te plantea el Estado”, contrapone y sostiene: “Si la zanahoria tiene que ser plata para que los productores hagan agroecología, no va por ahí, es un cambio de enfoque”


De todas formas también señala

la falta de voluntad que existió para la sanción de una Ley de Fomento a la Agroecología

 —se presentaron tres proyecto en el Congreso y no alcanzaron el tratamiento en el recinto— y propone otras políticas a encarar ante la vuelta de un gobierno que mire a la agroecología: Ley de Arrendamientos —a cuatro o cinco años para poder cuidar los suelos—, un plan estatal de rotación de cultivos, una Ley de Producción Apícola, Ley de Etiquetados de Transgénicos y un organismo que se encargue, de una vez, de medir la presencia de agrotóxicos en alimentos, agua, tierra y aire. “Iría por más capacitación, por más formación, con más grupos técnicos, a obtener más información de todos los productores agroecológicos, hacer redes de compra y venta”, concluye.


"

En l

a producción


extensiv

a


es donde está el gran cambio del modelo

"


Cerdá vuelve al presente, deja de lado la sensación de angustia de los tiempos actuales y resalta que “cuando se tejen vínculos, cuando nos encontramos, nos alegramos, nos damos cuenta que avanzamos, que hicimos cosas, que tenemos un camino para compartir”. Por eso la Renama continuó celebrando estos años el

Mes de la Agroecología

, estrenó el

documental

 “La Aurora: El principio del Camino” —sobre la historia del productor “faro”

Juan Khier

— y prepara una nuevo sobre la comensalidad para pensar: “¿Cómo me las arregló para cocinar y comer sano evitando tanto conservante y los productos ultraprocesados que son los que se venden en las góndolas de los supermercados?”.


También continúa fomentando la red …

author: Comunizar
title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Las protestas y las luchas en las que participaron Milton y Eneas no son terrorismo”
content:
La Coordinadora contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI) y la Gremial de Abogados reclaman el cierre de la causa contra Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, detenidos por haber participado de la masiva protesta ante el Congreso de la Nación contra la regresiva reforma laboral.


Compartimos el comunicado de CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogados:


LAS PROTESTAS Y LAS LUCHAS EN QUE PARTICIPARON MILTON Y ENEAS NO SON TERRORISMO LIBERTAD A MILTON Y ENEAS, CIERRE DE LA CAUSA.


El 11 de febrero de 2026 el Congreso Nacional perpetró un verdadero crimen al sancionar la llamada Ley de Reforma Laboral, que destruyó 200 años de derechos conquistados por las y los trabajadores de Argentina. Ese día hubo una masiva movilización en la Plaza de los Dos Congresos, con la participación de las centrales sindicales, infinidad de gremios y multitud de personas que manifestaron su repudio a lo que sucedía en el recinto.


Unos días después, varias personas que fueron “identificadas” a través de dudosos mecanismos de ciberpatrullaje y reconocimiento facial resultaron detenidas, acusadas de graves delitos por haber participado de la manifestación multitudinaria.


Desde mediados de febrero, dos trabajadores, Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, están detenidos en la prisión federal de Marcos Paz. A la vez, Oscar Rubén “Homero” Aguirre y Néstor Gabriel Barrera fueron detenidos y excarcelados, pero siguen procesados en la misma causa.


Cuando Milton fue detenido, se lo incluyó, por orden del Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional, en el SIGGPLAR (Sistema Integral de Gestión para Personas Privadas de la Libertad de Alto Riesgo), destinado a terroristas de gran peligrosidad, lo que significó un aislamiento absoluto, sin posibilidad de comunicarse ni tener visitas de sus familiares ni de sus defensores, con apenas una o dos horas de recreo para poder salir de su celda, usar los baños, comer o salir al patio, vigilado en todo momento por personal no identificado del Servicio Penitenciario Federal enmascarado con balaclavas.


Logramos, al mes, sacarlo de ese infierno y lograr su pase a un pabellón común.


Se los acusa por los delitos de tenencia de material incendiario, atentado y resistencia a la autoridad e intimidación pública, Milton y Eneas como coutores y Homero y Néstor como partícipes.


Como si eso fuera poco, ya esa acusación prevé la pena de 5 a 15 años de prisión, el Fiscal Stornelli requirió el agregado del agravante previsto en el art. 41 quinquies del Código Penal, que establece la duplicación de penas cuando el hecho se comete “para aterrorizar a la población u obligar a autoridades públicas nacionales, gobiernos extranjeros o agentes internacionales a realizar un acto o abstenerse de hacerlo”.


Este artículo fue incorporado al Código Penal en 2011 (ley 26.734), como parte de la batería de “leyes antiterroristas” dictadas a partir de 2007 por presión del GAFI (Grupo de Acción Financiera Internacional) y otros organismos internacionales de control financiero, y fue ampliado aún más en 2024 con la ley 27.739. Es una circunstancia agravante transversal a todo el Código Penal, que automáticamente lleva al doble la escala penal prevista, sin respetar el criterio de proporcionalidad de la pena.


Tanto al momento de su sanción inicial durante la presidencia de Cristina Fernández, como ante su reforma en la actual gestión de Javier Milei, desde las organizaciones populares y sectores académicos advertimos que es una norma peligrosísima, plagada de vaguedades, con expresiones completamente abiertas a la interpretación, como “aterrorizar a la población”, cuya definición queda discrecionalmente en manos de jueces y fiscales que decidan descargar todo su poder punitivo apuntando más a presuntas intencionalidades subjetivas del autor que a las características concretas de una conducta específica.


Decíamos también que, aunque la misma norma indica que esa agravante no se debe aplicar cuando los hechos de que se trate tuvieran lugar “en ocasión del ejercicio de derechos humanos y/o sociales o de cualquier otro derecho constitucional”, como es el de resistir una medida legislativa que cercena derechos, la falta de precisión de las definiciones que permiten cualquier interpretación intencionada de jueces y fiscales obedientes al poder político habilitan la indiscriminada persecución de la protesta y su híper criminalización.


Desde el inicio de la gestión del gobierno de la Libertad Avanza …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Por la salud y la vida del compañero Juan Aliste Vega. En el marco de una nueva conmemoración del 11 de septiembre
content:
Por la salud y la vida del compañero Juan Aliste Vega

En una noche de memoria, a 53 años de la barbarie dictatorial. Seguimos recordando a cada compañerx asesinadx, torturadx o desaparecidx, tanto en dictadura como en democracia. No desde la memoria pasiva, sino desde la acción subversiva, recordamos el pasado para cargarnos de aprendizajes y repensar el antagonismo del mañana.

Frente a un enemigo que precariza nuestras vidas, impone impunidad, miseria y devasta el mundo con guerras, ecocidios y genocidios. La propuesta desde el anarquismo organizado ha sido jamás dejar de resistir. Nos hemos abocado fervientemente a estar en la construcción de movimientos sociales y de organización popular. Siempre dotando de características anarquistas cada una de las trincheras de las que somos parte. Es decir, de autonomía, acción directa, horizontalidad y apoyo mutuo. A eso nos debemos compañeras/os, a dejar de poner la otra mejilla, organizarse y arrojarse al incomodo pero provechoso y necesario camino revolucionario para construir el mundo nuevo que queremos vivir.

Siempre sabiendo que el único poder capaz de hacer justicia a nuestro pueblo es el propio pueblo organizado.

Y particularmente también, considerando la urgente situación del compañero subversivo Juan Aliste, que afectado por los largos años de prisión, las duras condiciones de reclusión y las sistemáticas negligencias medicas-carcelarias hoy enfrenta nuevamente al estado, que en un afán vengativo niega otorgar cualquier beneficio, régimen alternativo o excarcelación, convirtiendo su enfermedad en prisión en una condena a muerte. Aún así, Juan Aliste Vega, sigue dando la pelea, enviando ánimos de resistencia y fortaleza, de lucha y dignidad. Ese es precisamente el ejemplo de coherencia del compañero, además de la de un hermano, amigo, expropiador, revolucionario, anticapitalista, padre e hijo; el de un combatiente contra la dictadura y su continuidad democrática, luchando dentro y fuera de la prisión, hasta las ultimas consecuencias. Desde esta perspectiva, efectivamente, la lucha por la salud, la vida y la liberación del prisionero subversivo Juan Aliste debe convocar nuestra más profunda atención.

Hasta el triunfo de la revolución social.

Porque nada ha acabado, nada ni nadie está olvidado.

Nuestro mejor homenaje es seguir combatiendo.

Muerte al Estado y que viva la anarquía.

author: anred
title: Violencia contra docentes: golpearon a un maestro en una escuela de Almirante Brown
content:
Un docente fue agredido el viernes por la tarde dentro de la Primaria N.º 36 de San José, Almirante Brown. La comunidad educativa logró resguardar a los estudiantes y contener la situación hasta la llegada de la policía. Ante el hecho, este lunes habrá paro docente distrital. Dialogamos con un docente de la institución, sobre lo ocurrido y la situación de violencia que atraviesan las escuelas.

Por ANRed


El viernes por la tarde, una madre que había sido convocada a una reunión con la directora de la Escuela Primaria N.º 36 de San José, en Almirante Brown, ingresó al establecimiento y agredió físicamente a uno de los docentes. Según relató a ANRed un profesor de la institución, la mujer golpeó al maestro en la cabeza, los hombros y la espalda mientras se encontraba frente a su grupo.


La situación se desencadenó luego de que la familia presentara quejas por el estado de angustia de una niña, quien había tenido un conflicto con otras estudiantes del establecimiento. El docente había intervenido para evitar la pelea y realizado un llamado de atención.


«El día viernes, la niña en cuestión no asistió a la escuela, pero su madre se presentó respondiendo a la citación. Al ingresar al establecimiento, se cruzó con el maestro, quien estaba frente a su grupo. Lo golpeó en su cabeza, hombros y espalda», explicó.


La agresión ocurrió frente a los estudiantes. Ante la situación, algunos niños intentaron interponerse para defender al docente. «Fue una situación muy dramática, dado que algunos niños se querían interponer entre él y la agresora, por lo que el maestro se abrazó con los alumnos para evitar que salieran lastimados», relató.


Entre cinco personas, entre ellas integrantes del equipo directivo, lograron separar a la agresora y poner al docente a resguardo. Mientras tanto, la vicedirectora contuvo a las familias que permanecían fuera de la escuela y habían escuchado los disturbios.


La situación volvió a tensarse cuando ingresaron otros familiares de la mujer. Ante la continuidad del conflicto, la escuela debió llamar al 911. «La mujer se retiró, pero el hombre se quedó acompañando a su hermana y acusándonos de cubrir al maestro, exigiendo que no debía trabajar más allí, y que sino iban a denunciarnos ante la justicia, ‘no lo queremos más acá’, nos decían», señaló el docente.


Una comunidad que se organizó para cuidar


Frente a la agresión, el cuerpo docente actuó siguiendo el plan de prevención de riesgos y priorizando el resguardo de los estudiantes y trabajadores.


«Los docentes del turno rápidamente actuamos según el plan de prevención de riesgo, el cuidado de los estudiantes y del personal, cada uno tomando el rol que le correspondía. Por eso, rápidamente se llamó al 911, se cerraron las puertas, se separaron a las partes conflictuadas, se resguardó a los niños y niñas, y se entregaron en mano a sus familiares», explicó.


Después de lo ocurrido, el cuerpo docente y directivo expresó su solidaridad con el maestro R. También hubo mensajes de apoyo de numerosas familias de la comunidad educativa.


Según relató el docente, el inspector del área 1 fue informado inmediatamente y acompañó la situación con orientaciones. También recibieron apoyo de organizaciones gremiales y asesoramiento de familiares de docentes vinculados a ámbitos de seguridad y justicia.


Para el entrevistado el desafío ahora es reconstruir las condiciones necesarias para continuar trabajando después de una situación de estas características.


«Será difícil, pero no imposible», sostuvo. Y destacó especialmente la actitud de las familias que permanecieron fuera de la escuela esperando de manera organizada hasta que todos los estudiantes pudieran retirarse.


«Valoro el respeto a la gestión de la escuela, a la autoridad pedagógica de los directivos, que produjo ese trabajo en conjunto para aminorar el daño, pues podría haber sido mayor. Considero que hay que valorar esto como comunidad, y seguir fortaleciendo los lazos de confianza, buena convivencia y resolución de conflictos.»


Paro docente y reclamo ante la violencia


El episodio de la Primaria N.º 36 no constituye, según docentes, un hecho aislado. Durante la semana anterior se habían registrado situaciones similares en Hurlingham, San Miguel, Ensenada y Guernica.


Frente a este escenario, este lunes se realizará un paro docente distrital. Para el docente, la medida resulta necesaria para visibilizar una problemática que atraviesa cotidianamente a las escuelas.

author: Natalia Viana
title: De apostas, predições e eleições
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Xeque na Democracia, enviada toda segunda-feira, 12h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui.


A seis dias da eleição, tudo o que queremos é saber:

quem vai ganhar?

 A urgência de adiantar o futuro, ou tentar mudar um futuro que nos parece imutável, é o que faz com que nós, pobres humanos, busquemos os oráculos, as adivinhações e

as apostas

. 


Foi a vontade de sair do buraco que levou milhões de brasileiras e brasileiros ao vício em apostas online, as bets, que sempre tiveram uma vantagem enorme sobre outros tipos, inclusive ilegais, como o Jogo do Bicho, porque aprenderam com as Big Techs a navegarem em um ambiente onde já estamos viciados à tela. Neste contexto, fazer um

design para viciar pessoas

 em jogos online é fácil e, como demonstrou nossa investigação, extremamente barato,

menos de mil reais

. O resultado, sabemos: uma nação viciada em jogos, ludopatia levando pessoas desesperadas ao SUS e ao suicídio, e uma fuga de 140 bilhões da economia brasileira. 


Pois isso tudo acabou na última sexta-feira, com uma canetada do presidente Lula. Ou melhor: é o começo do fim. 


O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva durante apresentação de novas medidas de proteção às famílias e à economia popular, como o fim das bets


Não há nenhuma dúvida de que Lula fez isso de olho nas eleições;

seu objetivo era claramente se colocar como aquele que acabou com as bets. Mas a Medida Provisória terá efeito para muito além do resultado eleitoral.

 Vai abrir um embate legal mais profundo – as bets vão recorrer à Justiça, o Congresso vai tentar derrubar – e, com isso, a sociedade será chamada a opinar, se mobilizar, a se mostrar de que lado está. 


Para fazer do seu ato algo permanente, Lula tem ao seu lado pesquisas que apontam que 75% dos brasileiros apoiam a proibição. Se outras pesquisas mostram que maioria diz que não vai mudar de voto por causa deste tema, isso é um problema menor. Em 5 de outubro, as malditas propagandas do tigrinho vão desaparecer das redes sociais, dos sites de notícias e dos programas esportivos da TV. Os aplicativos vão sumir das lojas de APPs; a poluição mental vai diminuir. Afinal, acessar os jogos ilegais tem um custo e uma fricção muito maior. 


Poderemos escutar o silêncio. 


Raramente dá pra dizer que uma investigação jornalística tem um impacto tão direto numa decisão do governo federal. Mas desta vez,

podemos dizer com orgulho: foi a nossa cobertura que tornou o tema relevante a ponto de convencer o presidente da República.

 


Desde 2025, preparamos com nossos repórteres uma grande investigação sobre o mercado de apostas online, em meio à epidemia de ludopatia. Para isso, fizemos uma campanha de arrecadação junto ao nosso público, e nos dedicamos a levantar histórias, documentos e dados sobre quem estava lucrando – inclusive os políticos que faziam lobby no Congresso – e quem eram as vítimas dessa realidade. Lançamos o especial

“

Jogo perigoso: O Brasil das Bets

”, em junho deste ano. 


Dentre os muitos documentos analisados pela nossa equipe, os jornalistas Thiago Domenici e Ed Wanderley encontraram uma carta de Vania Souza Borges, que perdeu o filho Rafael por causa de dívidas com as bets. A carta da professora de Uberlândia havia sido ignorada pela CPI das Bets – que terminou sem indiciar ninguém – mas Vânia abriu o coração aos nossos repórteres e comparou, pela primeira vez,

as bets com traficantes de drogas

. 


A história viralizou, e, em setembro, Vânia foi convidada para conhecer o presidente Lula. A ele, ela fez um pedido direto: “proíba as bets”. O pedido desta mãe, órfã de seu filho, foi hoje atendido pelo presidente da República.


Quando nenhum veículo dedica esforço e investimento para investigar a fundo o mundo das bets, nosso especial “

Jogo perigoso: O Brasil das Bets

” fez a diferença. 


Lula usou a comparação com vício em crack e

lembrou da Vânia ao assinar a Medida Provisória

. Compartilho aqui o agradecimento dessa mãe ao nosso trabalho. “Obrigada, Thiago! Devo muito à @agenciapublica toda a repercussão da minha triste história”.


Mas, enquanto podemos celebrar o fim das apostas, quero lembrar que, depois das bets, vêm os sites de apostas preditivas. Graças à coalizão LIE – Laboratórios de Investigação Eleitoral, uma parceria da

Pública

 com Aos Fatos, Amado Mundo e Núcleo, conseguimos mapear páginas da Polymarket em redes sociais postando …

title: Iran strikes Azadî Camp
content:
The Iranian state bombed Azadî Camp in the Koye district of Hewlêr (Erbil) with drones. Families of Peshmerga fighters affiliated with the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDP-I) live in the camp.

title: Safety Out, Fear In? The Mirage of Women’s Security under ‘Double Engine’ Government/s
content:
In a society where political leaders publicly endorse custodial deaths, support those accused or convicted of sexual offences, and scrutinise the ‘moral integrity’ of victims, the fear persists.


 


Debasree Sarkar


 


For the last few months of Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) ascendency to power on May 5, 2026, in West Bengal (WB), news reports of rapes of minors and women have become part of our daily routine. For example, in May, in Bankura’s Jaipur area, a BJP leader was arrested after being accused of raping a seven-year-old girl; an Adivasi woman was found dead in the Amrakola forest in Kharagpur after being brutally raped in May; in June, in the Chandrakona Road area of Paschim Midnapur, a woman accused a local BJP leader of dragging her from her home, physically assaulting her, and attempting to rape her while her husband was away; also in June, reports came of an alleged gang-rape of a minor Adivasi girl in Durgapur. There are many other cases, such as the alleged rape of a minor in Malda’s English Bazar area and the Baruipur minor girl rape and murder case in July; the Dhupgiri gang rape case in August; the alleged rape of a minor tribal girl in Belpahari on August 23; the alleged gang rape of a tribal woman in Lalgarh, and the Dinhata minor assault case in September, and so on.


The Adivasi community has been expressing outrage over incidents of sexual violence against tribal women over the past few months in the Jangalmahal region. The tribal social organization Bharat Jakat Majhi Paragana Mahal recently held a rally in Jhargram demanding women’s safety and swift justice for the complainants of sexual assault and violence. People from the various tribal communities of the region—including Jhargram, Purulia, Bankura, and Paschim Medinipur—along with local residents and representatives from various student and youth organizations have participated in the procession. Tribal community members stated that the atrocities against women witnessed in the few months following the change of government, are unprecedented in Bengal.


 


If we juxtapose this brief chronology of crimes against women in WB with the contemporary situation on a national level, these events illustrate a concerning depiction of the ongoing susceptibility of women, especially minors, Adivasi women, and those belonging to the minority community and economically disadvantaged social groups. The month of September only can reveal the concerning trend of women’s safety in the BJP-ruled states. As

The Print

reported, from a teenager allegedly gang-raped and killed in north Delhi to minors allegedly assaulted in homes, hotels, and various public spaces, at least 13 cases of alleged rape and sexual assault have been reported across the National Capital Region in September.


 


Several women students from different Delhi University colleges marched on September 25 in protest over violence against women following the alleged rape of a minor girl at the Aastha Kunj park with the slogan “Hum Auratein Azaad Hain” (we, the women, are free).

The

organizers criticised “protectionist policies” taken by the Delhi Development Authority’s alleged move to bar women from public parks after sunset, alongside colleges enforcing stricter hostel and PG curfews that effectively cage women rather than tackling offenders. It is not safe for women to drive on the roads of Delhi anymore. On September 12, a woman scooterist alleged that two men riding a motorcycle stalked and harassed her before hitting her scooter near South Delhi’s Panchsheel Metro Station, and the very next day, a video recorded by a camera mounted on Shivani Chauhan’s bike, appears to show a white car moving close and hitting her motorcycle. In the Hasanpur-Kotwali area in Uttar Pradesh’s Amroha district, two police personnel and two Central Reserve Police Force personnel have been arrested for allegedly raping a woman on 23rd September. And how can we forget the harassment and sexual assault of the minor girl from Jamui? Within a few days of this shocking incident, another minor girl was molested at Samastipur, Bihar.
