author: Alyssa Mae Clarin
title: Gov’t grants Mary Jane Veloso absolute pardon after 16 years
content:
May Jane Veloso is welcomed by her family at the Correctional Institute for Women in Mandaluyong City, Dec. 18. (Photo by Deo Montesclaros/ Pinoy Weekly)

Veloso’s freedom was not granted voluntarily but was won through years of struggle by her family, lawyers, and supporters.

MANILA — Nearly two years since her return to the Philippines in December 2024, Mary Jane Veloso has been granted an absolute pardon by Ferdinand Marcos Jr., ending more than 16 years of detention stemming from a drug trafficking case in Indonesia.

“Pinirmahan ko na yung pardon niya kahapon,” (I already signed [the pardon] yesterday) Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told reporters during an interview in Eastern Samar.

The development came after Malacañang Press Officer Claire Castro said the president was “seriously considering” granting Veloso an absolute pardon. Veloso had been sentenced to death in Indonesia after authorities accused her of carrying 2.6 kilograms of heroin in 2010.

She was granted last-minute reprieve following international pressure on the Indonesian government.

Veloso’s lawyers from the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) welcomed the decision, describing it as a “long-awaited act” that brings immeasurable relief to Veloso, her family, and the many supporters who stood by her throughout her years of detention.

Prior to the pardon, Veloso sent a handwritten letter to Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, reiterating that she was serving a sentence of reclusion perpetua despite what she said was the absence of any legal basis for such classification.

The NUPL also questioned Veloso’s continued detention after her transfer to the Philippines on December 18, 2024. The group argued that the Philippine government had no legal authority to continue enforcing a foreign criminal judgment in the absence of a treaty governing the transfer of sentenced prisoners.

Read: Lawyers, parents of Mary Jane Veloso urge SC to act on habeas corpus petition

Gabriela Women’s Party Rep. Sarah Elago said Veloso’s freedom was not granted voluntarily but was won through years of struggle by her family, lawyers, and supporters.

“Mary Jane should have been freed long ago. For years, we have asserted that she was a victim of human trafficking and exploitation, not a criminal who deserved punishment. Her release is a recognition of the long struggle to correct a grave injustice,” Elago said in Filipino.

She added that Veloso’s case reflects broader conditions that force millions of Filipinos to seek work abroad because of low wages, poverty, and the lack of decent jobs.

Elago further said, “As long as a system that relies on cheap labor and forced migration remains in place, our fellow Filipinos will continue to be vulnerable to trafficking, exploitation, and other forms of abuse.”

Migrante International also welcomed the grant of absolute pardon, describing it as a victory born from years of collective struggle, including vigils, rallies, protest actions, petition drives, letter and phone campaigns, and lobbying efforts.

“At the heart of this global campaign is the sheer determination of Mary Jane’s parents and family who did not waver in their commitment to pursue justice despite all the odds they faced,” Migrante said.

While welcoming the pardon, however, the group stressed that Veloso’s freedom was “long overdue,” saying the Marcos administration had also committed a grave injustice by prolonging her detention in a Philippine prison for one year and nine months despite the absence of charges against her in Philippine courts.

“Our campaign does not end here,” Migrante said. “This victory gives us the inspiration, courage and fuel to advance our movement to free migrant workers from exploitation and assert their full economic, social and political rights abroad and at home.”

For the NUPL, Veloso’s case has become emblematic of the plight of migrant workers and trafficking victims.

“Mary Jane’s story is one of extraordinary courage and resilience,” the group said in a statement, noting that despite coming perilously close to execution, Veloso never lost hope.

“She became a powerful symbol of the struggles endured by countless Filipinos driven abroad by necessity and made vulnerable to trafficking and exploitation,” the NUPL added.

“Her freedom is cause for celebration. It is also a reminder of why trafficking victims must be met first with protection, compassion, and justice, and why no victim should have to spend years fighting simply to be …

title: 20ό Αντιρατσιστικό Φεστιβάλ –  Γιορτή Κοινωνικής Αλληλεγγύης Χανίων, 25-26/9, στο πάρκο Ειρήνης & Φιλίας των λαών
content:
Αφίσα/Πρόγραμμα:


20ό Αντιρατσιστικό Φεστιβάλ –


Γιορτή Κοινωνικής Αλληλεγγύης Χανίων


25 & 26 Σεπτεμβρίου 2026 | Πάρκο Ειρήνης και Φιλίας των Λαών


20ό Αντιρατσιστικό Φεστιβάλ Γιορτή Κοινωνικής Αλληλεγγύης Χανίων


«Δεν παζαρεύουμε κι ως τον ύστατο χτύπο της καρδιάς μας θ’ αντιστεκόμαστε»


Σαμίχ Αλ Κάσεμ | Παλαιστίνιος ποιητής [παράφραση]


20 χρόνια συναντιόμαστε. 20 χρόνια επιμένουμε.


Απέναντι στον πόλεμο, τον ρατσισμό και τον αποκλεισμό, απαντάμε με αλληλεγγύη.


Υπάρχουν στιγμές που η αλληλεγγύη δεν είναι απλώς μια επιλογή αλλά γίνεται ανάγκη. Η σημερινή είναι μία από αυτές. Ζούμε σε μια εποχή όπου ο πόλεμος παύει να αποτελεί εξαίρεση και μετατρέπεται σε μια διαρκή συνθήκη. Από την Παλαιστίνη και τη συνεχιζόμενη γενοκτονία στη Γάζα μέχρι τους πολέμους και τις στρατιωτικές επεμβάσεις που απλώνονται στη Μέση Ανατολή, ολόκληρες κοινωνίες πληρώνουν με νεκρούς, εκτοπισμό, πείνα και καταστροφή.


Ζούμε σε μια εποχή όπου ο πόλεμος παύει να αποτελεί εξαίρεση και μετατρέπεται σε μια διαρκή συνθήκη. Από την Παλαιστίνη και τη συνεχιζόμενη γενοκτονία στη Γάζα μέχρι τους πολέμους και τις στρατιωτικές επεμβάσεις που απλώνονται στη Μέση Ανατολή, ολόκληρες κοινωνίες πληρώνουν με νεκρούς, εκτοπισμό, πείνα και καταστροφή. Την ίδια στιγμή, στην Ευρώπη και αλλού η ακροδεξιά δυναμώνει, ο ρατσισμός και ο εθνικισμός κανονικοποιούνται και οι στρατιωτικοί προϋπολογισμοί εκτοξεύονται. Το ΝΑΤΟ έχει πλέον δεσμεύσει τα κράτη-μέλη του σε δαπάνες που θα φτάνουν το 5% του ΑΕΠ έως το 2035, ενώ η πολεμική βιομηχανία καλείται να αυξήσει με ταχύτητα την παραγωγή της. Λεφτά υπάρχουν αρκεί όμως να προορίζονται για όπλα, φράχτες και πολέμους.


Στα Χανιά δεν μπορούμε να μιλάμε για όλα αυτά σαν να συμβαίνουν κάπου μακριά μας, αφού λίγο έξω από την πόλη βρίσκεται ένας από τους σημαντικότερους στρατιωτικούς κόμβους των ΗΠΑ και του ΝΑΤΟ στην Ανατολική Μεσόγειο. Η ίδια η αμερικανική διοίκηση περιγράφει τη νατοϊκή βάση στη Σούδα ως στρατηγικά τοποθετημένη για την «προβολή ισχύος», με αεροδρόμιο, εγκαταστάσεις ανεφοδιασμού και τη δυνατότητα υποστήριξης αμερικανικών, ΝΑΤΟϊκών και συμμαχικών επιχειρήσεων στην Ευρώπη, την Αφρική και τη Μέση Ανατολή. Τον Μάρτη του 2026, το αμερικανικό αεροπλανοφόρο USS Gerald R. Ford κατέπλευσε στη Σούδα για επισκευές και ανεφοδιασμό μετά από επιχειρήσεις στην Ερυθρά Θάλασσα. Ο πόλεμος δεν βρίσκεται μακριά μας. Περνά και από τον τόπο μας.


Και από την άλλη πλευρά της ίδιας θάλασσας βρίσκονται εκείνοι και εκείνες που προσπαθούν να ξεφύγουν από τους πολέμους, τη φτώχεια, τις διώξεις και την καταστροφή. Η Κρήτη και η Γαύδος έχουν μετατραπεί σε μία από τις βασικές πύλες εισόδου προσφύγικών ροών και μεταναστών στην Ευρώπη. Μόνο το πρώτο εξάμηνο του 2026 καταγράφηκαν 8.552 αφίξεις σε 198 περιστατικά, περίπου το 70% των αφίξεων ολόκληρης της χώρας εκείνη την περίοδο.


Πίσω όμως από τους αριθμούς υπάρχουν άνθρωποι. Και υπάρχουν νεκροί. Τον Φλεβάρη του 2026, ναυάγιο στους Καλούς Λιμένες άφησε πίσω του τρεις νεκρούς και 25 αγνοούμενους. Τον Μάρτη, επιζώντες από άλλο ναυάγιο ανοιχτά της Ιεράπετρας κατέθεσαν ότι 22 άνθρωποι έχασαν τη ζωή τους στη διάρκεια του ταξιδιού. Τον Ιούνιο, ένας 30χρονος από το Μπαγκλαντές, που είχε διασωθεί μαζί με άλλους 37 ανθρώπους νοτιοανατολικά της Ιεράπετρας, πέθανε λίγες ημέρες αργότερα στο Νοσοκομείο Χανίων. Η Μεσόγειος εξακολουθεί να είναι ένας από τους πιο θανατηφόρους δρόμους μετανάστευσης στον κόσμο, κι εμείς ζούμε ακριβώς πάνω στο σύνορό της.


Κι όταν οι άνθρωποι καταφέρνουν τελικά να φτάσουν ζωντανοί στην ακτή, η υποδοχή που τους περιμένει απέχει πολύ από αυτό που σημαίνει η λέξη «φιλοξενία». Στην Κρήτη, και ειδικότερα στα Χανιά, χιλιάδες άνθρωποι έχουν περάσει από τον ακατάλληλο και απάνθρωπο χώρο προσωρινής παραμονής/φυλακής στην Αγυιά, με το πρόβλημα ασφαλούς και αξιοπρεπούς φιλοξενίας να παραμένει άλυτο, ενώ το υπουργείο πλέον τον βαφτίζει νέα «προτυπή» δομή προσωρινής φιλοξενίας προσφύγων και προχωρά στην κατασκευή «περίφραξης τύπου ΝΑΤΟ», δημόσιας δαπάνης 75.000 ευρώ . Την ίδια στιγμή, δίνονται 5 εκατομμύρια ευρώ για τη μεταφορά 5.000 αιτούντων άσυλο από την Κρήτη προς την ηπειρωτική χώρα. Η επιλογή είναι αποκαλυπτική: αντί για αξιοπρεπείς ανοιχτούς χώρους φιλοξενίας, περίφραξη, επιτήρηση και εγκλεισμός.


Στην ίδια κατεύθυνση κινείται συνολικά η μεταναστευτική πολιτική, με τη μία νομοθετική σκλήρυνση να διαδέχεται την άλλη. Το πλαίσιο του 2025 ποινικοποίησε την παραμονή χωρίς χαρτιά, αύξησε τις ποινές για παράτυπη είσοδο και επέκτεινε τη διοικητική κράτηση έως και τους 24 μήνες. Το …

title: Filikaya binen binene, tüm siyasi bağlantılar açıklanacak mı? 900 milyarlık fon vurgunu AKP’yi sallıyor
content:
Milyonlarca emeklinin ve asgari ücretlinin geçim savaşı verdiği, 26 Eylül’de Ankara'nın orta yerinde “Para için değil, onurumuz içim” diyerek Ali Şekeroğlu’nun ölümüne dair öfke artarken, 900 milyar liralık "fon ve borsa vurgunu" birkaç ayda milyarlar alan isimler açığa çıktı, AKP’ye uzandı. Ayrıca hakkında daha önce yurt dışına çıkış yasağı kararı verilen Tera Portföy Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Erdin Özel ve şirketin CEO'su Emir Münir Sarpyener dün gözaltına alındı. Erdin Özel'in gözaltı aracındaki kelepçeli fotoğrafı ve Münir Sarpyener'in kelepçeli görüntüleri Anadolu Ajansı tarafından basına servis edildi.

Fon vurgunu AKP içinde büyük bir krizin ve güç savaşının fitilini ateşledi. Skandalın patlak vermesinin ardından ifşa olan, hedef tahtasına oturtulan ilk isim eski Aile ve Sosyal Politikalar Bakanı, AKP MKYK Üyesi ve Genel Başkan Yardımcısı Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya oldu. Kamuoyunda yükselen tepkiler ve parti içinden gelen doğrudan çağrıların ardından Kaya, görevlerinden "affını" talep ederek istifa etti. Kaya’nın ‘görevden af’ talebi ise kabul edildi.

Soruşturmanın siyasi ayağına dair en somut verileri Yeni Parti Sözcüsü Zeynel Emre kamuoyuyla paylaştı. Emre, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya’nın borsa ve fon işlemleri üzerinden sadece 4 ay gibi kısa bir sürede milyarlarca liralık haksız kazanç sağladığını söyledi.

Emre, “Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, 8 Nisan tarihinde Özata Denizcilik hisselerinden 255 TL fiyatla 250 bin adet satın aldı. Toplamda 63 milyon 359 bin TL yatıran Kaya, Eylül ayına gelindiğinde hisseleri 4 bin 482 TL seviyesinden satarak 1 milyar 344 milyon TL nakit çekti. Eşi İlyas Kaya, aynı şekilde 255 TL’den 150 bin adet hisse alıp 99 milyon 687 bin TL yatırdı. Eylül ayında satarak 826 milyon TL elde etti” dedi.

Gelişmeler üzerine iddiaları sormak isteyen basın mensuplarına sadece "Müsait değilim" yanıtını veren Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, parti içinde de yalnız bırakıldı. AKP’li Şamil Tayyar sosyal medya hesabından çıkış yaparak, "İddialar doğruysa kabul edilemez, hemen istifa etmeli. Doğru değilse yalanlayıp dava açmalı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı son 3 ayda fonlardan çıkış yapanların listesini istedi, haberiniz olsun" ifadelerini kullandı.

Aynı günün akşam saatlerinde açıklama yapan Kaya, görevlerinden "affını istediğini" duyurdu. AKP Sözcüsü Ömer Çelik ise istifanın ardından bir gün sonra adını anmadan "Her türlü yanlış, yolsuzluk ve usulsüzlükle mücadele tavizsiz verilecektir" açıklamasını yaptı.

Ayrıca basında yer alan iddialara göre, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, eşi İlyas Kaya ve çocuklarının mal varlıklarına kısıtlama getirilmesini, gayrimenkul, araç ve menkul kıymetlerinin dondurulmasını talep etti. Kaya’nın, skandal patlak verdikten sonra partideki üst düzey isimlere "ağlayarak parayı iade etmeyi teklif ettiği" de iddialar arasında yer aldı.

Öte yandan skandalın kalbindeki şirketin patronunun Tuzla siyasetindeki geçmişi açığa çıktı. Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınıp tutuklanan Özata Denizcilik’in Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Özdemir Ataseven’in de AKP Tuzla İlçe Başkan Yardımcılığı yaptığı ve eski AKP’li Tuzla Belediye Başkanı Şadi Yazıcı’nın ekibinde yer aldığı belirlendi. Şirketin diğer tutuklu ismi Gökhan Ataseven’in de 2018 yılındaki nikâhını Şadi Yazıcı’nın kıydığı, şahitliklerini ise iktidar kanadından üst düzey siyasetçilerin yaptığı öğrenildi. Binali Yıldırım’a yakınlığıyla bilinen Ataseven ailesinin ticari ve siyasi merkez adresi ise yine Tuzla. Çağdaş Tuzla’da yer alan soruşturma detaylarına göre, fon üzerinden fiyatı yapay şekilde şişirilen Özata Denizcilik hisseleri için 9,7 milyar TL ödeme yapıldı ve binlerce küçük yatırımcı mağdur edildi. Şüpheli işlemlerin tespit edilmesiyle birlikte Özdemir Ataseven ve Gökhan Ataseven tutuklanarak cezaevine gönderildi.

Gazeteci Barış Pehlivan ise Özata Denizcilik’in yönetim kurulunda da kriz patlamadan hemen önce kritik bir ayrılık yaşandığını açıkladı. Pehlivan, şirketin yönetim kurulu üyesi İskender Balcı’nın aniden görevinden istifa ettiğini belirterek belgesini kamuoyuyla paylaştı.

Söz konusu istifayı, "Tıpkı hisselerini satıp milyar kazanan Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya gibi, filikaya binip gemiyi terk etme" olarak nitelendiren Barış Pehlivan, istifa eden İskender Balcı’nın Hazine ve Maliye Bakan Yardımcısı Osman Çelik’in damadı olduğu ortaya çıktı. Pehlivan, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda; "Memleketin hazinesini emanet ettiğimiz insanların pek 'akıllı' damatları nerelerden çıkıyor? Sahi …

author: rezgar2
title: Un arma de destrucción masiva sin explosión: la inteligencia artificial y el desmantelamiento de la mente humana
content:
REzgar Akrawi: Lo que tenemos hoy delante no es un destino técnico ineludible. Es el producto de decisiones políticas y económicas que sirven a los intereses del capital, y puede ser combatido. Ello exige una organización de izquierda, progresista y de derechos a escala mundial, trabajar por construir alternativas digitales de izquierda y progresistas, situar la infraestructura de datos bajo el interés público y la administración social, convertir los algoritmos de «cajas negras» en software de código abierto sometido a auditoría independiente, imponer la transparencia en el diseño de los modelos y en las fuentes de sus datos, apoyar alternativas digitales cooperativas propiedad de quienes las usan y de quienes trabajan en ellas, y orientar esta tecnología al servicio de las necesidades de la sociedad y de la justicia social. Sin estos mecanismos, el llamamiento a las leyes y a la supervisión sigue siendo general e insuficiente, y la tecnología continúa rehén de un puñado de corporaciones monopolistas y de grandes potencias. En cambio, mediante la propiedad social, la rendición de cuentas social y las alternativas cooperativas, se vuelve posible arrancar la inteligencia artificial a la lógica del monopolio y del beneficio, y convertirla en propiedad colectiva y en un medio de liberación humana.

Lo que presenciamos hoy no es una toma del poder sobre la humanidad por parte de los robots, tal como la imaginó el cine. Es otro modelo de control digital, asentado en la automatización y en los algoritmos para gestionar ámbitos cada vez mayores de la vida cotidiana. Perder el control sobre estos sistemas es, sin embargo, solo el lado ruidoso del peligro, que se desarrolla con rapidez por efecto de la competencia entre las grandes potencias y las corporaciones monopolistas, hasta el punto de que las leyes no logran seguirle el paso, y su desarrollo ocurre dentro de relaciones de propiedad y de una competencia feroz que hacen más probable que se salgan de control y multiplican su coste para la gente. Su cara más grave es mucho más callada, ya que la inteligencia artificial, bajo la estructura capitalista que la desarrolla, contribuye a moldear la conciencia de miles de millones de personas en un sentido que sirve a la lógica del modelo capitalista, y esta competencia puede, a falta de leyes eficaces, infligir los daños más graves a la mente humana y convertir la inteligencia artificial en un arma de destrucción masiva.

Estas inquietudes ya no provienen únicamente de quienes critican. La revista TIME reveló que un sistema de inteligencia artificial se salió de control y atacó a otros sistemas, y días después cerca de 1.400 ingenieras e ingenieros de las mayores empresas firmaron una petición conjunta que reclama poner freno al ritmo del desarrollo, y entre quienes la suscribieron figuran altos responsables de esas mismas empresas. Decenas de miles de personas, entre ellas científicos destacados del campo, han firmado una declaración internacional que exige prohibir el desarrollo de la «superinteligencia» mientras no exista un consenso científico sobre su seguridad, mientras pensadores y técnicos han reclamado que su desarrollo se regule por ley y quede bajo supervisión social.

El 12 de septiembre de 2026, bajo una presión mundial popular, de derechos humanos y también técnica, las corporaciones del capitalismo digital se vieron obligadas a romper su silencio. Dario Amodei, director ejecutivo de Anthropic, publicó un artículo titulado «Debemos pautar el ritmo de la frontera» en el que llama a su propia industria a frenar la carrera del desarrollo y propone abrir los laboratorios a evaluadores independientes con plenas atribuciones, un organismo de normas comunes entre las empresas y un acuerdo internacional que incluya a China. En cuestión de horas Sam Altman anunció su acuerdo y adoptó la misma medida, Elon Musk escribió «Dario tiene razón», y a ellos se sumó Demis Hassabis, de Google DeepMind, mientras las tres empresas revelaron que llevaban semanas dialogando sobre el asunto.

Esta admisión de los propios propietarios es la confirmación más clara de la gravedad de la situación, pues dicen abiertamente que no pueden detenerse por separado, porque quien baja el ritmo pierde frente a sus competidores, lo que significa que el núcleo del problema está en la estructura misma de la propiedad y de la competencia. title: ΒΑΛΚΑΝΙΚΟ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟ ΦΕΣΤΙΒΑΛ ΒΙΒΛΙΟΥ 2026 ΣΚΟΠΙΑ Αυτόνομες δομές, κοινότητες αγώνα και κοινωνικό κίνημα ενάντια σε πόλεμο, μιλιταρισμό, φασισμό, καπιταλισμό
content:
Ανταπόκριση infolibre


3η μέρα χθες Σάββατο 25/9 στο Balkan Anarchist Bookfair που πραγματοποιείται αυτό το τετραήμερο στη Σχολή Καλών Τεχνών στην πρωτεύουσα της Βόρειας Μακεδονίας. Sυνεχίστηκαν οι εκδηλώσεις με πλούσιες σε περιεχόμενο συζητήσεις και θέματα: η άνοδος του φασισμού σήμερα και η απάντηση του κινήματος, η διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη και οι προκλήσεις οργάνωσής της, η οικοδόμηση αυτόνομων χώρων και υπεράσπισής τους. Παράλληλα διοργανώθηκαν εργαστήρια και συναντήσεις για: εκδόσεις, με συγγραφείς, την ΑΙ, την τέχνη ως πράξη αντίστασης κα.


>Οικοδομώντας και προστατεύοντας αυτόνομους χώρους


Οκτώ συλλογικότητες τοποθετήθηκαν στη συζήτηση με θέμα τις καταλήψεις και τους αυτοδιαχειριζόμενους χώρους. Η συζήτηση κράτησε πάνω από δύο ώρες και έθεσε ζητήματα που συνδυάζουν τα οργανωτικά προτάγματα με τις πολιτικές αξίες και την καθημερινή πρακτική.


Το κοινωνικό κέντρο της

Πρίστινα

,

Komuna

, οργανωτικός πυρήνας του Βαλκανικού Αναρχικού Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου το 2024, μίλησαν για τον θετικό ρόλο που έπαιξε η διοργάνωση του ΒΑΒ στην πόλη τους, αφού ενθάρρυνε πολλές νέες ομάδες και εργατικά σωματεία να συνδέσουν τις δραστηριότητές τους με την Komuna.


Σε μερικές μέρες το

Dunja

 κλείνει δέκα χρόνια ζωής. Έχει επιτύχει μια αξιόλογη απήχηση στην κοινωνία των

Σκοπίων

 και είναι χαρακτηριστικό ότι οι διαδηλώσεις στην πόλη οργανώνονται εκεί. Στον χώρο δραστηριοποιούνται, πέρα από τις αναρχικές συλλογικότητες και κομμουνιστικές και καλλιτεχνικές ομάδες.


To κοινωνικό κέντρο στο Τέτοβο, ο δεύτερος χώρος στη Βόρεια Μακεδονία μετά το Dunja, δημιουργήθηκε από ένα δίκτυο ατόμων από πολλές βαλκανικές χώρες. Είναι η τρίτη τους προσπάθεια για τη συγκρότηση ενός αυτοδιαχειριζόμενου χώρου. Όπως και το Dunja και η Komuna, έτσι και το

Space Tetova

 είναι και χώροι αντικουλτούρας και καλλιτεχνικής έκφρασης.


Ιδιαίτερα σημαντική ήταν η παρουσίαση της πεντάμηνης κατάληψης

SKC u blokadi

, το κέντρο αναφοράς του πιο ριζοσπαστικού κομματιού του κινήματος που ξέσπασε τον Φεβρουάριο του 2025 μετά το σιδηροδρομικό δυστύχημα – κρατικό έγκλημα στο

Νόβι Σαντ της Σερβίας

. Η κατάληψη, σε κρατικό και απαξιωμένο πλέον φοιτητικό πολιτιστικό κέντρο, προσέλκυσε χιλιάδες ανθρώπους στις πολιτικές και πολιτιστικές της εκδηλώσεις και είναι χαρακτηριστικό ότι πολλοί δήθεν προοδευτικοί πολιτικοί χώροι επιχείρησαν να προσεταιριστούν και να διεκδικήσουν την ακτινοβολία του.


Οι υπόλοιπες τρεις παρουσιάσεις ήταν από την ελληνική γεωγραφία. Η κατάληψη της

Υφανέτ

 έκανε ένα ιστορικό της κρατικής καταστολής και των πρακτικών της κατάληψης. Από μέλη της

πρώην Κατάληψης μεταναστ(ρι)ών Ορφανοτροφείο 

(2015-6) έγινε παρουσίαση της κρατικής αντιμεταναστευτικής πολιτικής το καλοκαίρι του 2015, τη μετέπειτα ΜΚΟ-ποίηση της «διαχείρισης του προσφυγικού» και την ωμή φασιστικοποίηση από το 2019, τονίζοντας πόσο σημαντικό είναι οι χώροι μας να φέρνουν σε επαφή μεταξύ τους πραγματικότητες που το κράτος και το κεφάλαιο θέλουν εντελώς διαχωρισμένες τη μία από την άλλη. Με αφορμή μια συζήτηση για τον ρόλο της εκκλησίας στα Βαλκάνια, παρέμβαση έγινε και από τον 

Ελεύθερο Κοινωνικό Χώρο Σχολείο

, περιουσία της Εκκλησίας Α.Ε., στην οποία δόθηκε έμφαση στον ρόλο της κατάληψης ως προτάγματος επανοικειοποίησης του κοινωνικού πλούτου που υπεξαιρεί η εκκλησία.


Τα

Προσφυγικά

 αναφέρθηκαν ως διαρκής έμπνευση σε πολλές βαλκανικές πόλεις. Στην εισήγηση των Προσφυγικών περιγράφηκε η πολυμορφία στη σύνθεση του πληθυσμού και τα εγχειρήματα αυτοοργάνωσης, από το Συλλογικό Αρτοποιείο και το Παιδικό Στέκι μέχρι το Αυτοοργανωμένη Δομή Υγείας και τον αυτοδιαχειριζόμενο ξενώνα για συγγενείς ασθενών του γειτονικού νοσοκομείου Άγιος Σάββας. Τέλος, μεταφέρθηκαν νέα από την υγεία των απεργών πείνας Αρίστου και της Σουζόν και την επιστροφή τους στις δραστηριότητες της κατάληψης. Ας σημειωθεί ότι δράσεις αλληλεγγύης στον πρόσφατο νικηφόρο αγώνα τους έγιναν σε πολλές βαλκανικές πόλεις.


>Άνοδος του φασισμού και οι απαντήσεις του κινήματος


Οι συμμετέχοντες αναφέρθηκαν στην άνοδο των φασιστικών μορφωμάτων στις διάφορες Βαλκανικές χώρες. Όχι μόνο ως ανάδυσή τους από τα κάτω στρώματα της κοινωνίας, αλλά και ως κρατική μορφή πολιτικής εξουσίας όπως πχ στην Τουρκία.


Επιχειρήθηκε να απαντηθεί το ερώτημα τις είδους δράση μπορεί να αναπτυχθεί, με μαζικά και συμπεριληπτικά χαρακτηριστικά. Να απελευθερώνουμε από φασίστες περιοχές και γειτονιές, ώστε να μη μπορούν να κάνουν την εμφάνισή τους. Γι αυτό να ασκηθούμε στην αυτοάμυνα. Επίσης, αναφέρθηκε η διείσδυση και αξιοποίηση του διαδικτυακού …

title: [Podcast] Éléments pour une critique de l'intelligence artificielle
content:
Les questions autour de l'intelligence artificielle hantent les discussions et débats théoriques contemporains sur le futur de l'économie, du capitalisme et de l'humanité. Dans la continuité d'une série d'émissions de «

 

Sortir du capitalisme

 

» qui tentaient déjà d'articuler critique de la technologie et du capitalisme, il s'agit de reprendre ces théories critiques tout en les actualisant à l'aune de l'

IA

.


Il ne s'agit pas de présenter une théorie définitive de l'intelligence artificielle, mais de discuter des débats qui animent les espaces de réflexion théorique autour de ces questions pour essayer d'y voir plus clair. Il s'agira aussi de dépasser les critiques qui se limitent à la «

 

bulle

 

» de l'

IA

 (financière et technologique) et de se concentrer sur les effets concrets de l'intelligence artificielle sur l'économie et le travail, notamment à travers les théories marxiennes autour de l'automation.


Sommaire de l'épisode :

Définitions et exemples des différents types d'intelligence artificielle (à partir de 7min36)

Discussion du lien entre

IA

 et automatisation (à partir de 15min11)

Brève histoire politique et économique de l'

IA

 (avant les années 2000) (à partir de 17min58)

Présentation des acteurs politiques et économiques actuels de l'

IA

 (après les années 2000) et de leurs stratégies (à partir de 25min14)

Description du procès de travail dans le secteur de l'

IA

 et son automatisation (à partir de 34min02)

L'impact/l'intérêt de l'

IA

 dans un capitalisme en stagnation (à partir de 44min32)

La défense du principe que tout travail est automatisable (à partir de 57min34)

Témoignages sur l'impact de l'

IA

 au travail (à partir de 1h5min40)

Précisions sur la notion de déqualification et la perspective d'un travail misérable pour nourrir des secteurs très automatisés (à partir de 1h8min24)

Pêle-mêle, quelques dernières remarques sur l'

IA

 et le travail : la division spatiale du travail

 

; l'automatisation d'un travail déjà dominé par le capital

 

; et l'hypothèse d'une prolétarisation des machines (à partir de 1h1min37)

Un survol d'autres critiques de l'

IA

, notamment sur l'impact écologique et sur les utilisation ou biais discriminatoires de certaines

IA

 (à partir de 1h16min30)

Un survol des luttes actuelles contre l'

IA

 et son infrastructure (à partir de 1h20min37)

author: Unknown
title: Of Soil and Blood: Lu Xun’s Revolutionary Literature Ninety Years After His Death
content:
The Thirty-First Art Bulletin (September 2026)


Listen to ‘

Pioneers Who Open the Road

’ (1934), composed by Nie Er with lyrics by Sun Shiyi for Sun Yu’s film

The Big Road

, a landmark of Shanghai’s left-wing cinema of the 1930s.


As I sat on a plane from Hong Kong to Beijing, I reread the speeches that Lu Xun – known as the father of modern Chinese literature – had delivered in Hong Kong almost exactly a century earlier. It is commonly said that around 1927 Lu Xun bid farewell to fiction and made a leftward turn ideologically. He increasingly turned to

zawen

 – short, polemical essays – as his principal means of intervening in the political and cultural struggles of his time, awakening the Chinese people, and giving voice to a nation living under semi-colonial and semi-feudal conditions. To mark ninety years since Lu Xun’s passing in 1936, this art bulletin revisits several zawen from the final decade of his life.


One such text is ‘Voiceless China’, a speech Lu Xun delivered at the Chinese YMCA of Hong Kong on 18 February 1927. Lu Xun championed

baihua

, or vernacular written Chinese, over Classical Chinese. He criticised the use of an ‘archaic language good only for expressing ancient and obsolete ideas’. In a society where illiteracy remained widespread, the distance between Classical Chinese and the language of everyday life placed yet another barrier between most people and the written word, while Classical Chinese itself could no longer adequately express their thoughts, feelings, and struggles. Lu Xun therefore called on young people to ‘transform China into a China with a voice’, insisting that only then could they ‘live in the world with others’. For him, this search was also part of a wider internationalist struggle, with China’s liberation bound up with that of other colonised peoples. ‘Have we heard voices from Egypt?’ he asked. ‘Have we heard the voices of Vietnam and Korea? Aside from Tagore, does India have any other voices?’


Against Despair


Käthe Kollwitz,

Sharpening the Scythe

, 1905.


The following day, on 19 February, Lu Xun delivered another speech at the Hong Kong YMCA, returning to the question of how China’s new voice might be created. In ‘The Old Tunes Are Finished’, he looked to revolutionary Russia – ten years into its socialist revolution – as a guiding light, a society where a new voice had emerged and the old songs were no longer being sung. For Lu Xun, this process was neither solitary nor individualistic. One person’s awakening could give rise to others, linking individual transformation to a broader collective awakening.


The year 1927 was tumultuous for China. By then, the republic established after the 1911 Revolution, which had brought an end to more than two thousand years of dynastic rule, had failed to overcome warlord rule, feudal oppression, and foreign imperial domination. With the support of the Comintern, the Chinese Communist Party (CPC) and the nationalist Kuomintang (KMT) had formed the First United Front, a short-lived alliance aimed at defeating the regional warlords and unifying China. One of its most important military institutions was the Whampoa Military Academy, founded with Soviet assistance, where Nationalist and Communist cadres trained alongside one another. Chiang Kai-shek served as its commandant, while Zhou Enlai had directed its Political Department. On 8 April 1927, the academy invited Lu Xun to speak on ‘Literature in Times of Revolution’. Reflecting on the persecution of radical students he had witnessed in Beijing, Lu Xun lamented, ‘Literature, oh literature, you are a most useless thing. Only those without power talk about you; no one with real strength bothers to talk, they just murder people. Oppressed people who say a few things or write a few words will be killed’.


Käthe Kollwitz,

March of the Weavers

, from the series

A Weavers’ Revolt

, 1893–1897.


Given the situation of China at the time, Lu Xun asked a sobering rhetorical question: ‘What value does this literature have for the people, then?’ Yet he never ceased to write, making it his personal philosophy to ‘resist despair’. In

Wild Grass

, his collection of prose poems published that same year, he confronted hope and despair not as simple opposites but as illusions that could both paralyse action. Rather than retreat into a lost past or defer everything to a promised future, he insisted on grappling with the present through struggle and creation.

title: HPG announces the death of German internationalist Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte
content:
The People’s Defence Forces (HPG) announced the death of guerrilla fighter Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte. The internationalist, who was known within the Kurdish freedom movement as Baran Nûjiyan Salîma, was born in Germany to a German mother and a Portuguese father. According to the HPG, he joined the guerrilla ranks in 2019 and was active in areas including Gare, Metîna and Qandil. He lost his life in Qandil on August 6, 2025.


The ID information of the fallen internationalist guerrilla fighter is as follows:


Nom de Guerre: Baran Nûjiyan Salîma


First-Last Name: Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte


Birthplace: Germany


Mother's-Father's Name: Angela – Romeu


Date and Place of Death: 6 August 2025 – Qandil


The obituary published by the HPG Press Centre reads as follows:


“Our comrade Baran Nûjiyan was born in Germany into an internationalist family, to a Portuguese father and a German mother. Although he grew up in a family environment where different cultures came together, from a very young age he began to fundamentally question the structure of capitalist modernity, which turns human beings into objects, strips them of their spirit and alienates them from their own essence.


With great seriousness, our comrade devoted himself to his education and successfully completed his university studies. Afterwards, he worked in various fields and earned his own living. The experiences he gained under the difficult conditions of working life sharpened his understanding of the reality of the capitalist system, the exploitation of human labor, and the social relations that increasingly isolate the individual.


Baran recognized that, within this capitalist predicament that constrains both mind and spirit, human beings cannot remain true to their human essence, their ethical principles, and their pursuit of freedom. For this reason, from a young age he began searching for a radical alternative way of life.


In the heart of Europe, he established close ties with various political circles, groups, and movements that regarded themselves as opponents of the capitalist system, seeking answers to his existential questions among them. However, when he realized that these oppositional structures were far from producing a genuine revolutionary alternative, he continued his search without interruption.


In 2018, he became acquainted with the Kurdish Freedom Movement, in which he saw the most radical and genuine response to humanity’s universal quest for freedom. The more deeply he engaged with the ideological, psychological, and sociological analyses of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] and the paradigm of a women’s liberationist, ecological, and democratic society, the more strongly he felt that he had found the historical truth he had been searching for.


But Baran was not influenced by theoretical texts alone. The attitude, consistency in life, and determination of the Apoist militants he met in Europe also left a profound impression on him. Unlike other circles critical of the system, the Apoists lived according to their convictions, put the principles they advocated into practice in every moment of their lives, and were prepared to make the greatest sacrifices for the values of freedom they defended. For him, this attitude fundamentally distinguished them from all other groups.


In light of this, he immersed himself ever more deeply in the study of Leader Apo and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. The more he studied, understood, and drew closer to what he regarded as the truth, the more firmly he embraced the Apoist philosophy. Having attained a radical clarity intellectually, spiritually, and ethically, Comrade Baran became convinced that no idea could change the world as long as it remained purely theoretical.


Like the Apoists he had come to know, he believed that he too had to shoulder the full historical burden of the revolution. With this determination, he left behind all the individual opportunities offered by capitalist Europe, an academic career, and a life within the system, and turned toward the free and powerful mountains of Kurdistan.


In 2019, our comrade Baran committed his entire life to joining the guerrilla. He completed his initial guerrilla and militant training in Gare, one of the striking regions of the Medya Defense Zones. He began his revolutionary journey with a clear ideological consciousness.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Poll: Approval of Socialism at Record High as Capitalist Principles Hit New Lows
content:
Views of big business and free enterprise have declined significantly in the past decade.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

New polling finds that Americans approve of socialism more than ever, surpassing the 40 percent threshold for the first time in a Gallup survey as left-wing ideas and politicians surge in popularity.

According to Gallup polling conducted last month, 43 percent of Americans say they have a positive view of socialism. In Gallup’s 16 years of polling this question, the proportion of Americans saying as such has never before surpassed 40 percent. This is a four-point increase from 2025, when 39 percent said they had a positive view of the ideology — a slight increase from 36 percent in 2010.

Socialism is most popular among young people, with 57 percent of those aged 18 to 34 saying they view it positively.

Democrats’ view of socialism has steadily become more popular since 2010 — with those viewing it positively rising from 50 percent in 2010 to 65 percent in 2019 — and has stayed steady since then.

The big change in the past year, rather, has been driven by independents; in 2025, 37 percent of independents said they had a favorable view of socialism, lower than the average. That proportion rose by 8 points in the past year to 45 percent — now higher than the average among all Americans.

The polling comes as socialist figures like New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani have surged in popularity, with Mamdani enjoying strong approval ratings among New Yorkers and in national surveys. It adds to a slate of other polls showing surging popularity for the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and the democratic socialist ideology, with Quinnipiac finding recently that over a quarter of voters in the U.S. now consider themselves supporters of DSA.

The surge in popularity comes even as the Trump administration is waging a fierce campaign to suppress left-wing groups and progressive ideology through its National Security Presidential Memorandum-7 (NSPM-7) initiative, which broadly equates principles like “anti-Americanism” and “anti-capitalism” with “criminal” speech.

But the capitalist principles that have long dominated the U.S. political system are also dropping in popularity, Gallup found.

According to the latest poll, only 35 percent of Americans have a positive view of big business, down from a high of 58 percent in 2012. Those who favor “free enterprise,” or the idea that businesses should operate relatively free from government regulation, have dropped from a proportion of nearly 90 percent to 77 percent in this year’s polling.

Approval of capitalism has also declined slightly from historic highs. For much of the 2010s, roughly 60 percent of Americans said they view capitalism positively. But that has since declined to roughly 55 percent.

While the changes to these opinions have largely been driven by Democrats, Gallup notes that the latest uptick in socialism’s approval “comes entirely from political independents.” Among Democrats, only 65 percent say they approve of free enterprise — down from 88 percent in 2021. Meanwhile, opinions of big business have cratered entirely among Democrats, from 48 percent in 2016 to a mere 17 percent in the latest poll.

Looking to the next 25 years, we launched a special fundraising campaign. We still need to raise $16,000.

We are asking for your support at this juncture because we face greater threats than ever before in our organizational history. Trump and his MAGA allies are determined to control the information ecosystem, and movement-based organizations are subject to dangerous censorship and scrutiny.

author: Nahuel Lag
title: La trashumancia, forma de vida y producción milenaria
content:
Por Oscar Soto

*


La ganadería pastoril es una modalidad ancestral por la cual se cría el ganado haciendo uso de entornos variables a partir del desplazamiento de los animales y la gestión de las pasturas que lo abastecen. Esta dinámica de trabajo rural provee de medios a los campesinos que recorren pastizales alrededor del globo. Por eso, las familias se mueven en busca del recurso, y eso es bastante común, dado que las características de los espacios rurales de matorrales y estepas donde prospera el pastoreo son diversas. Las lluvias y nevadas estacionales son parte del sostenimiento de esas praderas infinitas. Podríamos decir que el pastoreo se vale de saberes tradicionales para sortear esos climas y ambientes sumamente hostiles donde la humedad y la altura son las únicas que pueden garantizar comida a las crías.


Unos 200 millones de personas en cerca de 100 países están abocados a esta labor. Es más, los pastores tradicionales, migratorios y transfronterizos en todo el planeta conservan los territorios de pastoreo y los utilizan para obtener carne, leche y otros alimentos, así como fibra, combustible y otros bienes. De hecho, el rol ecológico y social de esta práctica campesina e indígena es una de las razones que alientan la necesidad de su preservación. 


En términos generales, la cría de ganado es variable. Es posible definir, grosso modo

,

 una producción ganadera intensiva en la que los animales se concentran en un espacio determinado, alimentados por forrajes y suplementos determinados, la mayoría de las veces «importados» y con cierto automatismo. En tanto, en otro extremo, podemos identificar el pastoreo que proyecta en la labor humana un dispositivo central para su existencia, en espacios abiertos y naturales. 


Sobre este último, cabe mencionar lógicas distintas respecto de la propiedad y el acceso a la tierra, siendo los derechos privados exclusivos sobre la tierra, en general, menos comunes en las sociedades pastoriles. Es importante desanclar la idea de museo que objetiviza al mundo pastoril. Se puede ser pastor viviendo en un pueblo o en un paraje limítrofe con la ciudad. Sin embargo, lo cierto es que las características centrales del pastoreo apuntan a un modo de vida con lógicas y consecuencias diferentes a las de la ganadería intensiva.


Entre el conjunto de elementos que dan relieve a una práctica como esta se pueden mencionar cuatro aspectos centrales: la movilidad, que remite a la estacionalidad de la práctica haciendo del movimiento una forma más efectiva de adaptación y subsistencia; la territorialidad de pastizales: una gran porción de la superficie terrestre del planeta son pastizales, donde los medios de vida no pastoriles y la producción de alimentos suelen ser poco probables; la alta densidad nutricional de los alimentos que produce la actividad pastoril y la mejora de la biodiversidad que proporcionan. En su gran mayoría, los sistemas pastoriles emulan formas de vida silvestre reduciendo emisiones totales de gases de efecto invernadero y favoreciendo la producción baja en carbono.


El pastoralismo latinoamericano en zonas áridas es una actividad de larga data. En Argentina, pese a ser marginal, los animales suben a valles altos de unos 1.200 metros sobre el nivel del mar, en el caso de la Patagonia y el sur cuyano. La veranada –dirán los puesteros malargüinos–

es una forma de vida

 que los antecede en el sur de Mendoza, y es también una modalidad actual de puja por el territorio: la instrumentación de algunas leyes a mediados de los años 90 del siglo XX, tal el caso de la

Ley 6086 de Promoción y Arraigo de Puesteros en Zonas no Irrigadas

, no ha impedido la multiplicación de desalojos, lastimosamente vigentes en la actualidad.


En nuestro país, los sistemas de pastoreo extensivos han sido estrategias por las cuales el ganado se ha asemejado a un producto de riqueza social y cultural. De hecho, esta actividad involucra a más de 30.000 familias con distintos tipos de ganado, es decir, no solo chivos sino también vacunos, camélidos, ovinos, que se movilizan para obtener agua y pasturas, actividad que, además de cultural es económico-productiva. Para eso, es oportuno resaltar que —en lo relativo a los insumos que generan— solo el cálculo de ingresos del sector equivale a generar una riqueza de 300 millones de dólares cada año para el país, si miramos años regulares en términos económicos, sin tener en cuenta la megadevaluación de la moneda de principios de 2024.

content:
Number 113

Anarchy, acracy and the rule of the archons


Back in the EUSSR

Standing up to zionism

Acorninfo


1. Anarchy, acracy and the rule of the archons


by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here


Because the term “anarchy” is so often used pejoratively to mean chaos, and because some contemporary anarchists are 

far from freedom-loving

, [1] people often look for a less off-putting term to describe the future society they would like to see.


I personally took to using “

real anarchism

” [2] to mark my own position, while others call themselves “voluntaryists” and here in France “

libertaires

“.


One term that is sometimes used to replace “anarchy” is “acracy”, although I suspect the label “acracist” is a non-starter for obvious reasons!


“Anarchy” 

means

 the absence of any “archy”, any form of government or rule, such as monarchy or oligarchy, [3] while “acracy” 

means

 the absence of any “cracy”, which is to say any coercive authority, such as plutocracy or so-called democracy. [4]


The term 

acracia

 first appeared in the Iberian world and is 

believed

 to have been invented by the Catalan syndicalist Rafael Farga i Pellicer (1844-1890), who founded a journal with that name. [5]


It was used by the likes of 

Peter Kropotkin

 (1842-1921) [6] and 

Martin Buber

 (1878-1965) [7] as a synonym for anarchy, but is seen by some as conveying the idea of a society that is 

ordered

, albeit in a voluntary and consensual manner, and/or as one without any kind of 

exploitation

 rather than without any kind of 

authority

, as is the case with anarchy. [8]


In a 2018 

interview

, French economist and thinker Frédéric Lordon argued that, etymologically, anarchy means the absence of an absolute foundation (

ᾰ̓ρχή, ărkhḗ

) on which power’s commandments can be based.


He said that because its political meaning is, in fact, a society in which there is neither power nor domination, the word should really be replaced by acracy, which is precisely that absence of power and domination (

κρατία, kratía

). [9]


With due respect to Lordon, the question does not seem to be as clear as he suggests. While the root word 

krátos

 can indeed 

mean

 “power, might”, [10] it can also mean an “act of strength, act of valour”, with the postulated Proto-Indo-European stem 

kret

 

also

 indicating “intelligence”. [11]


So acracy could alternatively be interpreted as a society without strength, valour and intelligence.


I think we may already be there!


Meanwhile, the 

ărkhḗ

 opposed by anarchy can be 

traced back

 to the verb 

ắrkhō

 which means, in the transitive sense, “to lead; to rule; to govern; to command” and, in the intransitive sense, “to be ruler; to hold an archonship”. [12]


My ears pricked up at that last word!


Historically, an archon 

was

 a chief magistrate of ancient Athens and more generally “a person who claims the right to rule, or to exercise power or sovereign authority over other human beings” or simply “a ruler, head of state or other leader”. [13]


But in the gnostic tradition it identifies “a supernatural ruler of the cosmos”. William Thompson has 

described

 “the cry of the archon Ialdabaoth that he was the Lord of the Universe and that there was nothing beyond him”. [14]


Per Shapiro writes about the archons in his book 

The War on Life: How We Are Manipulated by Archontic Intelligence

, which I 

reviewed

 in May this year. [15]


He explains that the archontic influence in our world is a psychopathic one which refuses to respect natural boundaries and human taboos: “In this range, we find everything from incest, rape and perversions to various manifestations of hubris, such as genetically manipulated crops, laboratory-made life and the fission of the atomic nucleus”. [16]


He sees this phenomenon as taking its most extreme form with Yahweh, the god of the Old Testament, who for the gnostics was a pretender god, “an insane demon who has the delusion of having created the universe. A deranged being who is jealous of the living planet and wants to destroy it”. [17]


There is definitely an anarchic flavour to the message from Sophia (Mother Earth) to archon leader Ialdabaoth: “The authority you claim rests on deception, and when the deception fails, you perish”. [18]

author: Unknown
title: «Чёрное знамя»: дело беларусских анархо-партизан во внутренних сводках МВД
content:
Белорусский портал Tribunal.info опубликовал статью об анархистах партизанах из группы «Чёрное знамя».

Неудавшаяся революция 2020 года в Беларуси в медиа-сфере ассоциируется, прежде всего, с яркими и массовыми проявлениями мирного сопротивления. Многотысячные воскресные марши, бело-красно-белые флаги, женские цепи солидарности, дворовые инициативы и демонстративный отказ от насилия сформировали главный визуальный образ беларусской революции.

Однако, события 2020-го не ограничивались только мирными шествиями. Пока большинство противников режима наивно надеялись на мирные перемены, были те, кто, понимая сущность режима, смотрел прагматично. Они решили подойти к разрешению революционного вопроса путём прямого действия.

Речь о четырёх беларусских анархистах - Игоре Олиневиче, Сергее Романове, Дмитрии Резановиче и Дмитрии Дубовском. В прессе и материалах следствия их нередко называют «группой Олиневича» или просто «анархо-партизанами». Сами участники использовали название «Чёрное знамя» — в память об одноимённой анархистской организации, действовавшей на территории Российской империи в начале XX века.

Игорь Олиневич позднее пояснял: «Медиа окрестили нас «группой Олиневича» — или даже «бандой», — но этот ярлык не соответствует действительности. Мы называемся «Чёрное Знамя», в честь одноимённой федерации анархистов, боровшихся на этой земле за свободу ещё в царские времена».

Слева направо: Дмитрий Резанович, Дмитрий Дубовский, Игорь Олиневич, Сергей Романов

Игорь Олиневич — вчера ему исполнилось 43 года. Один из наиболее известных представителей беларусского анархистского движения. Получил техническое образование, в 2000-е годы включился в деятельность анархистских инициатив. Широкую известность приобрел после уголовного дела, связанного с серией акций прямого действия против государственных и коммерческих объектов.

В ноябре 2010 года его фактически похитили в Москве, после чего он оказался в застенках спецслужб РБ. В 2011 году Олиневича приговорили к восьми годам лишения свободы. Правозащитные организации признали его политическим заключённым. В 2015 году он вышел на свободу в результате т.н. «политической оттепели» и покинул Беларусь.

В заключении Игорь написал книгу «Еду в Магадан», основанную на тюремном опыте, в последствии изданную на многих языках мира. Осенью 2020 года он вновь оказался в Беларуси и, согласно материалам дела, стал одним из участников подпольной группы.

Дмитрий Дубовский родился в 1986 году в Солигорске. В анархистском движении с конца 2000-х годов. После возбуждения уголовных дел против беларусских анархистов в 2010 году покинул страну. На протяжении почти десяти лет находился в бегах, в том числе жил в России и Украине. Много путешествовал, о чем даже писал заметки, публиковавшиеся на сайте анархо-группы «Революционное действие».

Его имя фигурировало в материалах старых уголовных дел, связанных с нападениями на государственные и коммерческие объекты. После задержания в 2020 году эти эпизоды вновь стали предметом расследования.

Сергей Романов родился в 1994 году в Гомеле. Он самый молодой участник группы. К моменту событий 2020 года он уже имел опыт столкновения с правоохранительной системой режима. Ранее его судили по делу о незаконном обороте оружия. После освобождения оставался под превентивным надзором милиции. В материалах нового дела это обстоятельство использовалось как подтверждение того, что правоохранительные органы считали его подготовленным к подпольной деятельности и обращению с оружием.

В заключении Сергей проявил себя, как художник. Он активно создавал из подручных материалов зарисовки, которые передавались на волю. В частности, в рамках арт-проекта художника Владислава Бохана, с творчеством Сергея Романова смогли познакомиться зрители в Польше, Германии и Италии. Вероятно, из-за этого тюремная цензура перестала пропускать его работы.

Дмитрий Резанович родился в 1989 году. Связан с беларусским анархистским движением задолго до 2020 года. В сравнении с Олиневичем и Дубовским он значительно реже упоминается в СМИ. Тем не менее, следствие рассматривало Резановича, как полноправного участника группы, принимавшего участие в подготовке и проведении акций прямого действия. В ночь с 28 на 29 октября 2020 года его задержали вместе с Олиневичем, Романовым и Дубовским неподалёку от беларусско-украинской границы.

История «Чёрного знамени» уже неоднократно пересказывалась СМИ, заявлениях правозащитников, материалах суда и письмах самих заключённых. Однако, в этой статье мы ещё раз …

author: Unknown
title: La bombe n'est pas à nous : pourquoi les anarchistes reparlent de l'arme nucléaire
content:
Lyon, le 22 septembre. Alors que les États augmentent leurs budgets militaires et modernisent leurs arsenaux nucléaires, les services sociaux ferment et les militant·es sont poursuivi·es. Les groupes anarchistes et antimilitaristes lyonnais appellent à relier la lutte contre l'arme nucléaire aux conflits sociaux du quotidien — et à descendre dans la rue pour une marche contre l'arme nucléaire à la fin du mois.


Ce qui se passe


Les dépenses mondiales consacrées aux programmes nucléaires continuent d'augmenter, malgré les déclarations sur le désarmement. La France, qui fait partie des puissances nucléaires, conserve et modernise son arsenal — tout en réduisant le financement des hôpitaux, des écoles et du logement social. Les sites militaires restent des zones de secret et de répression : les manifestations y sont interdites, les militant·es poursuivi·es, l'information verrouillée.


Pourquoi ça nous concerne


Pour les anarchistes, l'arme nucléaire n'est pas une menace abstraite : c'est la forme ultime du pouvoir étatique. La décision de vie ou de mort de millions de personnes est prise par une poignée d'individus, tandis que les conséquences pèsent sur tout le monde. Chaque euro investi dans des ogives est un euro volé aux hôpitaux, aux écoles et au logement. La logique qui sous-tend l'arsenal nucléaire est la même que celle qui sous-tend le déblocage des camps, l'expulsion des squats et l'interdiction des grèves.


Nous ne pouvons pas «

 

faire sauter

 

» les arsenaux seuls. Mais nous pouvons dénoncer le militarisme, relier la lutte pour le logement et le climat à la critique de la machine de guerre, soutenir les initiatives antinucléaires — et construire des structures horizontales plutôt que des verticales de la peur.


Ce que nous pouvons faire


Venir aux actions antinucléaires et antiguerre — marches, piquets, blocages.


Soutenir les grèves et les mouvements sociaux — relier le militarisme à l'exploitation quotidienne.


Exiger la transparence des budgets militaires et dénoncer la propagande de la «

 

sécurité

 

».


Construire l'entraide et des réseaux de solidarité locaux.


📢 Marche contre l'arme nucléaire — Lyon


Samedi 17 octobre, 14h00


Rassemblement : Place Bellecour, Lyon


Itinéraire : Bellecour → Préfecture → Base aérienne 942 (Mont Verdun)


Nous ne descendons pas seulement contre la bombe. Nous descendons contre l'État qui dépense pour la guerre ce qui nous est volé. Contre le militarisme qui tue ici et maintenant — à Gaza, en Ukraine, au Soudan et dans nos rues. Contre le pouvoir qui décide à notre place si nous vivons ou non.


Revendications de la marche :


Réduction des dépenses militaires et réorientation des moyens vers les services sociaux.


Fermeture des sites nucléaires et des bases militaires sur le territoire.


Liberté de manifester et fin des poursuites contre les antimilitaristes.


Non à la guerre — ici comme partout.


Apportez : banderoles, pancartes, instruments de musique, de l'eau, de la solidarité. Bloc de solidarité avec les grèves sociales — rassemblement à 13h30 à Place Guichard (près de la sortie du métro, Lyon 3

e

).


Toutes les annonces, la logistique et le contact — sur Telegram : t.me/Stop_Bombe_Lyon


La bombe n'est pas à nous. Elle appartient au pouvoir qui ne nous a pas consulté·es. Venez — et montrez que la décision doit être la nôtre, pas la leur.


Note sur le lieu : la Base aérienne 942 (Mont Verdun) est un site militaire réel de la région lyonnaise, situé au nord de Lyon (Monts d'Or). Elle abrite un centre de commandement souterrain et joue un rôle dans la défense aérienne et la dissuasion. Elle a déjà été la cible d'actions directes de militant·es antinucléaires dans les années 1970, ce qui rend ce point d'arrivée symboliquement et historiquement cohérent.

This is something the military and Islamists in Sudan take pride in, but it is not a new step in the political reality. It is a recycled tactic that was previously used under Bashir’s regime through what was called the “National Dialogue.” The forces involved in that process were largely those allied with the military regime, while the revolutionary opposition did not make a significant difference.

Today, a politically oriented committee is being formed with a new propaganda framework. We see figures who once criticized the policies of the authorities, such as Dr. Mohamed Jalal Hashim, Al-Badri, and other intellectuals associated with the authorities, submitting to Al-Burhan’s policy, which aims to legitimize military rule. With the clear popular and imperial rejection of the Muslim Brotherhood as an active organization in Sudan, the army has sought to use forces that were previously considered part of the revolution to legitimize and institutionalize its upcoming policies.

The army’s position became clear in the statement by its Chief of Staff, Yasser Abdel Rahman Al-Atta, regarding Al-Burhan potentially running for four terms, equivalent to 20 years in power. At the same time, intellectuals close to the authorities are attempting to legitimize the old political system, while imperialist forces are trying to exploit revolutionary positions in accordance with their own agendas.

This leaves many revolutionaries uncertain about what political tactics can preserve the continuity of the revolution and complete its objectives: overthrowing the authoritarian regime and carrying out a social revolution.

The war was a means for the Islamists to return to power after the overwhelming popular rejection they had faced. Their systematic policies of revenge were clear, including in their own speeches, and this is widely acknowledged. But let us look at where they have reached today.

If the Sudanese people, during the December Revolution, rejected the Islamist regime by around 50 percent, then today that rejection may be closer to 80 percent, for several reasons.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: The political topography of anarchism
content:
Olaus Magnus, detail from

Carta Marina

, 1539


On old maps, it is common to see areas populated by mythological creatures, mermaids and Amazons, dragons and unicorns. The beings that inhabit the most remote and unexplored regions – those known or presumed to exist, but which are not yet understood – are depicted in great detail. The accounts of the few travellers who have reached these places are passed on by word of mouth and become distorted as they are retold; they are magnified and exaggerated, until from a narrative—presumed to be more or less reliable—an entire imaginary topography emerges, which serves at the same time to prove the existence of the mythical creatures whose territory it delineates. The circular reasoning is evident.  Dragons exist because they live there, at the edge of the world. This places them on the map. And they live there because they exist and must be somewhere. That is why they can feature in the depiction of the world.


Similarly, in the nineteenth century, with the fantastical excesses of the Middle Ages and the Renaissance now a thing of the past, Victorian explorers – salacot hats on their heads and rifles at the ready – set about methodically filling in the gaps that still remained on the maps. Particularly on the African continent, these blank spaces acted as magnets for the colonial powers, which meticulously mapped out the coastline, yet still knew nothing of what lay inland. This presented a seemingly irresistible invitation to minds imbued with evangelising and imperialist fantasies. After all, as Kipling reminds us, it is the white man’s burden. Something similar occurs in politics too. Most of us grow up virtually as functionally illiterate in this sphere, which is not normally considered necessary for adult education. Generally speaking, the education system and society as a whole take the view that a country’s inhabitants must acquire a body of knowledge that will equip them as future workers and productive members of society, but this does not extend to the civic skills essential for political engagement.


Be that as it may, the fact remains that current democratic models restrict effective participation to a caste of professionals, which means that the rest of the population need only possess a bare inkling of how the system works – just enough to cast a vote in a ballot box and accept that the direct management of their affairs is no longer, if you’ll pardon the redundancy, their concern. But it seems that the tendency to invent what one does not know is a constant feature of human psychology. Just like the monsters on medieval maps, the political landscape is riddled with dark and unknown zones – grey areas of which one usually has only vague notions – from which a fantastical image is constructed that replaces more detailed knowledge and makes the latter seem unnecessary. On the basis of these vague notions, the political landscape is divided up, associating certain elements of the ideological spectrum with distant cardinal points and populating it with the corresponding mythological creatures that inhabit it. Evidently, these beings are not a spontaneous product of the imagination, but are often supplied by interested parties, through channels suited to the level of representation being sought. Cinema, television and, above all, the mainstream media supplant formal political education (in the broadest sense), and disseminate prejudices and preconceived images across a mental map that is intuited rather than drawn. Thus, most people (though not all) know that National Socialism lies somewhere to the right (the east?) of the conservatives, but not exactly why, or what the differences between them are. Similarly, the Marxist left lies to the west, in a zone populated by enemies of private property, although nobody knows how they got there, or why. And the anarchists? That’s where the dragons are…


If our knowledge of, shall we say, conventional political options is generally sketchy and vague, our understanding of those that transcend the conventions of the civic common sense of an era enters the realm of the nebulous. We find ourselves on fertile ground for the mythical. Any notion that goes beyond the parameters accepted as unquestionable in the foundations of the current democratic system is perceived as nonsense, difficult to take on board or even to conceive of as possible. Everyone knows that someone has to be in charge, and if not, things descend into …

author: Paul Tiyambe Zeleza
title: The Historiographical Legacy of B.A. Ogot and His Generation
content:
Good evening, colleagues, and the Governor of Kisumu County, Professor Anyang Nyong’o! It is truly a pleasure for me to join you in this commemoration of the towering historian, scholar, and public intellectual, Bethwell Alan Ogot. I believe I speak on behalf of all of us in extending our deep gratitude to the Council for the Development of Social Science Research in Africa (CODESRIA) and the Department of History at Kenyatta University for organizing this important conference. Personally, my appreciation extends to that rarity of experiences, the opportunity to meet several of my former students at Kenyatta University between 1984 and 1989 who have become distinguished academics and administrators. It’s a befitting tribute to our intellectual father, grandfather, quickly becoming a great-grandfather, who was raised and spent his last years and is buried in nearby Yala, that this conference is being held in his home city of Kisumu, under the transformative leadership of one of Kenya’s leading scholars and public intellectuals, Governor Peter Anyang Nyong’o.


Introduction


Let me begin by noting that I last visited Kisumu in January 2019 to join Professor Ogot as he celebrated his 90th birthday. I first visited this city nearly forty years earlier, in 1980, when I was doing research for my doctoral dissertation on Kenyan economic and labor history, and spent time at this venue, the Tom Mboya Labor College. Professor Ogot had a lot to do with my interest in Kenyan history. My engagement with him goes back to 1976 when he served as external examiner at the University of Malawi.


Years later, he would proudly tell audiences at events where both of us were present that I owed my degree with distinction to him! In our classes on East African history, we had read Ogot’s books, and it was an indescribable honor and privilege to meet him in person. I was deeply touched and humbled when he asked to meet the student who had received the distinction, and he prevailed upon the department to bring me to the cottage along Lake Malawi, where the department took him to show their gratitude for bestowing the department with the distinction of his presence. .


That was the beginning of a lifelong mentoring and intellectual relationship that changed the trajectory of my personal and professional life, on which I will say more later.


When Professor Ogot passed away in January 2025, there was an avalanche of tributes in the popular and academic media celebrating his life and immense scholarly contributions. It is befitting that we are gathered here to remember and celebrate him as a towering historian and intellectual polymath.


Ogot belongs to an exceptional generation of the pioneering architects of the African academy in its multifaceted epistemic and institutional dimensions. These were extraordinary individuals, inspired by the fierce historical and humanistic urgency and imperatives of African nationalism: decolonization, nation-building, regional integration, development, and democracy. They were driven by the audacity, passion, and commitment to remaking the production, dissemination, and consumption of knowledge in, and for, Africa and the world.


They were scholar-activists who transformed existing disciplines and founded new ones, who built interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary paradigms, perspectives and practices, who believed in the power of education as a public good and engine of development, who relished their role as rigorous academics and public intellectuals, who jealously guarded academic freedom and the intelligentsia as the conscience of their new nation-states.


Their lives were large, complex, and multilayered. The trajectory of Ogot’s career is quite emblematic of his peers, born between the third and fourth decades of the twentieth century in the immediate aftermath of the formation of the colonial conquest state, whose ideologues deluded themselves would last for centuries, if not millennia, only to collapse spectacularly as Ogot and his peers matured into adulthood. I would like to explore, rather briefly given the limitations of time, five aspects of Professor Ogot’s remarkable life and legacy: Ogot the man, the historian, the institution builder, the public figure, and the mentor. Let me add that today we’ve heard much about many of these themes. My excuse for revisiting them is that I came a long way, and I have to justify my ticket!


Ogot the Man


Biographical reflections and commemorations …

author: Nada Elia
title: Women and Youth Are at the Forefront of the Struggle for Palestinian Liberation
content:
They follow in the footsteps of Palestinian women and children who have resisted colonialism in the past century.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

I grew up in a household of women and children that, as my sisters and I matured, eventually became a household of only women. My father was frequently gone on long overseas business trips before his untimely death when I was seven. I often wonder if this is the reason the expression “women and children” strikes me as essentially flawed: It suggests that women and children are the more vulnerable members of society, rather than its resilient survivors. It infantilizes women by grouping them with children, rather than adult men.

In the context of a national struggle, it strips women of agency, as if such agency can only manifest through armed revolt. In a military context, the expression “women and children” — or “womenandchildren,” to use the term coined by antimilitary feminist scholar Cynthia Enloe — presumes that women and children never take up arms or participate in resistance, even as we see such actions occurring in numerous struggles around the world. And in listing casualties, it implies that men’s deaths and injuries are less tragic, less mournable.

In the case of Palestine, women and youth have led, and continue to lead, some of the most transformative efforts and initiatives in our people’s quest for justice — that is, our resistance first to imperialism, then to settler colonialism and apartheid. They have not been spared Israel’s violence, just for being women, or children, and many have been and remain at the forefront of popular resistance to Zionism’s ultimate aim of eliminating all Palestinians. While this may have become more obvious during Israel’s accelerated genocidal assault on Gaza following Hamas’s October 7, 2023, attacks, it had always been clear to anyone not deliberately looking away.

From a number of uprisings over the past century in Palestine, it is obvious that youth, “the children,” are not just among the leaders; they are the more effective, more transformational leaders. Unfettered by traditions and social norms they do not relate to, they engage in novel forms of organizing, seeking the complete abolition of oppressive systems, rather than their reversal. And women, in their capacity as autonomous adults, rather than merely as wives and mothers, have consistently resisted both the imperial ideology targeting their country, and the military assaults that accompanied it. They did so while providing men, as well as the youth and children, the moral, emotional, and practical support the Palestinian people need in order to persist. This was perhaps most evident on a global scale during the 1987–93 Intifada, when women organized most of the popular committees tending to the educational, nutritional, and health needs of Palestinians resisting Israel’s clampdown, as youth took to the streets daily to express their rejection of Israel’s decades-long oppressive rule. These defenseless children hurled rocks at armored tanks, fully aware of the hefty price they would pay for their defiant act, because they knew that risking limb and life is preferable to living without freedom and dignity.

Women’s and children’s agency is enacted daily in the courage of girls such as Janna Jihad, who was dubbed “the world’s youngest journalist” when she started documenting Israel’s crimes at a mere seven years of age. Jihad started recording Israel’s attacks using her mother’s cell phone, posting her recordings far and wide on social media. She has repeatedly said that her camera is her weapon of choice. Jihad is the cousin of Ahed Tamimi, the “lioness” who has confronted heavily armed Israeli soldiers determined to take over her village lands since she was a toddler. Israel imprisoned Tamimi for eight months when she was sixteen; she used the time behind bars to read up on international law, later enrolling in college planning to go to law school, so as to hold Israel accountable for its violations. “I am a freedom fighter. So I will not be the victim,” she told journalists upon her release.

Palestinian children’s agency was also clear in the 2022 uprising of rebellious youth standing up to Israel’s might. Ibrahim al-Nabulsi, dubbed “the Lion of Nablus,” was eighteen when he was brutally assassinated by the Israeli Occupation Forces. Following his martyrdom, his mother, Huda al-Nabulsi …

author: ROAPE
title: Food security or seed capture? The colonial potato and Africa’s seed wars
content:
It all begins with a potato. Not the kind that nourishes a nation in textbook stories, but a colonial potato. This potato was shipped, tested, rationed, pushed through mission gardens and military supply lines, and ultimately sold as progress. Tracing that potato across Nigeria’s highlands leads to today’s disputes over seed, debt, law, and who decides what African farmers cultivate. 


Seeds are not just seeds. They carry memory, labour, taste, law, power, and often, debt.

The colonial potato scheme in Nigeria

 is significant because it shows how dependency on seeds can develop even before it is codified in law. Nowadays, discussions about seed sovereignty in Africa often centre on patents, plant breeders’ rights, certified seed laws, and agribusiness. However, colonial Nigeria reveals an older method of control: emergency.       


In the 1930s and 1940s, British officials transformed the

Jos and Mambila Plateaus

 into experimental sites for growing potatos. Initially, the scheme was small and awkward, driven by European miners, missionaries, and colonial officers seeking familiar food. Then, the Second World War (1939-1945) changed everything. Supply routes were disrupted, troops needed food, and Nigerian highland farmers were forcibly integrated into a larger imperial food plan. An agricultural experiment became part of the British empire’s war effort.


An anthropological base map of Plateau Province reproduced from C.G. Ames, The Gazetteers of Plateau Province, 1932 (Copy in Nigerian National Archives, Kaduna)


The highlands were ideal for the crop. Potatos thrive in cooler conditions, and Jos and Mambila provided the climate colonial agronomists desired. However, these areas were not empty spaces waiting for improvement. They were inhabited, farmed, and politically complex societies with their own crops, markets, and knowledge systems.


Colonial rule altered the dynamics in these regions. Tin mining on the Jos Plateau attracted workers, administrators, and settlers. Demand for European foods increased. Potatos, once a garden crop for expatriates and mission stations, began to seem valuable to the colonial state.


Starting in the 1930s, British

officials based in Nigeria began importing seed potatos from Ireland, Britain, Europe, South Africa, the Canary Islands, and the United States.

 Mission stations cultivated the potatos. District heads distributed the seed. Farmers cautiously tried the crop, incorporating it into local routines where it made sense while rejecting it when it didn’t. The potato became a means of power.


This did not mean that older crops and seed systems disappeared. There was no formal ban, and local farmers continued to grow, save, and exchange seed in various ways. The scheme worked in subtler ways: it altered the rewards. Access to land, labour, credit, official support, and markets began to favour the colonial crop. Imported seed was seen as improved, while farmer-saved seed and local knowledge were pushed to the sidelines. Over time, diverse and adaptable seed systems were narrowed, though not completely erased, by a supply chain prioritising mines, mission stations, military demands, and imperial markets.


Before the Second World War, the scheme was no great success. Some farmers thought potatos were poisonous. Others saw no reason to cultivate a crop with a limited, European-dominated market. A 1937 attempt to sell imported ‘Great Scott’ seed potatos to the Jos Native Authority ended poorly: half went unsold, the remainder was given away, and the scheme lost money.


War transformed failure into urgency. The empire needed food close to military outposts. It aimed to save cargo space and lessen reliance on disrupted shipping routes. Suddenly, potatos on the Mambila and Jos Plateau became crucial.


The war economy and the creation of dependency


Production surged from around

90 tons at the beginning of the war in 1939 to about 1,200 tons by 1943. Seed stores and experimental stations emerged throughout Kagoro, Zonkwa, Kurmin Biri, and Riyom

. Colonial science advanced rapidly, too: London-based Kew scientists devised ways to transport sprouting ‘eyes’ of potatos instead of whole tubers, facilitating a steady supply from outside.


Wartime officials did not establish an independent Nigerian seed system; they created a supply chain. Farmers were encouraged to boost production. Yet, this authority remained elsewhere: seed, disease control, imports, and markets remained …
