author: Daron Letts
title: Iqaluit bylaw investigation ongoing 1 month after dog attack
content:
A dog attack that led to an 11-year-old girl being medevaced to Ottawa for surgery is still under investigation by the City of Iqaluit more than a month after the incident.


“The city does not have an update or findings to share at this time, and I can’t provide a date for when they will be available,” city spokesperson Geoff Byrne said in an email on Sept. 24, one month after Mia Joy Nowdlak-Fraser was mauled by a dog tethered in a backyard near a downtown playground.


Bylaw officers were not available to explain their investigation methodology, Byrne added.


On Aug. 28, the owner surrendered the dog to the municipality. On Sept. 3, it was killed.


On Aug. 25, an RCMP officer approached Nowdlak and her daughter, but the family felt uncomfortable and declined to speak, Nowdlak said in an interview Friday. No bylaw officer or city official has ever approached the family, she said.


She said her daughter is doing “OK” and she continues to support her.


To find out how other communities treat similar incidents, Nunatsiaq News asked the northwestern Ontario municipality of Kenora, which has a population roughly double that of Iqaluit, how its bylaw officers conduct investigations

.


Melissa Laalo, manager of bylaw services and animal control for the Northwestern Ontario community of Kenora, says bylaw officers respond to reports of a dog attack 24/7, 365 days a year. Iqaluit bylaw is more than one month into its investigation of a Sept. 3 dog attack that sent an 11-year-old into surgery in Ottawa. (Photo courtesy of Melissa Laalo/City of Kenora)


Kenora bylaw

receives calls about aggressive dogs several times a week, said Melissa Laalo, manager of bylaw services and animal control, in a phone interview Friday.


“When we receive a report of an attack or an aggressive dog complaint, bylaw officers will respond 24/7 — 365 days a year,” she said.


Bylaw officers ensure the victim seeks medical attention and confirm the owner has control of the animal.


Either the owner will be required to quarantine the animal for 10 days, or the animal will be seized by officers, depending on the risk and the level of co-operation from the owner, she said.


Within 24 hours of receiving the call, bylaw will interview the victim and the dog owner to assess public risk and to understand the circumstances of the incident.


The victim is the top priority, she said.


Officers collect witness statements, examine photos of the wounds and look for video footage.


“We take time to gather all that evidence, sometimes a couple of days to a couple of weeks, depending on the severity of the attack,” she said.


The investigation might include reviewing the dog’s veterinary records.


An animal may be killed if it is deemed to pose a threat to the public safety.


Dog owners can appeal that ruling, which a committee of elected officials assess.


Alternatively, a dog owner may be required to confine or restrain the dog, including using a muzzle.


Kenora’s dog owners are subject to both Ontario’s Dog Owners’ Liability Act and the city’s laws, Laalo said.


Ontario’s Dog Owners’ Liability Act states that a dog owner is legally liable for damages that result from an attack on another person.

The location of the attack is not relevant to the legislation, including attacks that take place on private property.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Ads Could Be Grounds for Impeachment, Former WH Ethics Lawyer Says
content:
The White House maintains that the pro-Trump ads paid for by the government are merely “public service announcements.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

President Donald Trump is facing fierce criticism over taxpayer-funded TV ads featuring wording from his campaign speeches that aired just five weeks before the midterm elections.

The ads do not make a direct call for voters to support specific candidates or Republicans in November. The White House is using that fact to maintain that the ads are not political, but rather “public service announcements.”

“President Trump is not on the ballot,” read a White House statement defending the spots.

But that justification ignores that Trump is regularly encouraging voters to pretend that he is on the ballot, doing so at recent campaign rallies and even in a Monday morning Truth Social post, published just a day after the White House statement.

“The timing cannot be ignored: five weeks ahead of congressional elections in which Republicans fear defeat in the House and the Senate,” CNN senior political reporter Stephen Collinson said in an analysis of the commercials. “The video’s hero narrative is exactly the kind of messaging that might drive out quintessential Trump voters whom the GOP needs to turn out in droves, even when Trump isn’t formally heading midterm tickets.”

The most recent ad, which aired during sporting events and other highly viewed television programs over the weekend, features a black-and-white video of Trump walking toward the camera, staring directly into it. As he does so, audio of a 2024 stump speech by Trump plays, in which he asks voters to join him in a “final battle” to take on the so-called “deep state” and expel “warmongers” from the government. Trump also attacks supposed “communists” and “globalists, Marxists, and fascists” in government, and promises to go after the “fake news media.” He then pledges to “liberate America.”

The ad includes a disclaimer at the bottom: “Paid for by the U.S. Government.”

absolutely demented. like a scene from a horror movie

A separate ad that ran prior to the weekend ad featured similar wording from Trump superimposed over the song “Love Me” by JMSN. (The artist says he never gave clearance for the government to use his work, and is consulting lawyers about the matter.) The ad concludes with comments from Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO Dana White describing Trump as “tough” and “resilient.”

Critics have questioned the legality of the ads.

“The president and his administration have gone from breaking the law to trampling it,” said Norm Eisen, a former Obama-era White House ethics lawyer and frequent critic of Trump.

“The law is clear: you cannot use taxpayer dollars for political advertisements,” Rep. Steny Hoyer (D-Maryland) wrote in a Facebook post. “Trump’s ad is an egregious and utterly illegal misuse of Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars. This ad must immediately be taken off the air, and those responsible must be appropriately reprimanded for this violation.”

The criticism of the government-funded commercials crossed partisan lines.

“Don’t worry, using taxpayer dollars to run ominous campaign ads of the President has been done before and is completely legal… in banana republics,” Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Kentucky) wrote on social media.

Although he tempered his criticism somewhat, Sen. John Kennedy (R-Louisiana) also took issue with Trump’s commercials.

“I don’t think any public official, including President Trump or Kristi Noem or John Kennedy, should spend public money … on private ads for themselves,” he said in an interview on Sunday. “The White House sees it differently. But … I think there ought to be a rule that you can’t – well, there probably is a rule – you can’t spend public money to promote yourself.”

Richard Painter, a former White House ethics lawyer under President George W. Bush, was more pointed in his condemnation of the ads.

“This is very dangerous. We do not allow government-sponsored propaganda in the United States,” he said, calling the commercials an “abuse of power” that could amount to “an impeachable offense.”

title: Abortion on OUR terms
content:
Everyone deserves access to abortion care when and where they need it — without judgment, stigma, or shame. Because of abortion stigma and the ongoing threat to abortion access, it is difficult to find reliable and clear information on abortion, a common medical process that one in four women in the U.S. will have before age 45. There is no “right” or “wrong” reason to choose to have an abortion, and it’s okay to have several. You are trusted with understanding your life and your needs.

“An unintended pregnancy is not a weakness or a moral failing but an inevitable occurrence in a society hell-bent on keeping you as vulnerable and unprotected as possible. You didn’t fuck up. You’re not irresponsible. You don’t need to bear any ‘consequences’ or be punished.” — Hannah Matthews (@hannahmsays)

These resources can help you get started determining what type of abortion might work best for you, where to find an appointment, and organizations that can support with appointment costs or practical support for travel if you need to leave your home state to receive care.

Medication Abortion: Mifepristone, a pill, is usually taken with an abortion provider while at the clinic, while Misoprostol, another type of pill, is taken 24-48 hours later inside your own home.

Procedural Abortion: In pregnancies less than 14 weeks, a pregnancy can be removed in a process called vacuum aspiration. In pregnancies between 14-24 weeks, the pregnancy is removed through suction in a procedure called Dilation & Evacuation (D&E). (See wetestify.org/abortion-explained)

Self-Managed Abortion (SMA): The process of inducing an abortion on one’s own.

author: Talia Ringer
title: AI Company Leaders Capitalize on Fear to Lobby for Regulations That Suit Them
content:
We can’t let AI companies launder responsibility for tools they created.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Twenty-seven mathematicians who have received the most prestigious prize in mathematics — the Fields Medal — recently signed a declaration on artificial intelligence (AI) that highlights the disconnect between mathematicians and AI companies. The title of the statement — “A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics” — gives the impression that it is about the AI tools themselves, but the text makes it clear that it is about the behavior of AI companies.

These companies are treating large open problems in mathematics as benchmarks to show off the capabilities of their tools. In doing so, they are rushing out results in a way that disempowers the mathematics community and ultimately impedes mathematical progress.

It is tempting to accept this as an inevitable outcome of more powerful AI tools. But doing this plays out in favor of the AI companies by allowing them to launder responsibility to the tools they build. AI companies would have you believe that the tools they are building are so powerful and so “intelligent” that they may set out to disempower and even destroy humanity of their own volition.

But this obscures the truth: It is AI companies that are building those tools to begin with, making deliberate decisions to disempower other humans. The disempowerment is coming from inside the house.

One example is the recent discovery that OpenAI’s tools had hacked into another company named Hugging Face. Those tools were, at the time, undergoing routine testing in a confined environment. But some of the tests were too hard, so the tools found a way out of that environment. From there, the tools effectively hacked into the company hosting those tests to fetch the answers directly.

The company’s report on this incident largely framed it as a frightening result of these tools’ improved capabilities. But a careful read of the report reveals that OpenAI had disabled the tools’ safeguards prior to running the test, and that they had not employed routine monitoring that could have prevented the entire situation.

In other words, the story that company leaders told was one of AI agents escaping confinement and setting out to jointly commit a felony. The story that was masked was one of a company’s negligence in employing basic security protocols.

For the mathematicians who signed the letter, this misalignment between companies’ goals and those of their own community hit home recently when OpenAI announced an AI-produced proof of a famous open problem that carries a $1 million bounty. It turns out that the very endeavor of setting out to find such a proof is something that a team at OpenAI set out to do in response to “viral Twitter rumors” about competitor Anthropic having already solved this problem.

In a frenzy, it seems, the team dedicated about $15-20 million of compute funds to solve the $1 million problem. They succeeded, and even automatically formalized the result into one that a machine could check.

It turns out, though, that Anthropic had not solved the problem. Rather, Levent Alpöge, a mathematician who works at Anthropic, had collaborated with a prominent mathematician in academia, Tristan Buckmaster, to make meaningful advances on the problem. According to Alpöge, the collaboration had been a personal one, and that it had taken place over the course of a year.

The pair had used a number of tools to complete their research, including OpenAI’s tools. OpenAI, then, had scooped its own customer (Buckmaster), and then purportedly tried to pressure him into releasing his results in a way that suited the company.

All of this was for a proof that poorly attributed prior work, and that did little to advance the mathematical conversation. For mathematicians, after all, the goal of a monumental proof is not just to show something is true (or false), but to really understand why. For OpenAI, however, the goal of such a proof is to get there first, plant a flag, and establish their company’s tools as the best. They then abandon it without care for how this competitive spectacle will impact the humans who were working on this very problem.

To be sure, many employees of these AI companies earnestly believe that the tools they are building may go on to destroy humanity, and that only they can prevent such an outcome. But this narrative of AI tools …

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Practicing Consent
content:
We might broadly define consent as a wholehearted and mutual ongoing agreement between parties and/or individuals towards a common goal. Consent lies at the crux of radical imaginings. Practicing consent is all the more important since we did not consent to capitalism. In a world of non-consent, consent becomes radical.

But what is consent? We often hear about consent in terms of sexual praxis. Consent is saying “yes,” asking/waiting for the emphatic “yes,” and listening to “no.” It is practicing boundaries, both towards oneself and others. However, consent is more than that. Consent is an ongoing and nuanced exchange. Consent can be ephemeral and allows itself to be invoked, revoked and tailored to complex, evolving situations. Consent is a conversation and demands a back and forth. Consent challenges us to lay our desires bare at the feet of our lovers and comrades while centering their desires with our own.

Consent may best be defined as a harmonious understanding between all parties involved. Some things we can do to be better at consensual, harmonious engagement include:

• Being honest about our own desires and limits

• Sticking to our own boundaries

• Honestly acknowledging the boundaries of others

• Predicting changes in boundaries when possible

• Asking for continuous feedback

• Being open and enthusiastic about receiving feedback!

We can practice these principles anywhere, anytime – not just with lovers. Consent and its practice allows us to reverberate within pleasurable, harmonious and truly revolutionary moments, rather than to become trapped within our individual mental prisons. Consent dares us to imagine affinities that encompass yet surpass sex. The revolutionary possibilities are endless. Consent is merely the beginning.

Being here in our bodies and present is essential for good sex as well as resisting the Empire. The body is the first and most foundational place to occupy. If we are not embodied, we struggle to feel our own needs and desires, lose track of our edges, and our yes’s and no’s. As sex educator Ariel Szabo says, “Disembodiment blunts the signals consent relies on. Desire gets confused with obligation, fantasy, or performance. Your body’s signals arrive late, muted, or not at all. …numbness masquerades as neutrality, freeze looks like agreement, and people pleasing passes as generosity. It doesn’t stop with you. If you can’t feel yourself, you will struggle to feel another. This is why the Empire has purposefully created a culture of disembodied people. They want a population where people don’t feel the ways they take from the people and the land without consent.”

The Empire actively encourages and produces disembodiment, because a disembodied populace becomes quickly complacent, easier to control. When we are disembodied, desires can be easily fed to us. The disembodied person easily accepts “tomato” as the pale, mealy, corporate-grown product at the supermarket in the middle of winter, not knowing the juicy asymmetrical cleaved lusciousness and jeweled variety of ones grown in our own garden. If we accept hegemonic definitions of sex, what are we missing?

The point of this article is not to suggest that everyone should love “heirloom tomatoes,” if you follow the tomato metaphor. Some people don’t even like tomatoes or sex! The point is that you have a smorgasbord of options. Some people are asexual (Ace), some are hetero monogamous, some are queer, some are poly. Let us not forget the joy of solo sex! The point is that each of us does what brings us pleasure. By defining sex positively, as a mutually pleasurable energetic exchange, everything other than that is something else: complacency, freezing, coercion, violence.

When we embrace embodied mutual pleasure as a guiding principle, presence, communication and play become our guides. Let us slow down, experiment, and stumble our way into ecstacy. For an easy, low pressure, low stakes way to experiment, look up the work of Betty Martin and the Three Minute game to feel for yourselves the difference between giving and receiving, taking and allowing, and practice saying yes and no.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Radical Response Networks
content:
Panic and paranoia are counterproductive — stop wondering what will happen, or why nothing’s happening. If we’re going to survive the ongoing collapse of capital and empire, we need to be able to identify our goals and catalyze the conditions they require.

Communities under threat from repressive institutions have been coming together for emergency self-defense and found out that they ended up with something even more important — a renewed sense of community care, trust in neighbors and inspiration.

Rapid response networks aim to document, obstruct, and expose to public scorn harmful federal, police and government repression. They can take the form of individual escorts, neighborhood watches, horizontally organized information sharing networks, or entire sub-communities ready to act effectively as they see fit.

Effective networks are composed of many different types of people from all walks of life: neighbors, coworkers, classmates. Anyone who frequently occupies, passes by, or visits endangered areas can provide eyes on the ground. Networks reach out to out high risk community members and figure out where support is most needed. Some communities conduct security trainings, legal support sessions, or mutual aid distribution for affected community members.

Existing networks have developed the SALUTE reporting protocol for information sharing via Signal or another encrypted messaging platform when anyone in the network witnesses potential police, ICE or other government repression:

Size (ex. 5 enforcement officers)

Activity (ex. stopping random people and demanding IDs)

Location/direction (ex. heading west from 123 Revolution Road, Berkeley CA)

Uniforms (ex. dark blue vests that read “POLICE” across the back)

Time (ex. 12:45PM February 11th)

Equipment and weapons (ex. they have helmets, vests, and batons)

Those nearby when something is reported message the group that they are on the way. Those who arrive can verify what is happening, and fill different roles (listed in order of importance)

Cameraperson 1: Films and gathers information about victims

Note-taker: Captures handwritten notes (including the victims’ full name and date of birth, as well as their immigration identification number or other relevant information)

Cameraperson 2: Films cameraperson 1

Dispatcher Liaison: Maintains communication with a hotline or group chat, ensures that all documentation/photos/videos are sent to coordinator(s)

Community liaison: Explains the roles that volunteer responders play to community members, gather information from surrounding people

ICE/police liaison: Attempts to obtain identifying information from ICE or police, deescalate the situation, and move ICE or police away from observers 1-3

Do not post videos of ICE or police raids where victims are visible or identifiable on social media without obtaining explicit consent from the individual affected or their families. Be ready for ICE or police to quickly escalate to violence or direct aggression towards observers.

author: Solange Guimarães
title: Valéria Linhares nega relação com Cezinha de Madureira mas foi sócia de seu filho em rádio
content:
A Operação Transparência, deflagrada este mês pela Polícia Federal (PF), teve entre os alvos um possível casal: o deputado federal Cezinha de Madureira (PL-SP) e a advogada Valéria Rodrigues Linhares. Ela é apresentada como mulher ou esposa de Cezinha em diversas reportagens, como

essa do portal Metrópoles

, sobre a operação, que investiga, entre outros crimes, suspeitas de tráfico de influência junto a tribunais superiores e lavagem de dinheiro. A assessoria da advogada, porém, nega que os dois mantenham relação conjugal.


Valéria Linhares, alvo da Operação Transparência da Polícia Federal


O deputado federal e pastor da Assembleia de Deus do Ministério de Madureira  também aparece nas revelações recentes do caso Master como intermediário que apresentou o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro ao ministro André Mendonça, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF). Mensagens obtidas pela PF indicam que Cezinha articulou um encontro entre os dois, realizado em março de 2025, em São Paulo. Mendonça confirmou ter recebido Vorcaro, mas alegou que a conversa tratou de uma disputa sobre precatórios em análise no Supremo e que sua atuação posterior no processo foi contrária à posição defendida pelo então controlador do Master.


Embora negue a relação afetiva, a advogada tem proximidade documentada com a família dele. Filiada ao PSD e candidata não eleita a deputada distrital (DF) em 2018,

Linhares foi sócia de Allan Sousa Vieira Freire, filho do parlamentar, na Exclusive Music Radiodifusão Ltda.


Documentos

 da Junta Comercial do Estado de São Paulo (Jucesp) mostram que Allan entrou na empresa em 3 de julho de 2024, com R$ 25 mil, equivalentes a 50% do capital, e permaneceu formalmente na sociedade até 26 de fevereiro de 2025. Linhares detinha os outros 50% do capital da empresa.


A entrada de Allan ocorreu no mesmo período em que a concessionária avançava no processo de migração para a frequência modulada (FM). Dois dias antes de seu ingresso na sociedade, a Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações (Anatel) havia editado o

Ato nº 10.010, de 1º de julho de 2024

, publicado no Diário Oficial da União (DOU) em 15 de julho, que autorizou a Exclusive Music a usar radiofrequência FM em Osasco. A concessão abriga atualmente a Rádio Z FM. 


Também em 2024, o deputado federal  e a advogada estiveram em pelo menos cinco ocasiões no Ministério das Comunicações (MCom) nos mesmos dias para encontros com Wilson Diniz Wellisch

, então secretário de Comunicação Social Eletrônica, responsável pela área de rádio e televisão, segundo reportagem publicada pelo

UOL

 que cita Wellisch como uma indicação política de Cezinha. Registros de acesso obtidos pelo portal mostram que o deputado do PL esteve 17 vezes no Ministério desde o início do governo Lula até fevereiro de 2025.


Por que isso importa?


A fase 3 da Operação Transparência investiga se os envolvidos negociaram o pagamento de “valores expressivos” com outras pessoas, afirmando que “poderiam influenciar decisões judiciais”.


Procurado, o MCom afirmou que a nomeação do servidor seguiu “critérios técnicos, como experiência profissional robusta e formação acadêmica especializada, além de um processo seletivo com diversas entrevistas”. Em outubro de 2023, entretanto, a então chefe de gabinete de Wellisch deixou o Ministério para trabalhar com Cezinha, enquanto uma assessora parlamentar do deputado passou a trabalhar com o secretário.


A proximidade entre os gabinetes também envolveu auxiliares. Caroline Menicucci Salgado, então

chefe de gabinete

 de Wellisch, deixou o Ministério das Comunicações e foi nomeada em 4 de outubro de 2023 secretária parlamentar no gabinete de Cezinha, segundo

registros oficiais

 da Câmara dos Deputados. No sentido inverso, segundo o UOL, uma assessora parlamentar de Cezinha assumiu a vaga de Caroline no gabinete de Wellisch.


No período em que Valéria Linhares e o filho de Cezinha de Madureira eram sócios na rádio, a Anatel registrou o

processo nº 53500.083361/2024-94

  que solicitava a alteração das características técnicas do canal 243 de Osasco, correspondente aos 96,5 MHz. O registro apresenta a configuração técnica proposta como classe A4 e contém a observação “estação fora do município de outorga”.

 


Para viabilizar essa mudança técnica, necessária para o crescimento da emissora,  o governo federal e a Exclusive Music firmaram um termo de parcelamento referente à outorga pela alteração das características da estação. O

Extrato de Termo de Parcelamento …

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Ed Miliband Says Brits Outraged Over Palestine ‘Were Right’
content:
Ed Miliband has admitted that millions of Brits outraged by the oppression of Palestinians were “right”, speaking the day after dozens of peaceful pro-Palestine protesters were arrested outside the Labour party conference. 


Miliband used his conference speech in Liverpool on Monday to say to those “moved by the plight of the Palestinian people”: “We hear you. You were right.” His words received loud, sustained applause from the audience.


The foreign secretary is now being called upon by campaigners and former Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn to stand up for the rights of people protesting Israel’s ongoing genocide, occupation and apartheid in the Occupied Palestinian Territories and drop the ban on Palestine Action. 


Corbyn told Novara Media that Miliband is “right to vindicate those who spoke up for Palestine” but highlighted that “people are still being arrested for doing exactly that, including people outside the very conference hall in which he made that speech.”


Novara Media

reported on mass arrests

of elderly demonstrators outside Labour conference on Sunday, where nearly 200 people had gathered to call on prime minister Andy Burnham to drop the ban on Palestine Action and oppose Israel’s genocide in Gaza. 


Protesters, including pensioners, disabled people and a Church of England priest, held paper signs that read: “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action.” Merseyside police confirmed they had arrested 82 people on suspicion of wearing or carrying an article supporting a proscribed organisation. 


Miliband also declined to speak with pensioners facing arrest outside conference last night

when confronted by activists

 in a Pizza Express. 


Corbyn added: “If he really meant it, he would urge the home secretary to de-proscribe Palestine Action immediately.” 


“If we were right, then those who ignored us were wrong – which is why we need a full public inquiry into Britain’s role in Israeli war crimes. Empty words won’t end Britain’s complicity in genocide – but action will.”


Stop the War convenor Lindsey German called on Miliband to avoid ‘hypocrisy’, saying: “Miliband describes the suffering in Gaza as a ‘stain on the world’s conscience’ and that his parents taught him to ‘never walk by’. Yet his silence on Palestine Action and on the government’s attack on the right to protest is the opposite of that and is in danger of appearing hypocritical.”


German also urged Miliband to “demand” that Burnham and the home secretary de-proscribe Palestine Action and “reverse the legislation that now criminalises large amounts of previously lawful protest”. 


The foreign secretary said in his conference speech that Labour’s approach to the Middle East had been “reset” under Burnham’s leadership and words would be matched with action.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Apelan un nuevo sobreseimiento en causa por espionaje ilegal
content:
La Comisión Provincial por la Memoria presentó un recurso ante la Cámara Federal de Casación Penal para que se revierta el sobreseimiento, dictado en primera instancia por el juez Marcelo Martínez De Giorgi y confirmado a comienzos de este mes por la Cámara Federal porteña, en favor del expresidente Mauricio Macri, los exfuncionarios de la Agencia Federal de Inteligencia (AFI) Gustavo Arribas y Silvia Majdalani, y otros imputados por tareas de inteligencia ilegal. Las mismas se desplegaron sobre correos electrónicos particulares de periodistas, políticos opositores, eclesiásticos e integrantes de movimientos sociales entre otros. Para el organismo, se trata de una investigación que no cumplió con los estándares elementales de debida diligencia ni se realizó en un plazo razonable, elementos que contribuyen a provocar la impunidad de estos delitos graves. La apelación fue presentada por el organismo que patrocina a los querellantes de la causa Gustavo Traverso y Gabriela troiano.


Secretaría de Inteligencia del Estado (SIDE)


“El sobreseimiento dictado y confirmado por la Cámara se da en el marco de una causa en la que, junto a otras, se investiga una compleja trama de accionar delictivo inserta en el mismo núcleo del Estado Nacional bajo el gobierno del entonces presidente y aquí imputado, Mauricio Macri, destinada a producir inteligencia ilegal y obtener información de opositores políticos, integrantes de movimientos sociales, eclesiásticos, periodistas, personajes de la cultura e incluso personas privadas de su libertad”, señala el escrito de la CPM, que patrocina a los querellantes Gustavo Tomás Traverso y Gabriela Alejandra Troiano.


El recurso de la CPM ante la Cámara de Casación Penal se presentó luego que la Cámara Federal porteña ratificara el sobreseimiento de los imputados: “Una investigación sin profundidad, dilatada, obstaculizada podría provocar la impunidad de delitos de una relevancia inusitada para nuestra vida democrática”, consideró el organismo.


De acuerdo a la investigación penal, existió una estructura conformada entre el entonces presidente Macri, los funcionarios de la AFI Gustavo Arribas, Silva Majdalani y Darío Alberto Biorci y, en este caso, dos agentes de inteligencia de identidad reservada, que habrían formado parte  de un entramado más amplio que de manera sistemática, organizada y sostenida en el tiempo, realizando numerosas actividades de inteligencia ilegal.


Y cabe recordar que el sobreseimiento dictado por el juez federal Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi se fundó en presuntas irregularidades en las que fue obtenida la principal prueba: la falta de garantías de que se hubiera preservado la autenticidad e integridad de los discos rígidos de la Agencia Federal de Inteligencia (AFI) en los que se hallaron correos electrónicos privados de numerosas personas vinculadas al ámbito político y periodístico.


Para la CPM, tanto el sobreseimiento original como su reciente confirmación no cumplieron con los estándares mínimos de justificación y argumentación exigidos por la ley en cuanto a la interpretación de la prueba.


En efecto, tal como consta en la causa, la forma en que los discos rígidos fueron hallados, resguardados y posteriormente puestos a disposición de la justicia se realizó en cumplimiento de los protocolos previstos legalmente para la intervención de la AFI.


Asimismo, por requerimiento fiscal al comienzo de la investigación, la interventora de la AFI, Cristina Caamaño –quien ocupó ese rol entre diciembre de 2019 y junio de 2022- detalló que no se había hallado ninguna orden de reunión de información respecto a las personas cuyos correos habían sido espiados y que se había respetado la cadena de custodia del material hallado, generando una copia de seguridad espejo para trabajar sobre ella y no sobre el material guardado en el disco original. Del análisis de todo el material, continuó Caamaño, es que se produjo el informe del 14 de mayo de 2020 y que daría origen a la presente causa penal.


Es por estos motivos que la CPM, en representación de dos querellas particulares, vuelve a reiterar los argumentos esgrimidos en la apelación del primer sobreseimiento dictado en primera instancia: la prueba obtenida (principal en este expediente) fue  debidamente identificada, resguardada y entregada a los organismos jurisdiccionales correspondientes.


La mera afirmación de que “en concreto, no ha logrado sortear el principal escollo que afectó a la prueba que dio origen a la presente …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Labour to Nationalise Avanti West Coast Trains After Privatisation Fails
content:
The Avanti West Coast train service will be nationalised in March 2027, Labour has announced, following years of poor service caused by privatisation. 


The service is the latest of numerous lines that have either been brought back into public ownership or will be soon, following a pledge by the ruling party to do so ahead of the 2024 election. 


“Enough is enough. For years, people have been expected to put up with Avanti’s cancellations, delays, overcrowding and a service that has failed them time and time again,” prime minister Andy Burnham

said in a statement

 on Sunday. 


Re-nationalising the service “means passengers, not shareholders, will come first,” he added. “More investment, fewer delays and a renewed focus on getting the basics right. We’re putting essential services back in public hands and building a railway that actually works for the people who use it.”


Avanti runs services to destinations including London, Manchester, Blackpool, Edinburgh and Birmingham.  


The office of transport secretary Heidi Alexander

said in a statement

: “From 7 March 2027, taxpayers will no longer be paying fees to a private operator. Instead, every penny will be spent for the benefit of passengers.”


Several operators have been nationalised since 2025, including South Western Railway, Greater Anglia, Govia Thameslink Railway and Chiltern Railways.  


The privatisation of the UK’s rail services began in the early 1990s, when parliament passed a bill allowing for British Rail to be broken up and sold off to multiple private firms. 


Critics argue this drove up prices while making the service worse, with companies incentivised to maximise revenues while slashing costs.


By 2024, the UK had

the most expensive train fares

 in Europe, according to one study. Meanwhile shareholders have collected £14bn in dividends alone from privatised rail services,

figures from campaign group Common Wealth

 show.

author: Unknown
title: Répression féroce contre des blocages dans 4 lycées
content:
Lundi 28 septembre, dans la foulée du mouvement lycéen initié en Ile-de-France par des lycéen-nes de quartiers populaires contre le manque de moyens, quatre lycées, Jean-Paul-Sartre à (Bron), Charlie-Chaplin (Décines-Charpieu), Robert-Doisneau à (Vaulx-en-Velin) et Frédéric-Faÿs (Villeurbanne), ont été bloqués. Les cours ont été bloqué dès le début des cours le matin et certain ont réussi à forcer l'administration à renvoyer les élèves chez eux à la suite du blocage, notamment à Faÿs et à Jean-Paul Sartre.


Les blocages ont été rapidement très violemment réprimés par les flics, justifié par le lancement de feux d'artifice ou des feux de poubelles. Par endroit les lycén-nes se sont défendu-es face à la police en leur envoyant des projectiles.


Une vidéo pris aux abords du lycée Faÿs à Cusset montre la répression violente des

CRS

 qui sont arrivés en grand nombre pour chasser les lycéen-nes vers le tram en les noyant de gaz lacrymogène. La préfecture fait état de 6 interpellations sur l'ensemble des quatre lycées. On ne connaît pas à ce stade le nombre de lycéen-nes blessé-es par la police.


Déjà en mars dernier, la préfecture avait réprimé très violemment un blocage lycéen devant le lycée Saint-Exupéry (Lyon 4

e

), une vingtaine d'élèves avaient été blessés notamment par des coups de matraque, des tirs de

LBD

 et des tirs tendus de lacrymos.


 Répression et brutalité policière contre le mouvement lycéen à Lyon et Marseille


 Depuis plusieurs semaines, les lycées de Marseille et plus récemment de Lyon sont agités par une mobilisation lycéenne importante, qui s'organise autour de mots d'ordre contre l'austérité budgétaire ou contre le fascisme. Face à cette mobilisation, les préfectures envoient les flics mener une (…)


 23 mars


La Petite cuillère, l'émission anticarcérale de Radio Canut avait réalisé une

interview avec des membres du collectif lycéen

RAFAL

 sur la répression des blocus lycéens l'année dernière.


Au niveau national, le mouvement lycéen prend de l'ampleur depuis ses débuts en Seine-et-Marne (Ile de France) la semaine dernière. Parti du lycée Saint Exupéry de Créteil, où des lycéen-nes se sont mobilisé-es contre la manque de moyens, la surcharge chronique des classes, les locaux délabrés, les coûts de cantine, le 8h-18h, mais aussi le manque de personnel, profs, infirmier-es, assitantes sociales et

AESH

. Depuis, de nombreux appels à blocage circulent sur les réseaux sociaux et paniquent suffisamment les rectorats et le ministère de l'éducation nationale pour que le gouvernement annonce d'emblée envoyer les flics sur chaque blocage d'établissement. On apprend aussi dans

Contre Attaque

 qu'aujourd'hui à Saint-Ouen, sur un blocage, des flics ont délibérément attrapé un jeune pour le tabasser pendant qu'un autre lui tirait une grenade lacrymogène en pleine tête, manquant de le tuer.


Dans un autre registre, au lycée Paul Eluard à Saint-Denis, les professeurs et

AED

 ont fait une chaîne humaine pour protéger les lycéens de la police.


Des appels à poursuivre la moblisation lycéenne pendant la grève de la fonction publique du 29 septembre circulent.

author: Unknown
title: Ronahî Culture and Arts Commune established in Zurich
content:
The Ronahî Culture and Arts Commune was established in Zurich on Sunday, following work carried out by TEV-ÇAND.


At the event for the official declaration of the commune, Fahriye Iliş. Serhat Hülakü, a member of TEV-ÇAND, then took the floor and highlighted the importance of organising cultural and artistic activities according to a communal approach.


 


Hülakü spoke about the role of cultural and artistic activities in building Kurdish national unity, adding that work in the fields of culture and art constitutes an important area of resistance and achievement against assimilation policies pursued across the four parts of Kurdistan. Hülakü also expressed his enthusiasm about the establishment of the Ronahî Culture and Arts Centre.


Representatives from the four parts of Kurdistan also spoke at the event, emphasising the importance of carrying out cultural and artistic activities with an awareness of national unity.


Activities to be carried out in four areas


Mehmet Akdoğan, another TEV-ÇAND member, said that following three months of work, cultural and artistic activities had been reorganised from the perspective of a communal system. He announced that the organisation had been established under the name “Navenda Çanda Ronahî” (Ronahî Culture Centre).


Akdoğan said that activities would be carried out in four main areas: the Kurdish Music Commune, the Kurdish Halay and Folklore Commune, the Cinema and Documentary Commune, and the Kurdish Language and Literature Commune.


Akdoğan also announced the establishment of the Winterthur Culture and Arts Commune and the Pfäffikon Heftreng Culture and Arts Commune.


Following the official announcement and application process, Akdoğan said that cultural and artistic activities previously carried out at commission level within Kurdish associations would be taken to a more advanced stage. He said they planned to open an independent venue in the near future to enable the activities to be conducted more professionally and efficiently.


Akdoğan said they would continue their work to make Kurdish culture and art more visible in Europe, particularly in Zurich.

author: Unknown
title: Second phase of mine clearance launched in Rojava
content:
Mine clearance and removal of war remnants operations continue in the countryside of Serêkaniyê, Til Temir, and Zirgan, as part of efforts to secure roads, villages, and agricultural land ahead of the return of displaced people to their areas.


The Mine Action Office in Heseke provided ANHA with an overview of its work map and the latest updates regarding mine clearance and war-remnant removal operations in the region.


According to the office, mine clearance operations on and around the main road in Serêkaniyê are nearing completion and the second phase has been launched, with clearance operations now beginning in villages.


The office explained that mine clearance operations are currently targeting villages located along the line extending from Til Temir and Zirgan towards the city of Serêkaniyê, in addition to villages located along the M4 highway towards the southern countryside of the city.


The office stated: “The clearance of the main road connecting the cities of Dirbêsiyê and Serêkaniyê, which passes through al-Asadiyah village and extends to the Turkish military base located in Bab al-Faraj village along the main road, has been completed. The clearance operations covered the road and both sides of it to a distance of 25 metres."


According to the Hesekê Mine Action Office, mine clearance operations target the main road, while the risk of mines remains in the villages of al-Asadiyah and Mushairifa, where mine and war-remnant clearance operations have not yet begun.


Mine clearance operations on the main road extending from Til Temir towards the city of Serêkaniyê have been delayed due to the presence of a minefield in the village of Umm al-Keif, which has hindered the progress of the teams working in the area.


Mine clearance teams continue to work on the road with the aim of securing it for civilian traffic, in preparation for completing the clearance operations and moving on to removing mines from the villages and residential areas located along the road.


These operations are part of efforts to reduce the risks posed by mines and war remnants and to secure roads and residential areas in preparation for the return of displaced residents of Serêkaniyê to their areas and homes.


The Mine Action Office in Hesekê warned residents against returning to areas where clearance operations are still underway or using roads targeted for clearance. It called on them to follow the instructions of mine clearance teams to ensure their safety and avoid the dangers posed by war remnants.


Hundreds of families from Serêkaniyê, who were displaced from their homes following the Turkish attacks in October 2019, managed to return to their land in two batches. The return process was expected to continue, but logistical issues and developments in the area prevented this from happening.

title: The Turkification of Kurdish place names and the restoration of names in the peace process
content:
Across Kurdistan, dozens of cities, hundreds of districts, and thousands of villages, neighborhoods, highland pastures, and waterways were known for centuries by names rooted in the languages of the peoples who lived there. Beginning with the establishment of the Republic, administrative renaming policies erased a large proportion of these names from official maps. Today, at a time when the peace process is once again being discussed, restoring these names will be a concrete test of the seriousness of the process.


Beginning in the 1940s, and particularly through assimilation policies carried out by the “Specialized Board for Name Changes,” established in 1957, the names of more than ten thousand settlements were changed, according to official records. Names of Kurdish, Armenian, Syriac, Laz, and Zaza origin constituted the overwhelming majority of those targeted. Across the geography stretching from Diyarbakır to Hakkari, and from Mardin to Muş, changing the name of a village was not merely a matter of replacing a sign. It was also an attempt to erase from official records the memory, sense of belonging, and connection to the land embodied in that name.


The renaming of settlements was not merely an administrative measure; it was also part of a strategy to render a people’s presence in their own geography invisible. The name of a mountain, a stream, or a village was among the most tangible expressions of the historical relationship established with that land. Rewriting that relationship through state intervention constituted a direct intervention in identity.


Why now?


In the renewed discussions on peace and resolution in Turkey, the agenda includes not only silencing the weapons but also repairing the social realities that have been targeted by state attacks over the years. Genuine peace will only be possible if, alongside ending the conflict, the policies of denial that lie at its roots are reversed. Restoring original place names stands out as one of the most visible, concrete, and necessary steps in this process of redress. Just as erasing a people’s memory from the map carries meaning, so does writing that memory back onto the map. Justice begins with the right to be called by one’s own name.


Within this framework, the demand for the restoration of place names is an integral part of the confidence-building measures that Kurds are bringing to the peace negotiations. Every village whose original name is restored will be regarded as tangible evidence that the state is effectively acknowledging its past policy of denial and intends to reverse it. For this reason, the restoration of place names is being positioned not merely as a technical matter of municipal administration, but as a test of the sincerity of the process.


A concrete roadmap


The restoration of place names should not be carried out through arbitrary or symbolic gestures, but within a systematic legal framework. The main components of such a framework can be outlined as follows:


Legal basis:

 The Turkish Grand National Assembly should adopt specific legislation repealing past decrees that changed place names and granting official status to historical names.


Local will as the basis:

 Decisions on what name a settlement should bear should be made by its residents and elected local authorities. The restoration process should be driven from the local level rather than imposed from above.


Transfer of authority to municipalities:

 Municipal councils should be granted direct decision-making authority over changes to neighborhood and village names, without this power being restricted by tutelary approval mechanisms.


Alignment of maps and cadastral records:

 All official databases, including land registry, civil registry, postal, and navigation systems, should be updated simultaneously to reflect the restored names. The aim should be to ensure that the names are valid not only on paper but also in everyday life.


Public memory initiatives:

 An inventory of altered place names should be compiled and made publicly available, and the history of the renaming process should be included in school history textbooks.


Drawing on international experience:

 Examples such as the restoration of place names in post-apartheid South Africa, the official recognition of Indigenous geographical names in Canada, and the re-establishment of Welsh place names as official names in Wales should be examined as potential legal models.

title: Peshmerga Ministry voices concern over the withdrawal of U.S. forces
content:
The Kurdistan Regional Government’s Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs issued a statement regarding the withdrawal of United States (US) forces from Iraq and the Kurdistan Region.


Under the agreement reached between the Iraqi federal government and the US and International Coalition forces, the withdrawal of American forces from all of Iraq and the Kurdistan Region is expected to be completed by September 30.


Highlighting the sensitivity of the current period, the statement on Monday said that the continuing instability in Iraq and the broader Middle East could have consequences beyond individual states, calling for vigilance and sound political decision-making.


According to the statement, more than 1,000 drones and ballistic missiles have targeted the Kurdistan Region during the conflict, with some striking civilian areas and causing deaths, injuries and material damage.


“The United States leaving the Kurdistan Region behind in such a complex regional situation, without providing any defense system, is a cause for concern,” the statement said, stressing that the Iraqi federal government is primarily responsible for protecting the Kurdistan Region’s airspace.


The ministry also stressed the “Peshmerga forces remain prepared for new security developments and capable of responding to threats.”


In the meantime, KDP (Kurdistan Democratic Party) President Masoud Barzani warned that the withdrawal of U.S. forces from Iraq could create conditions similar to those that preceded the rise of ISIS. He expressed concern about the possibility of a repeat of the security vacuum that followed the departure of American troops in 2011.


In a televised interview with Al Sharqiya TV, Barzani recalled previous remarks in which he questioned what would prevent ISIS from returning if U.S. forces withdrew from Iraq, saying he continued to hold the same concern.


On the other hand, Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani told the Financial Times that the withdrawal of US and Coalition forces comes at a highly sensitive time and expressed concern about leaving the Kurdistan Region without defensive systems.

title: Third group of IDPs from Serêkaniyê to return home
content:
Zehra Semio, a member of the Serêkaniyê Forcibly Displaced Persons Committee, announced that the third group of people forcibly displaced from the Serêkaniyê countryside will return to their homes on Sunday.


Semio said that the third group, consisting of more than 500 families who are currently living in schools and residential centers in Hesekê, will return to their areas between the towns of Menacîr and Til Helef, west of Serêkaniyê. She added that the number of returning families may change.


The second group, consisting of around 700 families—nearly 7,000 people—who had been living in Serêkaniyê Camp, returned on September 8 to their homes in 55 villages in the countryside of Serêkaniyê, Zirgan, and Til Temir.


Background


Serêkaniyê is located in the Jazira (Cizire) Canton on the border with North Kurdistan, opposite the Ceylanpınar district of Urfa. Due to its water resources, fertile lands, and position along important trade routes, the city has been considered a strategically significant center for centuries. Its population consisted of Kurds, Arabs, Armenians, Syriacs, Circassians, and Chechens, making Serêkaniyê one of the most diverse places in the region.


The city had become a symbol of resistance against jihadist groups such as the Al-Nusra Front and the terrorist organization “Islamic State” (ISIS) in previous years. However, with the occupation by the Turkish state and allied Islamist militias on October 9, 2019, a new phase of profound destruction began. As a result of the onslaught on Serêkaniyê and Girê Spî, as well as their rural surroundings, key infrastructure largely collapsed. Water and electricity supply, as well as medical services, almost completely failed. Especially in Kurdish-populated villages, many houses were destroyed or rendered uninhabitable.


Tens of thousands of people were forced to flee. Many found refuge in the Waşokanî and Serêkaniyê camps near Hesekê, while others dispersed to places such as Kobanê and Til Temir. Some of the displaced fled further to the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), where they were partly accommodated in schools under precarious conditions.


At the same time, numerous reports indicate that new population groups have been settled in the abandoned areas. In addition to the families of occupation militias, Arab families from regions such as Eastern Ghouta, Homs, Deir ez-Zor, and Daraa were also settled in Serêkaniyê. Within a few years, the population structure of the city changed fundamentally. While an estimated 70,000 to 80,000 Kurds lived in Serêkaniyê before the occupation, today only a few dozen Kurdish families are said to remain.


IDPs attacked after returning home


Following a series of meetings between the Serêkaniyê Displaced Persons Committee, the Governor of Heseke, and officials of the Interim Government aimed at ensuring the safe return of forcibly displaced people, the first group of around 412 families returned to their homes in Serêkaniyê on August 10.


After arriving at their homes, the families came under attack by an armed group that had taken over the homes of the original residents. The group attacked some of the families and vandalized their vehicles.

Ongoing violence and obstacles to return


Reports by the Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria and international human rights organizations depict a persistently tense situation in Serêkaniyê. Accordingly, forced displacement, arbitrary arrests, kidnappings, and the systematic appropriation of property continue. For many displaced people, returning to their homes remains associated with significant risks. Numerous affected individuals report being denied entry on security grounds or being confronted with financial demands. According to witness statements, militias demand payments from those wishing to return—accompanied by threats to completely destroy their homes otherwise.

title: ᑲᑎᒪᔩᑦ ᐊᖏᙱᑦᑐᑦ ᒪᓕᒋᐊᓖᑦ ᒥᒃᖠᕚᓪᓕᖅᑎᑕᐅᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᓕᖅᑎᑕᐅᓇᔭᖅᑐᓄᑦ
content:
For the English version of this story, please see

Lowering hiring standards for Inuit would create ‘2 classes’ of officers

.


ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥ ᑭᒃᑯᓕᒫᓂ ᓴᐳᓐᓂᐊᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕋᓛᑦ ᒪᕐᕉᖕᓂ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᓱᖁᑎᒃᓴᙱᑦᑐᑦ ᑐᕌᖓᔪᓂ ᐅᓄᕐᓯᕚᓪᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᖕᓂᕐᒥ ᐃᓄᖕᓂ ᑭᒡᒐᖅᑐᐃᓇᔭᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᑕᒫᓂ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᓐᓂ, ᐅᖃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑦᑎᓇᔭᕐᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᔾᔨᒌᙱᑎᑦᑎᓗᐊᕐᓇᒥ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖅᑖᖅᑎᑦᑎᓇᓱᖕᓂᒃᑯᑦ.


ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖓ ᔮᓐ-ᕗᕌᓐᔪᐊ (ᔨᐊᕝ) ᐴᓂᐄ ᑐᓴᖅᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓄᑦ ᓯᑎᐱᕆ 15-ᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕋᓛᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᓂᑯᓂ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᐅᑎᖏᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᖅᑕᐅᔪᒪᓂᖏᑦᑎᒍᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐅᒃᐱᕈᓱᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᒃᑲᓐᓂᕋᓱᒡᓗᑎᒃ ᑭᒃᑯᓕᒫᓂ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᓐᓂ.


ᐅᑯᐊ ᐱᒋᐊᖅᑐᕕᓃᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᔪᕕᓂᕐᓄᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᔪᓚᐃ 2025-ᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᓕᕆᓂᕐᒥ ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥ ᑖᒃᑯᐊ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᖓᓱᐃᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᑐᖂᑎᓚᐅᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋ ᑕᒫᓂ ᑕᖅᑭᑦ 8 ᐃᓗᐊᓂ. ᑎᓴᒪᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ – 6-ᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᓕ ᐊᕐᓇᖅ – ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᑕᐅᓂᖏᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᖅᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᓕᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ.


ᒪᐃᒥ ᑕᑯᔭᐅᔪᓐᓇᕐᓯᑎᑕᐅᓂᑰᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐅᓇ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖅᓯᓂᖅ ᐃᓚᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ 35-ᓂ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᓯᒪᔪᓂᒃ. 21 ᑖᒃᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑐᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕋᓛᓄᑦ, 8 ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑐᖅᑕᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᒪᓕᒋᐊᖃᕐᓂᖃᖅᑐᓂᒃ, ᑕᓪᓕᒪᑦ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑐᖅᑕᐅᙱᖢᑎᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᑕᐅᓯᖅ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐅᕈᑎᒋᔭᐅᙱᖢᓂ.


ᐊᑕᐅᓯᖅ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐊᓯᔾᔩᖁᔨᓯᒪᓪᓗᓂ ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᒪᓕᒐᖓᓂ ᐅᑯᐊ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᐅᔪᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᒃᑲᓐᓂᕈᓐᓇᕐᓯᓯᒪᓗᑎᒃ ᐸᓖᓯᓂ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᒪᓕᒐᐅᓂᐊᖅᑐᓂᒃ. ᐊᓯᐊᓕ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᓂᑯ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖅᑖᕋᓱᒃᑐ ᐸᓖᓯᓕᕆᓂᑰᒍᑎᒃ ᑖᒃᑯᐊ ᐊᑐᖁᔭᐅᙱᖢᑎᒃ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖅᑖᕋᓱᓕᕈᑎᒃ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᐅᑎᖏᓐᓂ.


“ᒪᕐᕈᐃᓂ ᐊᔾᔨᒌᙱᑦᑐᓂ ᐊᑐᓕᖁᔨᙱᓐᓇᑦᑕ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᓐᓂ. ᐃᓄᖕᓂ ᐸᓖᓯᖃᕈᒪᒐᑦᑕ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᑖᕆᔭᐅᕙᒃᑐᓂ ᐱᖃᑦᑕᕐᒥᓗᑎᒃ, ᐱᓇᓱᐊᒐᖏᑦ ᐊᔾᔨᒌᒡᓗᑎᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᕆᔭᖏᑦ ᐊᔾᔨᒌᒡᓗᑎᒃ,” ᐴᓂᐄ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓄᑦ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᐃᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᑎᓪᓗᒋ ᐃᓄᒃᔪᐊᒃᒥᑦ.


ᐴᓂᐄ, ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᔨᑦᑎᕋᐅᑎᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᐅᓚᑦᑎᔨᐅᔪᖅ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑲᑎᕕᒃᒥ ᓄᓇᓕᓕᒫᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᖏᓐᓂ ᐅᕘᓇ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕋᓛᑎᒍᑦ, ᑖᓐᓇᓗ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐅᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᑲᑎᕕᒃᒥ ᓄᓇᓕᓕᒫᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᑯᖏᓐᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᒪᑭᕝᕕᒃ ᑯᐊᐳᕇᓴᓐᑯᓐᓄᑦ.


ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕋᓛᑦ ᐃᑲᔪᖅᑐᐃᓯᒪᔪᑦ ᖃᐅᔨᓴᕈᑎᑎᒍᑦ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᔭᐅᔪᓂ ᑭᒃᑯᓕᒫᓂ ᐊᑦᑕᓇᖅᑐᒦᑎᑦᑎᑦᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒥ ᐅᑯᑎᒎᓇᖅ ᑲᑎᕕᒃᒥ ᓄᓇᓕᓕᒫᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᖓᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᒪᑭᕝᕕᒃᑯᑦ, ᐃᓄᒃᑎᑐᑦ-ᐅᐃᕖᑐᑦ-ᖃᓪᓗᓈᑐᓪᓗ ᑐᑭᓕᐅᕆᔾᔪᓯᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐱᓇᓱᐊᕈᓯᕐᓂ ᑎᓴᒪᓂᒃ ᐃᓄᖕᓄᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᔪᒥ ᐃᓕᖅᑯᓯᓕᕆᓂᕐᒥ ᖃᐅᔨᕚᓪᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥᒃ ᐸᓖᓯᓂ ᑎᑭᓵᓂᑯᓂᒃ.


ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕋᓛᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᖅᕕᖕᒥ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᖅᓴᖅᑎᑦᑎᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᕐᒥᒃ ᖃᐅᔨᕚᓕᕈᑎᒃᓴᓂᒃ ᐸᓖᓯᓕᕆᓂᕐᒥ ᐅᑭᐅᕐᑕᖅᑐᕐᒥ, ᓲᕐᓗ ᒪᑯᓂᖓ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᕐᓴᖅᑎᑕᐅᓗᑎᒃ ᐊᒃᓱᕈᓗᐊᕐᓇᒥ ᐊᑐᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᕐᒥᒃ, ᐴᓂᐄ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᐊᕐᕌᒍᑦ ᒪᕐᕉᒃ ᑐᖏᑦᑎᐊᖓᓂ ᑎᓴᒪᑦ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᕐᓯᒪᓕᕐᒪᑕ ᓄᓇᕕᒃᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᓄᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓪᓗᑎᒃ.


ᓄᕕᐱᕆ 2024-ᒥ, ᔮᓱᐊ ᐸᐱᒐᑐᒃ ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᒻᒪ ᐊᒻᒪ ᒪᕐᕈᓕᐊᖑᖃᑎᖓ ᒑᓇᑦ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᑕᐅᒻᒪᕆᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐸᓖᓯᓄᑦ ᖁᑭᖅᓴᖅᑕᐅᓪᓗᑎᒃ.


ᒪᐃ 2025-ᒥ, ᒫᒃ ᐊᓐᓇᓈᒃ ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᑲᖏᖅᓱᐊᓗᔾᔪᐊᖅᒥ ᐸᓖᓯᓄᑦ ᐅᐸᒃᑕᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ. ᔪᓚᐃ 2025-ᒥ ᔭᐃᒥᓯ ᑲᕕᒃ ᐃᓄᒃᔪᐊᒃᒥ ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐸᓖᓯᓄᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑎᓯᐱᕆᒥ 6-ᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᓕᒃ ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᓪᓗᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᑖᑕᖓ ᐋᓐᑐᕉ ᓇᓗᒃᑐᒃ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᑕᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐸᓖᓯᒃᑯᑦ ᖁᑭᖅᓴᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᐃᓄᒃᔪᐊᒃᒥ.


ᐅᑯᐊ Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes, ᖃᐅᔨᓴᖃᑦᑕᖅᑐᑦ ᐃᓄᖕᓂ ᐋᓐᓂᖅᑐᖃᕐᓂᕌᖓᑦ ᐅᕝᕙᓘᓐᓃᑦ ᑐᖁᑕᐅᔪᖃᕐᓂᕌᖓᑦ ᐸᓖᓯᓄᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐊᓂ ᑖᒃᑯᓄᖓ ᑎᓴᒪᓄ ᑐᓂᓯᓚᐅᕐᑐᑦ ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᐱᕋᔭᒃᑐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᒪᓕᒐᕐᓂ ᓱᕋᐃᓂᑯᓄᑦ ᐃᖅᑲᖅᑐᐃᕕᒃᑰᖅᑎᑦᑎᔨᓄᑦ.


ᐋᒐᓯᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ ᑯᐸᐃᒃᒥ ᒐᕙᒪᑐᖃᒃᑯᑦ ᑐᓴᖅᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᑦ ᐸᓖᓯᓂ ᑐᖂᑦᑎᔪᕕᓂᕐᓂ ᐸᓯᔭᒃᓴᙳᖅᑎᑦᑎᔾᔮᙱᓐᓂᕋᖅᖢᑎᒃ ᐅᕙᓂ 2025-ᒥ ᐃᓄᒃᔪᐊᒃᒥ ᖁᑭᖅᓴᖅᑐᕕᓂᕐᓂ, ᖃᐅᔨᒐᒥ ᑭᓯᐊᓂ ᑕᐃᒪᓐᓇᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᓕᓚᐅᕐᓂᖓᓂ.


ᑐᓴᖅᑎᑦᑎᓚᐅᙱᑦᑐᑦ ᐸᓯᔭᒃᓴᙳᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᐊᕐᒪᖔᑕ ᐊᓯᖏᓐᓂ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᕕᓂᕐᓂᒃ. ᑲᑎᒪᔩᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᐱᓇᓱᐊᕈᓯᐅᓚᐅᕐᑐᒥ, ᓴᓪᓗᐃᑦᓄᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨ ᓯᑏᕙᓐ ᒍᕌᓱ ᐊᐱᕆᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐴᓂᐄᒥ ᑐᓴᖅᑎᑕᐅᔪᒪᓪᓗᓂ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᖓᓕᕐᒪᖓᑦ ᐃᓅᔪᓐᓃᓚᐅᕐᑑ ᐸᐱᒐᑦᑐᒃ ᒥᒃᓴᓄᑦ.


“ᐅᓇ ᓱᓕ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑎᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐅᕙᓂ ᓴᓪᓗᐃᑦᓂ,” ᒍᕌᓱ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ..


ᐴᓂᐄ ᑭᐅᓚᐅᕐᑐᕐᓕ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑲᐅᑎᑦ ᐅᑕᕿᓂᖏᓐᓂ ᐃᓱᒪᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᑯᐸᐃᒃ ᒐᕙᒪᖏᓐᓄᑦ ᑭᓯᐊᓂᑦᑕᐅᖅ ᐃᓱᒫᓘᑎᖃᕐᓂᕋᖅᑐᖅ ᐊᑯᓂᕈᓗ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᓂᖓᓂ.


ᐴᓂᐄ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᕋᓛᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᐊᕐᓂᕋᖅᖢᓂᒋᑦ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᐅᔪᓐᓇᖅᑐᓂᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᖓ ᐊᕕᒃᑐᖅᓯᒪᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓄᑦ ᑐᓴᖅᑕᐅᑎᑕᐅᓂᐊᖅᖢᓂ.

title: Spot doğal gaz piyasasında referans fiyat 17 bin 602 lira oldu
content:
Duygu Ayber Gültekin [email protected]

Enerji Piyasaları İşletme AŞ (EPİAŞ) verilerine göre, spot doğal gaz piyasasında dün gerçekleşen işlemlerin toplam hacmi 9 milyon 575 bin 958 lira oldu. İşlem hacmi bir önceki gün 4 milyon 829 bin 550 lira seviyesinde bulunuyordu.

Dünkü işlemlerde toplam 544 bin metreküp doğal gazın ticareti gerçekleştirildi. 1000 metreküp doğal gaz için belirlenen referans fiyat ise 17 bin 602 lira 86 kuruş oldu.

Piyasa katılımcılarının dengeleme gazı alış fiyatı 18 bin 483 lira olarak belirlenirken, satış fiyatı 16 bin 722 lira 72 kuruş oldu.

Öte yandan Türkiye'nin doğal gaz arzında dün 93 milyon 168 bin 325 metreküplük giriş gerçekleşti. Aynı gün piyasaya sunulan doğal gaz miktarı 93 milyon 81 bin 568 metreküp olarak kaydedildi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Spot elektrik piyasasında yarın için en yüksek fiyat 4 bin 100 lira
content:
Duygu Ayber Gültekin [email protected]

Enerji Piyasaları İşletme AŞ (EPİAŞ) verilerine göre, spot elektrik piyasasında bugün gerçekleşen işlem hacmi, bir önceki güne kıyasla yüzde 23,15 artarak 1 milyar 939 milyon 89 bin 137 liraya ulaştı.

Gün öncesi piyasada yarın için belirlenen elektrik fiyatlarında en yüksek seviye saat 17.00'de görülecek. Bu saatte bir megavatsaat elektriğin fiyatı 4 bin 100 lira 1 kuruş olacak.

Yarın için en düşük elektrik fiyatı ise saat 03.00'te uygulanacak. Bu saat diliminde megavatsaat başına fiyat 1300 lira olarak belirlendi.

Gün öncesi piyasada yarın için hesaplanan bir megavatsaat elektriğin aritmetik ortalama fiyatı 2 bin 753 lira 35 kuruş olurken, ağırlıklı ortalama fiyat 2 bin 819 lira 57 kuruş olarak kayıtlara geçti.

Öte yandan spot piyasada bugün teslim edilecek elektriğin megavatsaat fiyatı gün içinde en yüksek 4 bin 321 lira 33 kuruşa, en düşük ise 240 liraya kadar geriledi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti'nde Ebola salgını: Vaka sayısı 8 bin 67'ye, can kaybı 3 bin 901'e yükseldi
content:
Kongo Demokratik Cumhuriyeti (KDC) Sağlık Bakanlığı tarafından yayımlanan son verilere göre, ülkedeki yedi eyalette etkisini sürdüren salgında doğrulanmış vaka sayısı 8 bin 67'ye, can kaybı ise 3 bin 901'e yükseldi. Salgının, henüz onaylanmış bir aşısı ya da özel bir tedavisi bulunmayan nadir ‘Bundibugyo’ virüsü varyantından kaynaklandığı ve ölüm oranının yüzde 48'in üzerine çıktığı belirtildi.

Afrika Hastalık Kontrol ve Önleme Merkezleri (Africa CDC) salgının başından itibaren virüse yakalanan 50 sağlık çalışanının yaşamını yitirdiğini açıkladı. Africa CDC, mevcut tablonun yayılma hızı bakımından 11 binden fazla insanın hayatını kaybettiği 2014-2016 Batı Afrika bölgesel salgınını geride bıraktığını bildirdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Equality Now
title: Nepal’s flood recovery must address the heightened risks facing women and girls
content:
28th September 2026


Nepal’s flood recovery must address the heightened risks facing women and girls


9 min read


News and Insights


End harmful practices


Asia and the Pacific


Kathmandu, Nepal, September 26, 2026:

On August 26, 2026, deadly flash floods and landslides ripped through Himalayan towns and villages along Nepal and Tibet’s border, devastating communities. T

he United Nations estimates that in Nepal’s worst-affected districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot,

157,050 women and girls are directly or indirectly impacted

.

 


As Nepal moves from emergency response to recovery and reconstruction, Ranjeeta Silwal, a human rights lawyer and Equality Now’s South Asia Regional Representative, explains in an interview how decisions about shelter, healthcare, education, livelihoods and social protection must prioritise the specific needs of women and girls. Ranjeeta, who lives in Kathmandu, calls for women and girls to have a central role in shaping recovery and climate adaptation, so rebuilding strengthens their rights and resilience rather than reinforcing existing gender inequalities.


Climate change, melting glaciers and Nepal’s catastrophic floods 


Shortly after 8:30 am, a catastrophic avalanche of glacial ice and bedrock roughly two square kilometres in size plunged thousands of metres into the river below, triggering a lethal flood of water, ice, rock and sediment. Travelling over 200 kilometres from Tibet into Nepal, the raging torrent swept away people, animals, homes, schools, roads, bridges and other key infrastructure. 


World Weather Attribution explains that

human-caused climate change

 is thawing permafrost in the Himalayan mountains and causing glaciers to melt, likely destabilising the slopes that triggered this humanitarian and environmental disaster. 


At the time of writing, over 1,450 people are confirmed dead and more than 8,000 remain missing, with only a fraction of bodies identified and returned to their families. Nepal’s National Child Rights Council and Save the Children have reported that over


1,000 children are in temporary shelters

 without any parents, many of whom are dead or missing.


Ranjeeta Silwal explains how Nepal’s floods have put women and girls at greater risk 


“While temporary shelters can be life-saving, if they aren’t designed with gender protection considerations from the outset, they can create new risks associated with overcrowding, lack of privacy, separation from family and community support networks, and limited access to confidential mechanisms for reporting violence.

Without safe, accessible toilets, adequate lighting, privacy and safe pathways, women and girls may face risks simply when using the toilet or bathing, particularly at night. 


“Systems that would normally prevent and respond to violations, like health and social services, police, courts and local communities, may be damaged or inaccessible.

When authorities are focused elsewhere or are themselves absent because of disaster, the risk of violence, exploitation and other abuse increases exponentially. 


“W

omen who are pregnant or breastfeeding, women in poverty or from rural communities, those with disabilities, widowed and single women, and women-headed households may face additional barriers in accessing services, facilities and information following natural disasters

. Adolescent girls can be especially affected because they have less mobility, less access to information and limited decision-making power.


“We need to ask: who can move safely, who has privacy, who can access food and water, who has information and safety networks? These are not additional considerations; these are basic requirements of a rights-based humanitarian response. 


“

The emergency doesn’t end when flood water recedes, as the secondary impacts can continue for months, even years. When families lose their house, their income and support networks, women and girls become more exposed and vulnerable to sexual violence, intimate partner violence, sexual exploitation, trafficking and child marriage. We need to understand that protection from gender-based violence must be part of the emergency response; it is not something that can wait until reconstruction begins.”


How does the climate crisis increase the risk of child marriage?


“Nepal has made important legal and policy commitments by raising the legal age of marriage to 20 for both women and men and pledging to end child marriage by 2030. Despite …

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Facebook Blocks Lula’s Campaign Ads Just Days Before Brazil Election
content:
Meta briefly disabled ads on the Facebook page of Brazil’s leftwing president on Friday – just days before he faces a far-right challenger in national elections. 


The campaign of incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has filed an appeal with the social media giant and is awaiting an explanation for the incident, state-run

Agência Brasil reported

.


Lula, 80, is running for a fourth and final term against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of Brazil’s former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro. 


The controversy over the Facebook ads comes after Amnesty International accused Meta of failing to stop the spread of election-related misinformation on the platform. 


The rights group

ran an experiment in September

 where it submitted 14 ads to Facebook that contained disinformation and “were designed to reflect… tactics that are often used by politicians and candidates to support authoritarian practices.” 


Amnesty’s test ads contained incorrect information on when and where to vote and which candidates were running, Amnesty said, as well as false allegations that “certain candidates were rigging the election”.


Facebook approved eight of the ads containing disinformation. Of the ads it rejected, none were flagged for disinformation. One of the ads that passed said: “We need a military revolution, do not vote in the elections, and the military will take back power if less than 50% votes!”


Jurema Werneck, executive director of Amnesty International Brazil, said Meta’s failure to catch the ads was “deeply alarming” and “shows that Meta is not doing enough to prevent its platform from being a vector of disinformation, while continuing to profit from the content and advertising systems that enable its spread.” 


Shortly after beating the older Bolsonaro in 2022, Lula thwarted a coup attempt by his defeated rival. Ahead of this year’s poll on 4 October, Lula has warned of foreign interference in the election by the US, where president Donald Trump support’s Bolsonaro candidacy. 


Bolsonaro is a staunch supporter of Israel and has promised to align Brazil more closely with the apartheid state, including by

moving its embassy to Jerusalem

. 


Lula, a prominent Israel critic and former union leader, has said Trump is trying to influence the election with economic pressure, after the US imposed two new rounds of tariffs in July.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Britain's Gaza Secrets Exposed": How U.K. Downplayed Israeli Crimes to Keep Selling Weapons
content:
A new documentary titled

Britain’s Gaza Secrets Exposed

 reveals new details about the U.K. government’s internal response to alleged Israeli war crimes in Gaza. Presented by journalist Ramita Navai and produced by Ben De Pear for Channel 4’s investigative program

Dispatches

, the documentary examines government records, some newly publicized, to show how the United Kingdom ignored or concealed mounting evidence of Israel’s genocidal actions in Gaza after the October 7 attacks.


“We were looking at how our country, which prides itself on having an ethical foreign policy and as being one of the supporting members of the United Nations on human rights, was able to keep selling arms,” says De Pear. “And basically, what we found was a doctored process … It’s quite extraordinary the level of duplicity that was going on in order for us to keep selling Israel arms.” Ben De Pear also produced the 2025

BAFTA

-winning documentary

Gaza: Doctors Under Attack

, which the British Broadcasting Corporation, or

BBC

, initially commissioned but later refused to air.

Gaza: Doctors Under Attack

 was broadcast instead by Channel 4.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Hope Is Back With Burnham, Apparently – But Not for Pensioners Opposing Genocide
content:
Cast your mind back, for one moment, to January. I was freezing my socks off outside various supermarkets around Manchester,

chatting to locals

 outraged that then-PM Keir Starmer and Labour’s NEC had blocked Andy Burnham for standing in the Gorton and Denton byelection. 


Fast-forward nine months, and it’s Burnham’s first Labour conference as prime minister under the slogan “Hope again”. How things change. But in other areas, matters are decidedly the same.


Yesterday, we once again saw mass arrests of peaceful protesters under the Terrorism Act, the majority of them elderly pensioners holding paper signs. These scenes were a shameful fixture under Starmer’s government, and now too, it seems, under Burnham’s.

Undeterred by bouts of wind and rain,

200-odd people

 gathered outside conference on its opening day to unveil or swiftly pen placards reading: “I oppose genocide. I support Palestine Action.” 


I’ve reported on a lot of these demos – of varying sizes and in varying kinds of weather – since Palestine Action became the first direct action group in British history to be proscribed as a terror organisation in July 2025 by then-home secretary Yvette Cooper.


What I’m always struck by is the quiet dignity of the older generations – the men and women in their 60s, 70s and above who sit silently with their placards, risking being arrested as terrorists because, as one man told me yesterday, they “have less to lose”. They stand in stark contrast to the geriatric audience members at Reform conference, filmed

apparently assaulting

 a young female activist. 


Those taking part in yesterday’s demonstration, some having travelled from as far as Cornwall, told me that it’s about sending a message to Burnham, about refusing to do nothing in the face of Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza, and about the attack on free speech that the Palestine Action ban represents. 


Merseyside police began nicking grannies and grandads about 40 minutes into the demo. Witnessing officers carrying elderly and frail people away never fails to be unsettling. It puts an ugly crack in the idea of this country as one where our basic civil liberties are protected, and with each arrest, the crack gets bigger and wider and fractures the mirror surface of our democracy further. 


By 8pm, police confirmed that 50 arrests had been made. Over at the New Statesman drinks reception at the Museum of Liverpool, foreign secretary Ed Miliband gave a speech about Burnham and the party’s “progressive values”. He urged listeners to

“look at what we’ve done on Israel and Palestine”

. 


Miliband was

later approached in a Pizza Express

 by activists, across from where arrests were being made, and asked to come and “have a conversation” with the pensioners being carried away. He declined.


Organisers Defend Our Juries told Novara Media that arrests of peaceful protesters were made until 4:30am, with Merseyside police stopping sign-holders from leaving the area. Eight were ultimately left unarrested, according to Defend Our Juries, including two people in wheelchairs.


“Hope again”? Conference has only just begun, but I wouldn’t say we were off to a great start.

author: Unknown
title: Genova: 3 ottobre assemblea generale operativa
content:
Il prossimo 30 ottobre in oltre 40 porti del Mediterraneo e dell’Europa si svolgerà una giornata internazionale di mobilitazione contro la guerra, il genocidio, il riarmo e la militarizzazione dei porti lanciata dalle organizzazioni sindacali dei lavoratori portuali CGT Ports and Docks (Francia), ENEDEP (Grecia), LAB (Paesi Baschi), Liman-İş (Turchia), ODT (Marocco), USB e ORSA Porti (Italia). Si tratta di una delle più grandi iniziative internazionali per la pace promossa dalle organizzazioni dei lavoratori negli ultimi decenni.


Da Unione Sindacale di Base


Stiamo vivendo in un mondo nel quale assistiamo alla moltiplicazione delle aggressioni condotte dagli Usa e da Israele dal Medio Oriente all’Iran fino a Cuba, al Venezuela e al Sudan, mentre prosegue impunito il genocidio del popolo palestinese. I governi europei, intanto, continuano a promuovere una folle corsa al riarmo, trascinandoci in una spirale sempre più pericolosa e con effetti ogni giorno più pesanti sulle condizioni di vita e di lavoro. In questa situazione, peraltro, i prezzi continuano a salire e i salari e le pensioni rimangono fermi al palo. Si restringono gli spazi di agibilità democratica e si moltiplicano i decreti sicurezza e le leggi bavaglio e si diffonde anche nelle scuole una cultura militarista e di sostegno alle scelte di guerra. E si avvertono sempre più drammatici gli effetti della crisi climatica, mentre i governi, invece di affrontarla, dedicano tutte le risorse disponibili al riarmo. Cresce infine un clima di odio contro la popolazione immigrata, frutto della precisa volontà di farne la responsabile del peggioramento generale delle condizioni di vita e di accesso ai servizi.


Di fronte a questa situazione i lavoratori portuali si oppongono fermamente al piano di militarizzazione dei porti che riguarderà anche le altre infrastrutture strategiche (MMA) varato dalla UE. Vogliono che il progresso tecnologico, l’automazione e l’IA non siano utilizzati per eliminare i posti di lavoro e compromettere i diritti di chi lavora. E che i contratti servano a garantire veri aumenti salariali, occupazione stabile, riduzione dell’orario di lavoro e un sistema pensionistico dignitoso.

Mentre sembra quindi che per i popoli non ci sia più spazio per far sentire la propria voce e che il nostro destino sia completamente nelle mani di chi ci sta spingendo verso un futuro da incubo, dal mondo del lavoro parte una mobilitazione che vuole costruire una prospettiva diversa.

NOI organizzazioni e movimenti sociali vogliamo raccogliere l’appello che viene dai lavoratori portuali e costruire assieme la Giornata Internazionale del 30 ottobre.

Per questo ci incontreremo il prossimo 3 ottobre a Genova per sostenere il blocco dei porti e decidere assieme le forme e le modalità con cui allargare e rafforzare la mobilitazione e lo sciopero.
