author: Unknown
title: Mithat Sancar concludes talks in Switzerland
content:
İmralı Delegation member Mithat Sancar traveled to Switzerland at the invitation of the “Peace and Solidarity Platform,” which brings together political parties, trade unions, and civil society organizations, to hold a series of meetings. Sancar participated in events organized by the platform and also held separate meetings at the Federal Parliament with delegations from the Socialist Party (SP) and the Green Party (Grüne).


Sancar took part in a roundtable meeting with the leadership of the Swiss Democracy Platform. Finally, he attended a panel organized by the Peace and Solidarity Platform on the latest developments in Turkey and the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


The panel was moderated by Rebekka Wyler, General Secretary of VPOD (Swiss Public Service Union), with İmralı Delegation member Mithat Sancar and Meral Çiçek, representative of the Kurdish Women’s Movement in Europe, participating as speakers.


Mithat Sancar gave a comprehensive presentation on the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


‘There is a need for a climate of trust’


Sancar emphasized that some progress had been made in the ongoing talks between the Turkish state and Abdullah Öcalan, and that certain reciprocal steps had been taken. He stressed that the issue of trust, however, remained a key matter that needed to be addressed.


“Overall, there is a need for a climate of trust. If we are talking about a ‘peace process,’ a climate of trust needs to develop. Mutual trust needs to be established. There is a shortcoming in this regard, and it must be overcome as soon as possible.”


“The March 27 call and the developments that followed have shown that the Kurdish people, together with Mr. Öcalan, remain committed to peace. They say that there is no path ahead other than peace. The people state that they will remain committed to the peace process and continue to insist on peace,” he said.


‘Switzerland can play an important role in the peace process’


DEM Party MP Mithat Sancar also spoke about his meetings in Switzerland, saying:


“We met with political party delegations in the Federal Parliament. Switzerland, in particular, can play an important role in this peace process. Switzerland has a longstanding tradition in this regard and has hosted many peace processes. It should also contribute to this process. Both the Federal Parliament and political actors need to renew their efforts in this regard. However, no such initiative has been taken so far.


There must be no turning back from this process. Peace benefits everyone. Developments in the Middle East show us just how valuable this peace process is. The state must address this process within a legal and constitutional framework and develop solutions.”


We are making every effort within our means


In her speech, Meral Çiçek addressed the role of women in the ongoing talks with the Turkish state, with particular emphasis on the efforts abroad.


“We are in the diaspora, so naturally our assessments will be shaped to some extent by this perspective. The Kurdish women’s movement has a clear position on peace. We have been struggling for years. Now we are making every effort within our means to ensure that these ongoing talks with the Turkish state succeed,” Meral Çiçek said.

author: Mada Masr
title: With region in turmoil Madbuly, Abdel Atty go to UNGA
content:
As diplomats and heads of states from around the world descend on New York this week to hold official and unofficial talks during the United Nations General Assembly, the already-long ledger of regional crises continues to grow.


In recent weeks the Houthis have taken key areas overlooking the crucial Bab al-Mandab Strait, triggering renewed fighting in Yemen. Meanwhile in Ethiopia, the long-simmering tensions in Tigray have boiled over, with the Tigray People’s Liberation Front

seizing

 on Wednesday the restive northern state’s three airports and setting the stage for what could become another complex regional war in the Horn of Africa.


This is in addition to the continued war in Sudan, the threat of escalation in Iran, the dire oil crisis that the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz has created, and the stalled diplomatic process on Gaza.


Egypt finds itself at the intersection, if not directly involved in many of these crises. To represent Egypt’s position at the mega-diplomatic forum that is the UNGA, President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi called on Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly for the second year in a row to lead Cairo’s delegation.


Sisi led Egypt’s delegations to the UNGA himself from 2014 to 2019. Since then, he has sent his foreign minister in his place: first Sameh Shoukry, who held the post from 2014 to 2024, and now Badr Abdel Atty.


The president’s decision to not personally lead the delegation this year, according to a government official, comes down to the fact that he “did not want to personally participate in the meeting of the Board of Peace, even though the primary issue on the agenda was Gaza — a pivotal matter for Egypt.”


“To this day, the board remains unable to take serious action to improve the situation for Palestinians on the ground — despite a full year having passed since the ceasefire agreement between Hamas and Israel, following two years of an Israeli war of extermination against Gaza — which is, of course, deeply embarrassing for Cairo,” the government official says.


The Board of Peace, chaired by United States President Donald Trump, was established earlier this year, with Bulgarian diplomat Nickolay Mladenov selected as the board’s envoy to the Gaza Strip. According to a member of the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza — a body established by the Board of Peace to succeed Hamas — the board is “completely powerless to even secure Israel’s consent for the committee to enter the Strip, or to allow the exit of 10,000 individuals selected for training in Egypt to serve as a Palestinian police force replacing Hamas’s police, even though Hamas has publicly declared its readiness to relinquish all its weapons.”


Although a source with direct insight into Egyptian-Israeli relations states that Cairo is maintaining all official and unofficial communication channels with Tel Aviv to address the situation in Gaza, this does not imply that the head of government will personally participate in Board of Peace meetings, given its limited effectiveness.


Instead it was Madbuly who led the delegation to the Board of Peace meetings to discuss the situation in Gaza on Wednesday.


Setting aside what a member of the team preparing for the Egyptian delegation’s visit to New York described to Mada Masr as Madbouly’s largely ceremonial role, much of Egypt’s political messaging is being handled by Foreign Minister Badr Abdel Atty, whose schedule has been packed with meetings. Egypt’s top diplomat arrived in New York on September 19 — two days before Madbouly — and is set to return to Cairo next week.


According to the team member, there are four key issues atop Abdel Atty’s agenda during his meetings in New York. The first is the situation in Sudan.


Egypt hopes to extend the UN Security Council resolution regarding the arms embargo in Darfur without expanding it to cover the entire country — a move the United States

pushed

 for earlier this month before the UNSC opted to maintain the status quo for one month.


Careful not to stir up a diplomatic confrontation with the US, Egypt is still trying to make the case that extending the embargo to all of Sudan would equate the “Sudanese national army” with the “Rapid Support Forces militia,” an Egyptian diplomat explains.


“Egypt’s stance here is not merely a reflection of its support for the Sudanese military led by Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. It stems from Egypt’s firm refusal to allow any party to undermine the national military …

author: Unknown
title: Marinëz
content:
Riceviamo e pubblichiamo questo contributo di

Elon Miloti

 che ci testimonia la lotta territoriale di Marinëz in Albania.


Nel paese dei miei, Marinëz (Albania), un’intensissima lotta autonoma ha ottenuto una vittoria enorme contro la multinazionale che gestisce i pozzi petroliferi del territorio. Marinëz si trova al centro del più grande giacimento su terraferma d’Europa e i pozzi, a decine e decine, sorgono su terreni di proprietà della gente del posto da generazioni. Regolati da contratti d’affitto irrisori rispetto ai profitti dell’azienda, da mesi non venivano nemmeno più pagati. L’auto-organizzazione degli abitanti, iniziata ad agosto, si è presentata inizialmente negli uffici in città. Per due volte li ha occupati. Presidio sotto il sole cocente, apertura dei cancelli a spinta, parapiglia con le guardie private, occupazione. Pur di imporre un confronto con i vertici dell’azienda, che si rifiutavano di incontrarli. Poi la protesta è passata direttamente tra i pozzi del paese, fino a occupare, la settimana scorsa, i locali amministrativi, rimasti occupati anche di notte, chiedendo un incontro risolutivo con il CEO.


La multinazionale cinese rifiutava di riconoscere gli abitanti come controparte, chiedendo di interloquire solo con le istituzioni locali e lo Stato. Ma se la terra appartiene a chi la vive, socialmente e legalmente, perché chiamare in causa lo Stato rimuovendo i diretti interessati? E soprattutto, perché farlo in un contesto in cui le istituzioni locali e nazionali sono piegate agli interessi del profitto? La domanda, ovviamente, è retorica e gli abitanti non si sono piegati: “Le trattative le facciamo noi”. Alla fine la dirigenza si è dovuta presentare, con il CEO in persona, garantendo lo sblocco immediato degli affitti arretrati e il rispetto dei contratti.


Una vittoria del tutto auto-organizzata: senza partiti, senza sindacati, senza deleghe, senza collettivi. Neanche per scelta, ma per necessità, visto che la transizione democratica post-comunismo è stata immediata e netta per privati e sfruttatori, ma di cancellazione totale verso organizzazioni democratiche e sociali.


Una vittoria gigantesca, ma che è solo il primo passo. Fin dall’inizio la vertenza ha assunto una dimensione politica profonda. Si chiede equità salariale e giustizia ecologica, ambiente e salute. I pozzi causano danni devastanti alla salute: patologie del sangue e delle vie respiratorie, accumulo di alterazioni genetiche e disturbi neurologici. In un contesto nazionale dove la sanità è privatizzata e cure e prevenzione sono negate. Per massimizzare i profitti, l’azienda ha provocato negli anni scosse sismiche artificiali o ci sono state esplosioni che hanno abbattuto le case, senza che molti abbiano mai visto un risarcimento. I lavoratori sono sfruttati e le tutele ambientali, già minime e insufficienti, vengono sistematicamente raggirate. Petrolio che scorre a fiumi, ma ricchezze ad altri, un paese senza nemmeno molte strade asfaltate e le esternalizzazioni negative, come le chiamano gli economisti, tutte sul groppone alla gente che in quei territori ci vive da sempre.


Quando arrivi a Marinëz, un paese di 5000 abitanti ormai decimato dall’emigrazione e dalla privazione, l’odore acre del greggio ti investe già ai confini del centro abitato. Dentro, si fonde con la vita contadina e coltivatrice, allevatrice e operaia: con i pascoli e le coltivazioni, i frutti e gli animali. Terreni da sempre della gente del posto, sotto controllo statale durante il comunismo -che in cambio, oltre a piena occupazione, favoriva attività aggregative e sociali, culturali e folkloristiche- che dal ’90 la popolazione ha lottato per mantenere propri, finendo però nella tenaglia della deregolamentazione incontrollata. Gli stessi vertici dell’attuale multinazionale cinese, nei mesi scorsi, sono stati arrestati per frode e corruzione, riciclaggio ed evasione.


Sono piccoli tasselli di lotte territoriali che oggi, mentre a Tirana la protesta nazionale va avanti da oltre 100 giorni, si interconnettono contro le prepotenze di partiti e multinazionali. Questa vittoria dimostra che, anche quando la coesione sociale viene forzatamente erosa, l’aggregazione ostacolata e la comunità privata di risorse e spazi culturali, la lotta continua a scorrere, quotidianamente, sottotraccia. E quando si organizza collettivamente, la società vince contro i prepotenti. Marinëz, aty ku nafta derdhej lume

author: 张皓翔
title: Here Is Rhodes: Begin the Dance of Roses!【在罗陀斯的土地上起一曲玫瑰花的舞】
content:
This book asks a question that is at once old and urgently contemporary: has class struggle become obsolete? Against both the triumphalism of “the end of history” and the moralistic complaint that the masses have grown apathetic, it proposes an analytical variable: the gravitational mechanism of association.

Through a historical sequence—from the primacy of nation in agrarian-feudal societies, to the direct class gravity of industrial capitalism, to the split gravities of the digital age (renascent nationalism at the macro level and identity-, taste-, and singularity-based bonds at the micro level)—it reinterprets feminism, environmentalism, and identity politics as displaced, uneven, yet still progressive forms of class struggle.

Engaging critically with post-Marxism, it insists that the material base and the capital-labor antagonism remain decisive. The new bonds are a genuine advance in human richness, but without reconnecting to material interest they risk becoming depoliticized enclaves.

The book argues that AI-driven mass unemployment will produce a social—not merely physiological—crisis of survival, recentering class interest while also making possible a higher unity of collective struggle and individual freedom. Here Is Rhodes: Begin the Dance of Roses! is a political intervention: partisan, predictive, and written for those who would act.

title: Russia: il voto premia il partito di Putin ma l’analisi deve scavare tra apparenti contraddizioni
content:
“La situazione in sintesi è che abbiamo

un partito del potere che dopo oltre 4 anni di guerra migliora sensibilmente il proprio risultato ma sarebbe forse una lettura troppo semplice legare questo 58% di consensi al partito di Putin come il 58% di russi favorevoli alla prosecuzione della guerra

, secondo me sarebbe una conclusione che non ci consentirebbe di trarre poi delle analisi più profonde. ”


Da Radio Onda d’Urto


La

giornalista e attivista Daniela Galiè

, collaboratrice di Dinamo Press, Il Manifesto e altre realtà informative indipendenti è stata in agosto nella Federazione Russa ed ha avuto la possibilità di constatare come si vive in un grande paese in guerra, quali ricadute ci sono sulle condizioni di vita della popolazione, come queste influenzano l’orientamento politico. In questa articolata intervista a Radio Onda d’Urto la giornalista analizza il risultato elettorale, il panorama politico russo con i vari partiti e riporta i dati emersi dal sondaggio realizzato ad inizio settembre dall’ istituto di statistica e ricerca indipendente

Levada Center

 secondo cui

.

? I dati che abbiamo secondo me non ci consentono di trasformare troppo questa domanda in una risposta definitiva ma più che altro ci mostrano come le due cose non si escludono necessariamente;

quindi il desiderio di negoziati allo stesso tempo può anche convivere con il sostegno dichiarato alle proprie forze armate, e allo stesso tempo la preoccupazione per le condizioni materiali per l’aumento dei prezzi può convivere con il voto al partito di governo.”

author: Unknown
title: Tunç: Process must not be left at the mercy of the state
content:
Writer Aziz Tunç assessed the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that despite setbacks, disruptions and obstacles, the process was continuing. He said the main problem was that resolving the Kurdish question had not been placed at its centre.


Tunç said past experiences offered important lessons regarding the state and argued that approaching the process solely in terms of disarmament would not produce a lasting solution. He emphasised the need for all sections of society to become more actively involved in the process and said: “This process is too important and valuable to be left at the mercy of the state.”


Tunç said the process was moving forward, but not as it should, pointing to significant obstacles at every stage. He recalled that the atmosphere when the process first began had created an expectation that the issue would be resolved within a few months. Nearly two years later, however, he said the process was still moving “at idle speed”, repeatedly encountering obstacles and difficulties.


Tunç identified a fundamental mismatch between the process itself and the way it was being conducted. He said the Kurdish question was not being sufficiently discussed within a process presented as seeking to resolve it. He said, “Of course, a process discussing the resolution of the Kurdish question cannot move forward without discussing the Kurdish question itself.”


Tunç warned that the state’s tendency to approach the issue primarily through the question of disarmament could lead to further deadlock. He stressed that laying down arms alone would not eliminate the Kurdish question, which had existed before the period of armed struggle, and said its resolution could not be reduced solely to the removal of weapons.


The state should have demonstrated its reliability


Tunç said past experiences offered important lessons for the current process, particularly regarding questions over the state’s reliability.


Tunç also said: “The lesson that should have been drawn at precisely this stage was the importance of demonstrating the state’s reliability. In previous processes, the state obstructed progress, provoked events, halted the process and ultimately abandoned it midway. The first time, they used the Kurdish people’s joy at Habur as a pretext. The second time, they used the killing of two police officers as a pretext.


Using the Kurdish people’s joy as a pretext was not an innocent response. Nor was it normal. What could have been more natural than being happy about the prospect of peace? Kurds expressed and celebrated their joy. What the state should have done at the time was to embrace this pro-peace stance demonstrated by Kurds and allow that sense of joy to spread to other parts of Turkey.


Demonstrations celebrating peace could easily have been held in Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir and many other parts of Turkey. Instead, the peace process became deadlocked over the question of ‘Why were the Kurds celebrating?’, I say this ironically, but that was essentially what happened. The second time, an incident involving the killing of two police officers, which they themselves said was carried out by followers of Fethullah Gülen, was used as a pretext. The state also brought the process to a halt in one way or another when the Dolmabahçe agreement was abandoned and the negotiating table collapsed. The table was overturned and the process did not move forward. Abdullah Öcalan was placed under isolation, and the process was then frozen for ten years. They themselves said as much. President Erdoğan said at the time that they had ‘frozen the process’.”


Tunç continued: “Looking at the situation today in light of all this, the state should have adopted an approach that would overcome the mistrust created by its previous actions. Instead, it is moving in the opposite direction. The state is pursuing an approach that further deepens and fuels mistrust. That is why the process is not moving forward.


People genuinely want peace and are making every effort to achieve it. But what has accumulated in people’s memories from the past is casting a shadow of mistrust over today’s peace process. Kurds and democratic forces in particular, as well as Alevis and different sections of society, do not trust the state. The state continues to pursue policies that deepen this mistrust.”

author: Unknown
title: Memorial for Rıza Altun and Freedom Martyrs to be held in London
content:
A memorial for Rıza Altun, one of the founding members of the PKK, and the Kurdistan Freedom Martyrs will be held in London tomorrow, Sunday.


The commemoration will be held at the Haringey Kurdish Community Centre under the slogan “Şehîd Heqîqet e”. The families of the martyrs, as well as families of those whose deaths have recently been announced and whose relatives live in the UK will attend the memorial. Following the event, the families will receive condolences.


A special stage is being prepared for the commemoration, featuring photographs of Kurdistan Freedom Guerrillas whose deaths have been announced recently. Artists will perform songs in memory of the martyrs, and video presentations will also be screened.


Altun's to be highlighted


A video presentation about the life and struggle of Rıza Altun will be shown at the commemoration. A member of the founding generation of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement, Altun took on responsibilities in various fields throughout his five decades of activism, from Amed Prison to political and diplomatic work in Europe.


Rıza Altun’s death on 25 September 2019, was announced in May 2025, following the PKK’s 12th Congress.


Martyr Fîraz Dağ to be commemorated


Journalist and filmmaker Fîraz Dağ (Mehmet Aksoy) will also be commemorated on the ninth anniversary of his death.


Fîraz Dağ, who worked in journalism and filmmaking in London, travelled to Rojava in 2017. Aksoy was killed on 26 September 2017, in an ISIS attack on the press centre where he was based in Raqqa.


The memorial, which will also feature video presentations about the Kurdistan Freedom Martyrs, will begin at 3:30 p.m. on Sunday at the Haringey Kurdish Community Centre.

author: Unknown
title: KJAR: Whereabouts of Zehra Pirdehqan and Parvin Raseq Qezelbash unknown for months
content:
The Community of Free Women of Eastern Kurdistan (KJAR) holds the Islamic Republic of Iran responsible for the fate of two of its members, from whom there has been no sign of life for nearly three months. Zehra Pirdehqan (Dicle Makû) and Parvin Raseq Qezelbash (Adar Makû) were in Urmia carrying out civil society work and organizing women when they disappeared within days of each other in early July.


Zehra Pirdehqan is 32 years old and comes from Qere Êynî (Chaldiran), while Parvin Raseq Qezelbash, also 32, is from Maku. According to KJAR, the organization’s inquiries found that both women had been detained by Iranian regime forces and taken to an unknown location.


No news for nearly three months


“For nearly three months, we have received no information whatsoever about the fate or condition of our two comrades,” KJAR said on Saturday. The security authorities have refused to provide the families with any clear information about where the two women are being held or their current condition.


According to KJAR, the families are also being subjected to pressure aimed at preventing them from pursuing legal and civil society channels to determine the women’s whereabouts. This has further heightened concerns for their safety.


“We, as the Community of Free Women of Eastern Kurdistan, express our deep concern over the fate and condition of our two friends and hold the Islamic Republic of Iran responsible for protecting their lives and health,” the statement said. KJAR called for the immediate disclosure of the women’s whereabouts and condition.


Appeal to human rights and women’s organizations


In its statement on Saturday, KJAR described the case as an enforced disappearance and called on international human rights organizations, as well as women’s organizations and initiatives, not to remain silent. It urged them to follow the case and exert human rights pressure to help “bring an end to the ongoing uncertainty and the violation of their rights.”

title: Spot elektrikte işlem hacmi geriledi
content:
Duygu Ayber Gültekin [email protected]

Spot elektrik piyasasında yarın geçerli olacak fiyatlar belli oldu. Gün öncesi piyasada elektriğin megavatsaat fiyatı en yüksek 3 bin 200 lira 1 kuruş, en düşük ise 170 lira 1 kuruş olarak kaydedildi.

Enerji Piyasaları İşletme AŞ verilerine göre, spot elektrik piyasasında bugün işlem hacmi düne kıyasla yüzde 50,1 geriledi. Günlük işlem hacmi 870 milyon 586 bin 340 lira seviyesinde gerçekleşti.

Gün öncesi piyasada yarın için belirlenen fiyatlara göre megavatsaat başına en yüksek tutar 19.00'da 3 bin 200 lira 1 kuruş oldu. En düşük fiyat ise 09.00, 10.00 ve 11.00 saatlerinde 170 lira 1 kuruş olarak belirlendi.

Yarının fiyatları üzerinden hesaplanan aritmetik ortalama megavatsaat fiyatı 1.424 lira 18 kuruş olurken, ağırlıklı ortalama fiyat 1.472 lira 39 kuruş olarak açıklandı.

Öte yandan spot piyasada bugün elektriğin megavatsaat fiyatı en yüksek 4 bin 295 lira seviyesine çıktı. Günün en düşük fiyatı ise 311 lira 99 kuruş olarak kayıtlara geçti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Crowdfunding für das Film-Projekt von Labournet TV und AngryWorkers: Jeder Acker, jede Fabrik – Ideen für eine notwendige Revolution
content:
„

Art und Weise, wie wir unser Leben produzieren, ist unvernünftig, gefährlich und grausam. Es ist an der Zeit, über eine Revolution nachzudenken, die die Gesellschaft grundlegend verändert. author: Unknown
title: Cumartesi Anneleri’nin 1122’nci eylemi: 32 yıldır soruyoruz: İbrahim ve Edip Çelik nerede?
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

Cumartesi Anneleri/ İnsanları, gözaltında kaybedilenlerin yakınlarının akıbetini sormak için Galatasaray Meydanı’nda bin 122’nci eylemini gerçekleştirdi. Bu haftaki eylemde, 10 Temmuz 1994’te Batman’da Hizbullah tarafından evlerinden alınıp kaybedilen İbrahim Çelik ve oğlu Edip Çelik’in akıbeti soruldu. Cumartesi Anneleri adına basın metnini İHD İstanbul Şube Sekreteri Jiyan Kaya okudu.

Zorla kaybetmenin, sadece bir insanın yaşamdan koparılması anlamına gelmediği, geride kalanların da hayatını yıllarca sürecek bir belirsizliğe mahkûm etmek olduğunu belirten Kaya; “Cevapsız kalan sorular, sevdiklerinin nerede olduğunu, başına ne geldiğini bilmeden geçen her gün; aileler için ağır bir işkenceye dönüşür. Kayıpların akıbeti açıklanmadıkça, failler etkili biçimde soruşturulmadıkça bu işkence de sürer. Devlet, kaybedilenlerin akıbetini açıklama ve faillerden adalet önünde hesap sorma yükümlülüğünü yerine getirmediğinde, ailelerin maruz bırakıldığı belirsizlik yıllara, hatta kuşaklara yayılır. Ama kayıp yakınları bu işkencenin içinde susup kalmadı. Gözaltında kaybedilenlerin hatırasını sessizliğe karşı yükselen bir söze dönüştürdüler. Yarım bırakılan hayatların izini sürmeyi, hakikati aramayı ve adalet talebini çocuklarına, torunlarına aktardılar” dedi.

İbrahim ve Edip Çelik’in hikâyesinin 32 yıldır yerine getirilmeyen bir devlet yükümlülüğünün ve bir ailenin kuşaktan kuşağa taşıdığı adalet arayışının hikâyesi olduğun ifade eden Kaya; “50 yaşındaki İbrahim Çelik, Batman’ın Soğuksu Mezrası’nda yaşıyor ve tarımla uğraşıyordu. 1990’lı yıllarda Batman’da Hizbullah tarafından çok sayıda insan evlerinden alınarak ya da sokaklardan kaçırılarak zorla tutuldu, işkence gördü, öldürüldü ve kaybedildi. Bu ağır suçların işlendiği dönemde, güvenlik ve idari bürokrasinin koruması, desteği, göz yumması ve yol vermesiyle hareket edildiğine ilişkin çok sayıda bulgu ve tanıklık olmasına rağmen bu suçlarla etkili bir müdahale gerçekleşmedi. 10 Temmuz 1994 gecesi maskeli ve silahlı dört kişi Çelik ailesinin kapısını çaldı. İbrahim Çelik’i “yer göstereceğiz” bahanesiyle evinden alarak yanlarında götürdüler. 19 yaşındaki oğlu Edip Çelik ise babasını yalnız bırakmamak için onların peşinden gitti. Baba ve oğul eve dönmeyince aile, Jandarma ve Emniyet’e başvurdu. Ardından savcılığa suç duyurusunda bulundu. Olayla ilgili olarak Hizbullah üyeleri Talat Rüzgar, Aziz Önlük, İlhan Önlük, Resul Güneş ve Çetin Dursun’un isimlerini verdi” ifadelerini kullandı.

Yapılan başvuruların sonuçsuz bırakıldığını ve İbrahim ve Edip Çelik’ten bir daha haber alınamadığını vurgulayan Kaya şunlara söyledi; “Merese Çelik, eşi İbrahim ile oğlu Edip’in bulunması için yıllarca başvurular yaptı. Ancak bu başvurular üzerine etkili bir araştırma ve soruşturma yürütülmedi. Tanıkların dinlenmesi, şüphelilerin sorgulanması ve olayın bütün yönleriyle ortaya çıkarılması için gereken adımlar atılmadı. Merese Çelik’in arayışı, çocukları, torunları tarafından sürdürülmeye devam ediyor. Kaç yıl geçerse geçsin; İbrahim ve Edip Çelik için, tüm kayıplarımız için, adalet istemekten ve devletin hukuk normları içinde hareket etmek zorunda olduğunu hatırlatmaktan vazgeçmeyeceğiz.”

Açıklama sonrası söz alan Berfin Çelik ise şunları söyledi;

“Ben bir Cumartesi Torunuyum. 32 yıl önce gözaltında kaybedilen İbrahim Çelik ‘in torunu, Edip Çelik’in yeğeniyim.

Biz 3 kuşaktır Galatasaray’dayız. Dedemi ve dayımı arama mücadelemiz anneannem ile başladı. Sonra çocukları, şimdi de torunları ile devam ediyor.

Dedemi ve dayımı kaybedenler ailemizi de büyük bir acı içinde bıraktılar. Onların nerede olduğunu, başlarına ne geldiğini bilmemek ailemiz için ağır bir işkenceye dönüştü. Bu işkencenin sona ermesi kayıplarımıza ve adalete ulaşmamız ile mümkün.

Daha kaç kuşak bu yükü taşıyacak? Daha kaç kuşak adaletin peşinde koşacak? Biz üç kuşaktır bunu öğrenmek istiyoruz; dedem ve dayıma ne oldu? Bunu öğrenene kadar sormaya devam edeceğiz. İbrahim ve Edip Çelik’in ailesi olarak onları aramaktan vazgeçmeyeceğiz.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Chi ha parlato della fine del mondo?
content:
Riceviamo e volentieri pubblichiamo questo contributo a cura della trasmissione Stakka Stakka in onda sulle libere frequenze di

 Radio Blackout

. Buona lettura e buon ascolto!


All’inizio del mese di settembre, sul social network X è comparso un post di Jacob Coxon, ricercatore appena dimissionario dall’azienda di intelligenza artificiale Anthropic. Il testo annuncia le dimissioni e sostiene che un’intelligenza artificiale di tipo “forte” potrebbe sterminare l’umanità entro la fine del decennio. Prima di pubblicarlo, Coxon ha cancellato integralmente il proprio account. Fino a quel momento, la sua figura era sconosciuta pressoché a chiunque: nessuna pubblicazione degna di nota, nessuna presenza pubblica, nessuna copertura pregressa. Eppure, nel giro di poche ore, quell’account è diventato il centro di una discussione sulla sicurezza dell’IA che ha raggiunto i  quattro angoli del mondo.

Prima di discutere di ciò che è successo, è opportuno fornire qualche  minima coordinata sull’ambiente in cui la vicenda si inserisce.


La “sicurezza dell’IA” non è una categoria neutra, e l’ambiente che la produce lo è ancora meno. Sotto questa etichetta si muove un ecosistema formato dal

“lungotermismo”

 e dall’“altruismo efficace”: dottrine elaborate nei centri del potere tecnologico della Silicon Valley, che subordinano il presente a un futuro lontano e ipotetico, di fronte al quale sacrificare vite presenti può essere considerato perfettamente razionale. Attorno a queste dottrine si addensa un’infrastruttura completa – think tank, borse di studio, fellowship, canali di comunicazione, fondi di investimento – finanziata in larga parte dai miliardari che controllano le maggiori aziende di IA.


Su questo apparato ideologico si possono dare due letture. La prima è che essa costituisca davvero una cosmologia millenaristica: un sistema di credenze sincere, nel quale la minaccia dell’estinzione non è un espediente retorico ma una convinzione profonda, a cui proprio la vicinanza allo stato dell’arte della ricerca avvicina.

La seconda è che lo stesso apparato funzioni come una macchina: un modo di produrre valore, autorità e influenza distribuendo la paura secondo logiche di interesse ben precise. Le due letture, detto in breve, possono coesistere. E la vicenda che stiamo per raccontare è interessante proprio perché non costringe a scegliere: sul piano dei fatti tende piuttosto a

mostrare come una convinzione sincera possa essere, allo stesso tempo, uno strumento perfettamente funzionale.

Non ci pronunciamo, per ora, sulle intenzioni di Coxon.


Veniamo ai fatti. Il contatore di visualizzazioni del post di Coxon è salito con una costanza sospetta, quasi meccanica: 133,7 milioni, poi 134,6. Nonostante avesse azzerato i suoi contenuti, ha superato i duecentomila follower nel giro di poche ore. Per dare un’idea della

sproporzione: quando Ilya Sutskever – cofondatore di OpenAI – ha annunciato la propria partenza, la sua comunicazione ha totalizzato sei milioni di visualizzazioni. Qui parliamo di più di venti volte tanto, per un uomo di cui nessuno aveva sentito parlare ventiquattro ore prima.


Ancora più istruttiva è la sequenza temporale. Entro quindici minuti dalla pubblicazione, tre account rispondono al post. Nathan Calvin, consulente legale di Encode AI, in 6 minuti e 6 secondi; Daniel Kokotajlo, direttore dell’AI Futures Project, in 9 minuti e 54 secondi; Peter Wildeford, responsabile di policy dell’AI Policy Network, il quale si presenta addirittura con un articolo del Wall Street Journal già in mano. L’articolo è stato pubblicato alle 19:46: diciotto minuti prima che lo stesso tweet di dimissioni andasse online, alle 20:04. L’esclusiva giornalistica ha preceduto l’evento di cui doveva riferire

versione archiviata del WSJ

.

Non solo hanno risposto tempestivamente ad un account senza alcuna visibilità pregressa, ma il Wall Street Journal aveva anche un’esclusiva già pronta che citava le parole esatte del ricercatore, cosa che fa pensare fa pensare ad un’efficiente campagna di influenza.


Infatti questi tre account non sarebbero stati scelti a caso: tutti appartengono al mondo della “sicurezza IA” che fanno advocacy sul “rischio esistenziale” dell’AI. E tutte e tre le organizzazioni condividono un medesimo benefattore: il Survival and Flourishing Fund, guidato da Jaan Tallinn – uno dei principali investitori e membro del consiglio esterno di Anthropic, l’azienda che Coxon ha appena lasciato. title: Far and away, the best accessibility aid is money. It’s money. Money to get the insurance and pay…
content:
Far and away, the best accessibility aid is money. It’s money. Money to get the insurance and pay rent and medical bills and get mobility aids insurance refuses to cover. Ubers to doctor’s appointments, specialist copays, PCP copays, ER bills, ambulance bills, surgery bills, etc etc etc. Disabled people on benefits in America live in enforced poverty. It’s miserable. People are dying from their disabilities solely because they cannot afford the medical care they need.

Being disabled is expensive. So damn fucking expensive.

And it’s utterly infuriating, because it shouldn’t be this costly to stay alive.

title: Verleihung der BigBrotherAwards 2026 am 25. September in Bielefeld und online
content:
Die BigBrotherAwards sind die „Oscars für Überwachung”, seit 2000 organisiert durch Digitalcourage e. V. in Zusammenarbeit mit Kooperationspartnern. Vergeben wird der Negativ-Preis alljährlich an Firmen, Organisationen und Personen, die auf besonders übergriffige Weise die Privatsphäre von Menschen beeinträchtigen und persönliche Daten verkaufen oder gegen ursprüngliche Interessen verwenden. Mit ihnen werden jedes Jahr Datensünder in Wirtschaft und Politik ausgezeichnet. Die Verleihung der diesjährigen 26. BigBrotherAwards findet am 25.09.2026 (Freitag), ab 18:00 Uhr im Rahmen eines Gala-Abends in der Hechelei im Ravensberger Park in Bielefeld statt. Die gesamte Veranstaltung wird außerdem als Livestream auf der Website

https://bigbrotherawards.de


 übertragen. Siehe für mehr Vorabinformationen die

Pressemitteilung vom 3.08.2026 bei Digitalcourage e. V.

Fielmann und Apollo Optik normalisieren heimliches Filmen und Abhören – und verdienen Geld an der Stalkerware

Infos und Laudatio

Artikel von Jette Scheibchen vom 25. September 2026 in Netzpolitik

title: Özgür Özel Gaziemir'de YENİ Parti'nin üye sayısını açıkladı
content:
YENİ Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel, partisinin Gaziemir İlçe Başkanlığı ön seçimlerine katıldı ve açıklama yaptı.


Konuşmasında Türkiye'nin değişime ihtiyacı olduğunu vurgulayan Özel, partinin üye sayısını paylaşarak makam sınırlamaları ve iktidar hedefiyle ilgili net mesajlar verdi.


Konuşmasına Türkiye siyasetinin mevcut durumuna değinerek başlayan Özgür Özel, şöyle dedi:


"Artık Türkiye’nin yepyeni bir enerjiye ihtiyacı var. Genç bir siyasete ihtiyacı var. Her yaştan, 10’uncu Yıl Nutku'nda olduğu gibi her yaştan gençlere ihtiyacı var, tertemiz bir sayfaya ihtiyacı var. Türkiye’nin yeni bir başlangıca ihtiyacı var.


Partimizi millet kurmuştur, adını millet koymuştur. Bütçesini, bağışlarıyla ödediği aidatlarla milletimiz oluşturmaktadır. Arkamızdaki yegane gücümüz milletimizdir. Karşımızdakiler ne yaparlarsa yapsınlar, hangi kumpaslara başvurursa başvursunlar milletin üzerinde bir güç tanımadık, tanımayacağız. Buradan, Gaziemir‘den tüm Türkiye’ye sesleniyorum; eskinin, eskimişin, yaşlanmışın devri geride kalmıştır. Yeni siyaset iktidara yürümektedir."


Partisinin örgütlenme süreci hakkında da bilgi veren Özel, YENİ Parti'nin üye sayısının 723 bine ulaştığını, 81 il ve 870 ilçede örgütlenmelerini tamamladıklarını belirtti.


"Büyük bir sosyal patlama görüyorum"


Ankara'daki emekli eylemi sırasında hayatına son veren emekli polis memuru Ali Şekeroğlu'nu hatırlatan Özel, ekonomik sıkıntılara ve toplumsal tepkiye dikkat çekti:


"Burada içimizdeki büyük acıyı bir kez daha buradan ifade etmek isterim. Dün emekliler, yıllar önce kendilerine verilmeyen seyyanen zammın Anayasa Mahkemesi’ndeki görüşmesi sırasında orada eylem yaparken bir emekli polis memuru Ali Şekeroğlu ‘Para değil, onurumuzu istiyoruz’ diyerek yıllarca devletin kendine emanet ettiği, hepimizin canını malını koruduğu beylik silahıyla maalesef hayatına son verdi.


Her yaptığımız mitingte şunu söylüyorum; ‘Emeklilerin gözündeki öfkeyi, emeklilerin gözündeki hayal kırıklığını görüyorum. Bir büyük sosyal patlamayı görüyorum. Ve buna önlem almak gerekir’ diye yıllardır söylüyoruz. Maalesef dün yaşanan acı olayı, o acıyı kalbimize gömüp tekrarının olmasından korkup, tekrarının olmaması için Allah’a dua edip bir yandan da bu iktidara şunu söylüyoruz: Bu kadar kötülük, bu kadar haksızlık, bu kadar eşitsizlik, bu kadar vefasızlık, bu emeklilerin hiçbirine reva değildir. Eninde sonunda AK Parti’nin kara düzenini yerle bir edeceğiz, emeklilerimiz için yepyeni bir düzen kuracağız."


"Partiyi iktidar yapamazsam görevi bırakırım"


Makamların geçici olduğunu ve parti içinde dönem sınırlaması getireceklerini vurgulayan Özel, kendi görev süresiyle ilgili de iddialı konuştu:


"Makamların emanet sayıldığı bir düzen kuracağız. Kimse oturduğu koltuğa kök salmayacak. Her görevde dönem sınırlaması olacak. Milletvekilliğinde de, belediye başkanlığında da, parti yöneticiliğinde de. İki dönem - üç dönem kuralı geldiğinde koltuktaki gidecek ve yerine yenisi, daha yenisi, en yenisi gelecek.


Bu iki dönem ya da üç dönem kuralından milletvekili olarak ya da parti yöneticisi olarak bu kurala tabii olmayan bir kişi var. O da benim. Başka bir kurala tabiyim: Tek dönem kuralı. Eğer girdiğimiz herhangi bir seçimde partiyi iktidar yapmaz, birinci parti yapmazsam o gün görevi bırakacağım, o gün görevi bırakacağım."


(EMK)

author: Unknown
title: La morte del lavoro
content:
Oggi scrivere dell’omicidio sul lavoro di Andrea Moretti, operaio rocciatore, non è facile.


Nel farlo esprimiamo la nostra vicinanza ai suoi colleghi e familiari. In questo paese sul lavoro muoiono in media 3 persone al giorno. Una statistica mostruosa che cela il più grande rimosso di questo Paese inebetito e fermo: le condizioni dei lavoratori e delle lavoratrici. Raramente questi fatti “fanno notizia”, si legga: interessano ai padroni e magnati che possiedono in poche mani la stragrande maggioranza dei giornali e telegiornali italiani. Ma per le persone a cui erano legati, per i territori in cui abitavano, queste “notizie” pesano come macigni e sono all’ordine del giorno. 


Chi muore di lavoro ha tutte le età e le cause sono quasi sempre le stesse: mancanza di dispositivi di sicurezza, orari esasperanti, stanchezza, imprevisti, avarizia del padrone o padroncino di turno che ha risparmiato sui materiali eccetera eccetera. Ed è così a prescindere da questo caso in particolare su cui speriamo si arrivi a fare chiarezza.


Questa volta però è successo in un posto “speciale”, il Colosseo, e questo ha determinato una canea mediatica e lo sciacallaggio di politicanti di ogni risma. Perché, in un giorno a caso della settimana scorsa, non si sono accalcati in un altro posto della penisola per un altro lavoratore morto in circostanze simili? Perché sono principalmente degli ipocriti, che non si fanno scrupoli ad usare la morte di un ragazzo per mettersi in mostra. Si, ma non solo. Andrea è morto sul loro palcoscenico, in centro alla Capitale, e allora non si può permettere che qualche sindacato confederale, venduto quanto loro, possa dire che non gliene importi. E allora si scrivano profluvi di inchiostro andando ad indagare fino all’ultimo dettaglio: la biografia, la tragedia, il dolore devono essere spettacolarizzati perché migliaia di altri morti rimangano nascosti, senza nome. 


I giornali padronali ci devono pure deliziare con articoli che descrivono l’antica origine del

mazzetto di fiori

 che quel mentecatto del ministro Giuli ha portato in dono, a favor di telecamera, al defunto. Da persone comuni che hanno passato, nostro malgrado, la vita a lavorare e a sentire decine di storie di morti e infortuni, abbiamo la nausea. Ci consola solo il fatto che magari questa esposizione mediatica possa portare qualche tipo di “giustizia” alla famiglia. Poi sfilano i sindacalisti  confederali che, in giacca e cravatta, si mettono in mostra senza neanche degnarsi di indicare le vere cause di tutti questi incidenti. Ma come si fa a prendere sul serio chi molto probabilmente non si fa un turno di lavoro da 20 anni o più, e che sta lì perché deve tutelare il suo stipendio da sindacalista?


Il giorno dopo, o quello dopo ancora, tutto sparisce e si viene dimenticati dai giornali. Tutto torna nella opprimente normalità. 


Il problema enorme da affrontare sono le condizioni in cui lavoriamo e la rispettiva paga. I salari nel nostro paese sono il margine di profitto maggiore per le aziende. Sui salari si scarica tutto: crisi, incapacità di sopravvivere nel mercato globalizzato, i benefit per i manager. Ora ci dicono pure di voler spostare ancora l’età pensionabile, perché anche la pensione è salario, stipendio, paga.


Ma cosa c’è dietro quei soldi? Dietro quelli che ci mettono in busta paga e dietro quelli delle trattenute che dovrebbero pagare i servizi essenziali. Ci sono le nostre vite, soprattutto i nostri interessi, le nostre capacità di realizzarci come persone. Se i soldi non bastano allora siamo infelici e fatichiamo ad arrivare alla fine del mese, ci stressiamo, ci auto sfruttiamo con un altro lavoretto extra. Ma quei soldi rappresentano un doppio ricatto e un doppio potere. Sono il ricatto di monetizzare quello che sappiamo fare e di imprigionarlo in mansioni spesso ripetitive e che non ci appartengono più, che realizziamo per qualcun altro, per fini non nostri. Sono il ricatto per tenerci attaccati agli interessi di qualcun altro, altrimenti non mangiamo e consumiamo. Hanno il potere però di essere un costo ineludibile per le aziende: senza stipendio, per quanto misero, niente lavoro e quindi niente profitto. Lo stipendio ha il potere di aumentare a parità di lavoro messo in campo dai lavoratori, anche se non ci crediamo quasi più. Nulla lega i soldi alla nostra mansione, a parte le lacrime di chi si divide i profitti aziendali, all’attività concreta che svolgiamo.


Il lavoro è l’insieme di tutto questo: è una catena …

author: Extremadura Libre
title: Ya está en la calle el nº 37 de Extremadura Libre.
content:
El número 37 de

Extremadura Libre

 ya está en la calle. Una nueva edición de nuestro periódico que vuelve a poner sobre la mesa las luchas, los problemas y las preocupaciones que atraviesan a la clase trabajadora, pero también nuestra historia y nuestra cultura.


En sus páginas hablamos de

acción sindical y organización en los centros de trabajo

, de la importancia de las secciones sindicales y de la autonomía de quienes trabajan para decidir sobre sus propias luchas. También nos acercamos a conflictos concretos, como el de

las trabajadoras y trabajadores de la campaña de la cereza

, marcado por la precariedad, o la situación laboral en el

CIIAE

.


El periódico dedica también espacio a la lucha por el

indulto de las seis personas del caso de La Suiza

, perseguidas por hacer sindicalismo, y a otros conflictos sociales que nos recuerdan que

son las trabajadoras y los trabajadores quienes siguen pagando un precio demasiado alto por defender sus derechos

.


El

feminismo

 también está presente en este número, con un artículo que aborda las desigualdades y las luchas de las mujeres desde una perspectiva vinculada a la realidad de la clase trabajadora. Porque la explotación y la discriminación no desaparecen por decreto, por mucho que algunos discursos institucionales se empeñen en anunciar lo contrario.


La

memoria histórica

 ocupa un lugar destacado en este número, con artículos que recuperan nuestra historia y cuestionan la permanencia de los símbolos del franquismo. También hablamos de vivienda, territorio, condiciones laborales y de los efectos que están teniendo los nuevos modelos energéticos sobre nuestras vidas y nuestros pueblos.


No falta la cultura. En este número encontramos una entrevista con

Antonio Salas «Tonio»

, en la que hablamos de flamenco y de cultura popular, además de otros contenidos dedicados a la literatura, el pensamiento libertario y la recuperación de nuestra memoria militante.


El

90 aniversario de la Revolución Social de 1936

 sirve también como hilo conductor de este número. No para convertir aquella experiencia en una pieza de museo, sino para recordar que hubo trabajadores y trabajadoras que intentaron construir una sociedad diferente y que muchas de las preguntas que entonces se plantearon siguen estando encima de la mesa.


Todo esto y mucho más puede encontrarse en las páginas del nº 37 de

Extremadura Libre

, una publicación hecha desde CNT y pensada para quienes trabajan, se organizan y no se resignan a que otros decidan por ellos.


La edición en papel está disponible

en todos los sindicatos de CNT Extremadura

. También puedes descargarla en PDF desde la web de CNT Extremadura:


https://extremadura.cnt.es


Porque un periódico como este tiene sentido cuando se lee, se comparte y circula de mano en mano.


La entrada

Ya está en la calle el nº 37 de Extremadura Libre.

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Perseus
title: Πρώτη δημόσια επιστολή του συντρόφου Θύμιου Α., προφυλακισμένου για τη σκευωρία της Μαρφίν Vol 3
content:
Πρώτη δημόσια επιστολή του συντρόφου Θύμιου Α., προφυλακισμένου για τη σκευωρία της Μαρφίν Vol 3


1η ΔΗΜΟΣΙΑ ΕΠΙΣΤΟΛΗ ΤΟΥ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΟΥ ΘΥΜΙΟΥ Α.,


ΠΡΟΦΥΛΑΚΙΣΜΕΝΟΥ ΓΙΑ ΤΗΝ ΣΚΕΥΩΡΙΑ ΤΗΣ

MARFIN


vol

3


(…) όνοι παιδαγωγοί κι εθνοπατέρες,


κροκόδειλοι που κάνουν τους σωτήρες,


ο Ηγέτης, το τσακάλι, ο εργολάβος


του μέλλοντος, το ένστολο γουρούνι,


ο υιός ο εκλεκτός της Εκκλησίας


που πλένει μ’ αγιασμό τα μαύρα δόντια


κι ακούει μαθήματα αγγλικών κατ’ οίκον


ή και δημοκρατίας, αθέατοι τοίχοι


και σάπιες προσωπίδες που χωρίζουν


τον άνθρωπο απ’ τους άλλους τους ανθρώπους,


τον άνθρωπο απ’ τον ίδιο,


καταρρέουν (…)


Οκτάβιο Πας, Ηλιόπετρα


Προσπαθώ να σπάσω το μονοπώλιο της «αλήθειας» των ισχυρών, πλακωμένος κάτω από τόνους «λάσπης», πίστομα και έγκλειστος πια στον τσιμεντένιο τάφο, τη φυλακή, υπό την σκιά της δυστοπίας που τώρα ονομάζουνε «ζωή». Γιατί μια παρασκευιάτικη πρωία (10/7/26) έξω από το σπίτι μου και ενώ κατευθυνόμουν στη δουλειά, απήχθην από τους έμμισθους δολοφόνους χωρίς εξηγήσεις. Μου έτυχε ο κλήρος να κατηγορούμαι για το θλιβερό γεγονός στην

Marfin

 το 2010 που στοίχισε τη ζωή σε 3 συνανθρώπους μας. Μου έλαχε να συγκαταλέγομαι στην 3η κατά σειρά ομάδα κατηγορουμένων γι’ αυτό το θλιβερό γεγονός, που όπως έμαθα στη συνέχεια, στη «λίστα» αυτή βρίσκεται ο σύντροφος Κώστας αλλά και η συντρόφισσα Ελένη. Για 3η φορά, οι κάθε λογής δημαγωγοί και Κλουζώ χτίζουν καριερίτσα και με την ίδια αδιαμφισβήτητη σιγουριά, διαπομπεύουν εμάς και τους οικείους μας. Γι’ αυτούς δεν έχουν σημασία τα πρόσωπα αλλά η πολιτική εκμετάλλευση της υπόθεσης.


Και στοιχεία; Ποια στοιχεία; Χρειάζονται; Αρκούσε η περατζάδα του υπουργού δημοσίας τάξης, Χρυσοχοϊδη στα κανάλια και οι δηλώσεις περί «δεμένης υπόθεσης», η τροφοδοσία των «αδέκαστων» δημοσιογράφων με κατασκευασμένα «στοιχεία» και οι ανακριτές άρχισαν να εκτυπώνουν τα εντάλματα σύλληψης. Και αφού μας προ-δίκασαν στα τηλεδικεία τους, ήταν αρκετό ένα ανορθόγραφο ανώνυμο

mail

-τσαπατσουλιά που συντάχθηκε μέσα στο υπουργείο δημόσιας τάξης που στους δήθεν «δράστες» περιλαμβάνει και κάποιον που την εποχή εκείνη ήταν φυλακισμένος…


Ακόμα και σήμερα, την έλλειψη και της παραμικρής ένδειξης εναντίον μου προσπαθούν να την υποκαταστήσουν με την «σύνθεση του εγκληματικού προφίλ μου». Σκανάρουν

pixel

 το

pixel

 κάθε πτυχή της ζωής μου για να παράγουν «υποψίες» από καθημερινές συμπεριφορές, φωτογραφίες διακοπών και αναμνήσεις μου, καθημερινά ρούχα, μετακινήσεις και σχέσεις μου. Αυτή την φορά πρέπει να εξαπατήσουν την κοινή γνώμη ότι «έχουν ενόχους»…


Όλη μου τη ζωή δεν κρύβομαι. Αντίθετα, κατοικώ, εργάζομαι και αγωνίζομαι ανοιχτά και συλλογικά στην Αθήνα. Από που κι ως που κρίνομαι ύποπτος φυγής και τέλεσης ίδιων αδικημάτων; Τελικά ήταν αρκετά αυτά τα «αδιάσειστα στοιχεία» για να μας προφυλακίσουν. Αλλά ποιος νοιάζεται;


16 χρόνια μετά, δεν μου ζητήθηκε καν να δώσω εξηγήσεις, να καταθέσω. Με πετάξανε στην αθλιότητα των κρατητηρίων της ΓΑΔΑ, χωρίς καμία δυνατότητα να υπερασπιστώ τον εαυτό μου. 16 χρόνια μετά καλούμαι να αποδείξω ότι δεν είμαι ελέφαντας.


Ας τα πάρουμε, όμως, από την αρχή. 16 χρόνια πίσω, την 5η Μάη του 2010 ψηφίστηκε το 1ο μνημόνιο από τους νεοαποικιοποιημένους πολιτικούς-τεχνοκράτες-ειδικούς. Βάλθηκαν να σώσουν τα «σπασμένα» της κλίκας του Επστάιν και του χρέους των ΗΠΑ μετά το σκάσιμο της χρηματοπιστωτικής φούσκας του 2008. Μια γνωστή πρακτική αρπαγής, λεηλασίας και ιδιοποίησης που εφαρμόζεται από την στρατιωτική επιβολή της αστυνομίας και των φασιστών και την «κατά βούληση» δημαγωγία των ΜΜΕ. Με τα γνωστά αποτελέσματα: την κατάλυση κάθε συλλογικού δικαιώματος και κοινωνικής ελευθερίας, την φτωχοποίηση των μεσαίων και χαμηλών κοινωνικών στρωμάτων και την παράλληλη απότομη συσσώρευση πλούτου και εξουσίας στα χέρια ντόπιων και διεθνών αρπακτικών με γραβάτες.


Την ψήφιση του 1ου μνημονίου, όπως ήταν αναμενόμενο, διαδέχτηκε το κάλεσμα απεργίας που ανέλπιστα αποτέλεσε την μεγαλύτερη μεταπολιτευτική διαδήλωση. Πάνω από μισό εκατομμύριο πολίτες κατέκλυσαν τους δρόμους σ’ όλη τη χώρα. Ένα διαταξικό και διαπολιτικό πλήθος εξέφρασε με τη διάχυτη οργή του την αντίθεση στις κρατικές πολιτικές. Εκεί βρισκόταν και ο αναρχικός/αντιεξουσιαστικός χώρος με συνέπεια, σε συνέχεια ενός ψηφιδωτού αυτοοργανωμένων εγχειρημάτων που πολλαπλασιάζονταν ταχύτατα, ως αναπόσπαστο κομμάτι του συλλογικού αναχώματος στην επίθεση που δεχόμασταν.


Συνεπής στα καθήκοντά της ήταν και η πολιτική ελίτ όπως ο τότε βουλευτής, και νυν υπουργός δημόσιας τάξης, Μιχάλης Χρυσοχοϊδης. Αυτός που …

author: Perseus
title: Πρώτη δημόσια τοποθέτηση του συντρόφου Κώστα για την προφυλάκιση του για την υπόθεση της Μαρφίν Vol 3
content:
Πρώτη δημόσια τοποθέτηση του συντρόφου Κώστα για την προφυλάκιση του για την υπόθεση της Μαρφιν Vol 3


Παρασκευή 10/07 βγαίνω από το σπίτι για να πάω στην δουλειά. Χαιδεύω τον σκύλο μας και μπαίνω στο αμάξι μου. Ξαφνικά ακούγονται φρεναρίσματα. Κουκουλοφόροι με αρπάζουν φωνάζοντας “Αστυνομία”. Με βάζουν σε συμβατικό αμάξι, με προσταγή “το κεφάλι κάτω”. Τους ρωτάω που με πηγαίνουν, “θα μάθεις σε λίγο” μου απαντούν. Φτάνω στον 11

ο

 όροφο της ΓΑΔΑ. Με βάζουν σε ένα δωμάτιο φρουρούμενο. Σε λίγο εμφανίζεται κάποιος με πολιτικά και μου δίνει ένα ένταλμα σύλληψης. Κατηγορούμαι μαζί με άλλα άτομα για τον εμπρησμό της

Μαρφίν

 το 2010. Χάνω την γη κάτω από τα πόδια μου. Κατηγορούμενος είναι και ο φίλος μου ο Θύμιος καθώς και μία συντρόφισσα η Ελένη. Οι σκέψεις μου μαυρίζουν. Δεν μπορώ να διανοηθώ ότι η μπίλια αυτή την φορά έκατσε σε εμένα…


Οδηγούμαι στα κρατητήρια. Κάθε δύο μέρες περίπου, σε αυτές τις 11 μέρες της κράτησης μου, με οδηγούν στο γραφείο του αρχηγού (μάλλον…) των Ανθρωποκτονιών για “φιλική συζήτηση”. Μου ζητούν να υποδείξω ποιοι πέταξαν τις μολότοφ στην τράπεζα για να ελαφρύνω την θέση μου. Η άγνοια μου είναι η μόνη απάντηση που παίρνουν. Οι αφηγήσεις άλλων συντρόφων που έπεσαν στα χέρια τους στο παρελθόν ήταν αρκετές για να γνωρίζω αυτές τις πρακτικές τους και η επικοινωνία από το καρτοτηλέφωνο των κρατητηρίων, μαζί με τις επισκέψεις των δικών μου ανθρώπων, μου έδωσε δύναμη να αντέξω, πνευματικά και ψυχικά.


Στην συνέχεια, δικαστήρια, ανακριτής, εισαγγελέας. Τελευταίες γρήγορες ματιές δύναμης και αλληλεγγύης με τους ανθρώπους μου και τους συντρόφους μου που βρίσκονταν απ’ έξω. Τελικά, μεταγωγή στις φυλακές Μαλανδρίνου. Οι πόρτες κλείνουν και ο εγκλεισμός ξεκινάει.


Ήμουν, είμαι και θα είμαι στο πλευρό των αγωνιζόμενων ανθρώπων, γιατί πάντα ονειρευόμουν έναν διαφορετικό κόσμο, δομημένο με τις αρχές της ισότητας και της αλληλεγγύης, μακριά από τις λογικές της εκμετάλλευσης ανθρώπου από άνθρωπο, ενάντια σε εξουσιαστικές και ιεραρχικές λογικές. Έγινα κομμάτι της πολιτικής διαδρομής που χαράσσει δεκαετίες τώρα ο χώρος της αντεξουσίας και έχει μόνιμη παρουσίασε όλα τα κοινωνικά κινήματα που αναπτύσσονται ενάντια στην καπιταλιστική-κρατική βαρβαρότητα. Ο πόλεμος των κρατών απέναντι στους ανθρώπους είναι ανυποχώρητος και συνεχής. Από τις δολοφονίες μεταναστών στα σύνορα και τα στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης, από τις εργασιακές γαλέρες και τα εργατικά “ατυχήματα”, από τους ιμπεριαλιστικούς πολέμους και τα πυρηνικά τους εργοστάσια, από την καταστροφή του περιβάλλοντος και ολόκληρων περιοχών για τα κέρδη τους, από τις μίζες και τα υπόγεια αλισβερίσια τους, είναι ξεκάθαρο ότι αυτοί κρατούν το μονοπώλιο της βίας. Της βίας που θυμούνται να στηλιτεύουν και να λοιδορούν όταν ασκείται από τους καταπιεσμένους ως αυτοάμυνα. Για αυτό ο α/α χώρος βρίσκεται συνεχώς στο στόχαστρό τους. Γιατί είναι ένα από τα κοινωνικά κινήματα που στις κρίσιμες στιγμές για την κοινωνία, αναδεικνύει όλη αυτή την συστημική και καθημερινή βία του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου. Ο α/α χώρος στέκεται ανάχωμα μακριά από λογικές ανάθεσης και πολιτικής κεφαλαιοποίησης, ώστε να ανακόψει την ολική αποδιάρθρωση του κοινωνικού συνόλου.


Την 5/5 του 2010 η κοινωνία βρισκόταν σε αναβρασμό, η χρεωκοπία των τραπεζών και της χώρας ήταν προ των πυλών. Εκατομμύρια κόσμου διαδήλωσαν σε όλη την χώρα. Στην Αθήνα, η συμμετοχή στην διαδήλωση-απεργία ήταν τεράστια και η δυναμική οργή του πλήθους, άνευ προηγουμένου. Στην διάρκεια της διαδήλωσης τρεις άνθρωποι της τάξης μας έχασαν άδικα την ζωή τους, γεγονός που προκάλεσε πένθος σε ολόκληρη την κοινωνία. Το τραγικό γεγονός του θανάτου αυτών των εργαζομένων αποτέλεσε φρένο στην κοινωνική οργή. Οι εργαζόμενοι της τράπεζας ήταν κλειδωμένοι μέσα στο κτίριο, μία μέρα που όλα υπολειτουργούσαν. Η οργή του κόσμου είχε δυναμιτιστεί από τις προκλητικές δηλώσεις του πρωθυπουργού και των κυβερνητικών στελεχών της περιόδου. Κανένας Βγενόπουλος

,

κανένας διευθυντής, καμία αστυνομία δεν ενδιαφέρθηκε για αυτούς. Καμία δικαιοσύνη δεν έβαλε στην φυλακή κανέναν υπεύθυνο της τράπεζας για τις ελλείψεις μέτρων ασφαλείας, καμία αστυνομία δεν εισέβαλε στα σπίτια τους, κανένας δημοσιογράφος δεν διαπόμπευσε δημόσια αυτούς και τα οικεία τους πρόσωπα με απευθείας συνδέσεις από τα σπίτια των οικογενειών τους. Αυτό που κάνουν από την πρώτη στιγμή, είναι να στοχοποιούν και να σέρνουν στα δικαστήρια άτομα από τον α/α χώρο. Λες και αυτοί είναι οι μόνοι που οργανώνονται και διαδηλώνουν, οι μόνοι που εκφράζουν δημόσια την οργή και την αγανάκτηση τους στους …

author: Unknown
title: Mother seeks answers for 29 years
content:
Almost every household in Kurdistan carries memories shaped by the loss of loved ones, massacres, detentions and arrests. Some witnessed the killing of a loved one, some the disappearance of a sibling, some the arrest and torture of their mother, and others the death of their child. Even as the years pass, these stories are remembered anew every day in the lives of those left behind.


At a time when peace is once again on the agenda, the people of Kurdistan are demanding that the pain of the past be confronted and that similar losses never happen again. Yet for thousands of families, the past still means a search that has never reached a conclusion.


One of these families is that of Dilber Eren, a relative of the disappeared who has been trying for 29 years to learn the fate of her son and daughter-in-law. Dilber Eren has been searching for traces of her relatives ever since her son Orhan Eren and daughter-in-law Zozan Eren disappeared and were never heard from again.


Dilber Eren’s search is not limited to her struggle to learn the fate of her missing loved ones. For 29 years, she has held on to the hope that her son might one day return, repeatedly going to his home to check whether he has come back.


Her story is also part of the pain experienced by thousands of families in Kurdistan who have spent years seeking truth and justice for their missing loved ones.


Nurse Zozan Eren and her husband Orhan Eren disappeared on 25 September 1997 after setting out from Lice (Licê), a district of Diyarbakır (Amed), for Kulp (Pasur). The couple’s vehicle was found about 50 metres from the Angül Gendarmerie Station. Despite the discovery of their vehicle, Zozan and Orhan Eren were never heard from again.


Before the couple disappeared, Zozan Eren was reportedly summoned to the office of the Kulp district governor and asked to request a transfer out of the district. Two police officers working at the district governor’s office reportedly told her, “You are sending medicine to PKK members, so you have to leave.”


Pembe Toprak, who had received no news from her daughter and son-in-law, attempted to file a report at the Kulp Gendarmerie Station on 26 September. However, officers at the station refused to accept her application on the grounds that it was a holiday and told her to return on Monday. Pembe Toprak applied to the Kulp Prosecutor’s Office on Monday and reported the situation. The prosecutor reportedly called the gendarmerie station in the area where the incident occurred in an attempt to obtain information.


The station reportedly informed the prosecutor’s office that Zozan and Orhan Eren had been abducted by the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).


After exhausting domestic legal remedies without obtaining a result, the family took the case to the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR). On 21 February 2005, the ECtHR found Turkey responsible for a violation of the right to life.


Later, relatives of brothers Sadık and Seyithan Ulusmaskan, who disappeared in custody, reportedly said that while investigating the fate of their own missing relatives, they had heard from members of the Gendarmerie Intelligence and Counter-Terrorism Unit (JİTEM) that Zozan and Orhan Eren had been held in custody.


However, no information has been obtained about the fate of Zozan and Orhan Eren since their disappearance on 25 September 1997.


Grave claim was not investigated


Years later, a burial site was reportedly identified in an area close to where the couple’s vehicle had been found. Following an application by the lawyers, the prosecutor’s office initially accepted the request, but later did not conduct an inspection of the site said to contain graves, citing “security” concerns.


Following this development in 2014, the investigation file was transferred from the then Specially Authorized Diyarbakır Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office to the Lice Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office, where the case file reportedly remains.


Their children grew up longing for them


Dilber Eren, one of thousands of relatives of the disappeared, has spent years trying to learn what happened to her son and daughter-in-law. She said they had found neither any record showing that the couple had been detained nor their names on any grave, and had been unable to obtain a single piece of information about their fate. Eren added that the couple’s two daughters grew up without either their father or their mother.


After years of turning everywhere she could …

author: Unknown
title: Others tried to decide her life, but Beyan Ferec chose her own path
content:
1 January 2000 marked a turning point in Beyan Ferec’s life. That day, her husband, Bekir Abdülkerim Abdullah, left home to go to his shop in Halabja. Beyan recalled that before leaving, Bekir mentioned an elderly and impoverished man whose television had broken down. He said he would give the man a new television because he did not want him to enter the new year without one.


Around ten minutes later, the sound of an explosion from the shop changed Beyan Ferec’s life. Beyan recalled going to the shop with her mother-in-law and others who were at home, only to find the building completely destroyed. According to her account, an explosive device planted inside a television in the shop detonated, and Bekir was martyred at the scene. Beyan had only recently turned 27.


Forced into marriage at 16


Beyan was born in 1974 in the Necîbek neighbourhood of Sulaymaniyah. She said her family had been kept under surveillance because of their political activities during the Baath regime, preventing her from continuing her education as a child.


Beyan attended school until the sixth grade and said her father had forced her to marry at the age of 16. She married her cousin Bekir in 1990, and they had four children, two daughters and two sons.


The family lived for a time in Darbandikhan. Beyan said they later returned to Sulaymaniyah because of war and displacement along the Shahrazur and Garmian border areas during the 1990s.


Bekir was an electrical engineer but was unable to practise his profession officially. He instead opened a repair shop in Sulaymaniyah’s Necîbek neighbourhood. Beyan said a change in Bekir’s life began after he met several people who visited his shop. She recalled that Bekir was influenced by the way they spoke and conducted themselves, and that after some time they told him they were affiliated with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK).


Bekir subsequently began working with PKK members, Beyan said, and their home gradually became one of the places where they would meet. She recalled that her husband became increasingly involved in political and social activities and devoted himself to serving his people.


She stood by her husband despite the pressure


Beyan said Bekir moved to Halabja in 1994, where he became involved in press activities. She recalled that he was detained several times by the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) because of his activities and spent time in prison.


Beyan said she also faced pressure from those around her during this period. She recalled being warned that “if you are associated with the PKK, your family and children will suffer,” but said she nevertheless stood by her husband. The news of the explosion on 1 January 2000 irreversibly changed the life of the family.


After her husband’s martyrdom


One of the greatest difficulties Beyan faced after Bekir’s martyrdom was the attitude of his family towards her children. Beyan said Bekir’s family wanted to take the children away from her and force her out of the house. She recalled being told that she either had to marry another member of the family or leave the home.


Beyan said her mother provided her greatest support during this period, telling her: “I will not allow a woman with four children to be oppressed.” Beyan said that for around five years after her husband’s martyrdom, she did not know how to rebuild her life. She eventually began working and, over time, was able to buy her own home and car.


Three of her four children were now married, while one still lived with her.


She rebuilt her own life


Beyan Ferec said she stayed away from political and social activities for a period after her husband’s martyrdom, but joined the work of the Kurdistan Democratic Solution Party (PÇDK) in 2004.


Beyan followed in her husband’s footsteps while also working to raise her children and achieve economic independence. She eventually established her own business. She has been running a plant nursery for around 17 years. Today, she spends much of her day at the nursery, working, tending the grounds and caring for the plants.


For Beyan, the nursery is more than simply a means of earning a living. It is also an important part of the life she rebuilt through her own efforts after her husband’s martyrdom. Beyan said, “I can’t imagine being without my shop.” Her children have now built lives of their own, and Beyan said she still had the strength to continue working.


‘Women must be able to build their own lives’

author: Unknown
title: Psychologists: Tests not in mother tongue label children
content:
The second session of the congress organised by the Mesopotamia Psychologists Association (DER-MEZ) in Amed (Diyarbakır) under the slogan “Human psychology should be understood through language and identity” focused on “Testing and therapy in psychological practice” and “The role of the mother tongue in the construction and denial of identity”.


As reported by Mezopotamya Agency (MA), psychologist Emel Izgi Demir said psychometric tests took shape in response to the needs of the Industrial Revolution and the capitalist system in the 19th century. She said these tools were fundamentally designed to control, classify and filter populations and fit people into predetermined categories. Demir also pointed to the historical influence of eugenic approaches on psychological testing. Demir said, “Although efforts are now being made to develop these tests into more dynamic tools that focus on the process, the underlying risk of categorisation and labelling remains.”


‘How is children’s intelligence measured?’


Demir said Kurdish therapists faced serious difficulties in clinical practice and that children’s intelligence and developmental levels were assessed using imposed measurement tools that disregarded their mother tongue. She said strict standardisation was required in training on how to administer the tests: “Practitioners are expected not to change even a single sentence in the test instructions. Yet there is a major discrepancy between this standardisation in theory and the reality of clinical practice. A child who has developed their everyday and play language in their mother tongue from the earliest stages of life is assessed using tests designed in a different language, leading to labelling and exclusion.”


‘The tests do not match our language’


Psychologist Ismail Güven then spoke about the problems faced by psychologists working in hospitals. He said hospital psychologists generally worked with several groups of patients: “The first group consists of people who apply directly to hospitals to obtain a medical report. These include people seeking reports for a driving licence, a firearms' licence, work in the police or as a school bus driver, as well as those who need psychological testing for retirement or disability assessments. We administer tests to these people and assess their condition. The second group consists of patients referred by psychiatrists or neurologists for a diagnosis or clarification of their condition. The third is the treatment and therapy group. These are patients who have undergone a medical examination and come to receive psychotherapy as part of their treatment. One of the greatest problems and injustices we encounter in this process is that our people are unable to fully benefit from these healthcare services. Materials appropriate to our language and culture are not available. Developing, standardising and adapting a test involves many stages. Tests developed in Turkey or translated from English into Turkish, for example, do not correspond to our language or culture.”


‘Language creates national unity’


Psychologist Azad Dildar described language as a living and social entity that carries people’s emotions and thoughts, and said there was a profound relationship between language, human beings and life. He said this was where the importance of language to mental health began: “Language creates national unity among a people and provides access to their history, culture and folklore. We cannot say that language is merely a means of communication. A child begins to form a relationship with language while still in the womb. Even if the child does not understand the language, they recognise its sound. Research has been conducted on this. Mothers recognise their children by their cries, and children recognise their mothers by their voices. But my favourite expression on this subject comes from the Finnish writer and language advocate Antti Jalava: ‘My mother tongue is my skin, while other languages are my clothes. I can change my clothes whenever I want and put on new ones, but I cannot tear off my skin.’ This clearly demonstrates the importance of the mother tongue, that first and primary language. Heidegger also said, ‘Language is the house of Being.’ We can therefore say that killing a language means killing a world.”


‘The mother tongue has a direct counterpart in the brain’

title: I’m so tired of performative violence fantasies against abusers derailing conversations that are…
content:
I’m so tired of performative violence fantasies against abusers derailing conversations that are actually materially helping victims. Someone made a great post saying when educating kids about CSA Prevention to never say “I’ll hurt anyone who does this to you” or anything like that because usually it’s someone the kid knows and cares about and they won’t disclose if they think that person will be hurt. Or (which they didn’t mention but I’m adding) in certain types of abuse children are made to believe they are perpetrators when they aren’t and will feel you’ll hurt them and not love them if they disclose. And the comments were just a bunch of stupid, cringey shit about “Well, the kid doesn’t need to know”. Yes, more secrets and gaslighting, that’s what victims need. Shut up. It’s so stupid and not helping the discussion. The kid would find out most likely and would be retraumatized by that. You need to care about victims more than you hate abusers.
